title: Booking & Cancellation Policy
body:
1. Cancellation Windows
Members may cancel any court reservation free of charge up to six hours before the scheduled start time. Cancellations made within this window are processed automatically through the app or member portal, with no need to contact staff. Requests submitted later than six hours before play, but before the session begins, are subject to the late cancellation terms outlined elsewhere in this policy. We recommend cancelling as early as possible so that courts can be released back into general availability for other members and guests hoping to book last-minute sessions across our clubs.

2. Refunds to Wallet
Where a cancellation qualifies for a refund, funds are returned to the member's Baseline wallet rather than the original payment method, unless local regulations require otherwise. Wallet credit can be used against any future booking, coaching session, or retail purchase at participating clubs. Refunds are typically processed within a few hours of cancellation, though busier periods may extend this slightly. Members are notified by app notification and email once the credit has landed. Wallet balances do not expire under standard terms, though promotional credits may carry their own separate validity period as stated at the time of issue.

3. Peak-Time Rules
Bookings made during peak hours, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends, carry stricter cancellation terms due to high demand. Members cancelling a peak-time slot within twelve hours of the start time will not receive a refund or wallet credit, regardless of reason, except where covered under weather or force majeure clauses. Peak windows are clearly marked within the booking app before confirmation, so members can plan accordingly. We encourage forward planning for popular slots, as courts released close to play are rarely rebooked in time, resulting in lost availability for the wider membership community.

4. Partial Cancellations
For bookings involving multiple courts or extended time blocks, members may cancel a portion of the reservation without forfeiting the entire booking. Partial cancellations are subject to the same time-based windows as full cancellations, calculated individually for each court or hour affected. Any refund or wallet credit due will reflect only the cancelled portion, while the remaining booking stays confirmed and payable as normal. Members wishing to adjust a booking in this way should do so through the app rather than by contacting the club directly, ensuring the change is recorded accurately and immediately.

5. Transfers to Another Player
Members unable to attend a confirmed session may transfer their booking to another registered player rather than cancelling outright. Transfers can be arranged directly through the app by entering the new player's membership details, and must be completed before the original session start time. There is no fee for transferring a booking, and doing so avoids any late cancellation charge. The incoming player assumes all responsibilities tied to the reservation, including adherence to court etiquette and timing. Transfers are not permitted once a session has begun or after a no-show has already been recorded.

6. No-Shows
A booking is classed as a no-show when no player from the reserved group arrives within fifteen minutes of the scheduled start time. No-shows are charged in full, with no refund or wallet credit issued under any circumstance other than a documented emergency reviewed by club management. Repeated no-shows may result in a temporary restriction on future advance bookings. We understand that plans change unexpectedly, which is why the app allows cancellations and transfers right up until the final moments before a session, offering a simple alternative to forfeiting the reservation entirely.

7. Late Arrival
Court time is reserved for the full session regardless of when players actually arrive, meaning late arrival does not extend the booking beyond its original end time. Members arriving more than fifteen minutes late without prior notice may find their slot released to another member, in line with the no-show terms above. If delay is unavoidable, notifying the club in advance through the app helps hold the court where possible. Coaches and staff will always try to accommodate reasonable delays, though this cannot be guaranteed during busy periods when subsequent bookings follow immediately after.

8. Coach-Led Session Cancellations
Private and semi-private coaching sessions follow a separate cancellation window of twenty-four hours, reflecting the coach's own scheduling commitments. Cancellations made within this window receive full wallet credit, while later cancellations are charged at the full session rate and paid directly to the coach. Where a coach cancels a session, whether due to illness or unavailability, members receive full credit automatically and are offered priority rebooking at the next available slot. Group coaching clinics follow the standard group booking terms described separately, as attendance numbers affect how sessions are run and refunded.

9. Group Bookings
Bookings made on behalf of a group, such as a social ladder night or corporate event, are managed by a single lead booker responsible for coordinating cancellations on the group's behalf. Cancellation terms mirror standard court booking windows, though refunds are issued as a single wallet credit to the lead booker's account rather than divided among participants. Groups of eight or more should give at least twenty-four hours' notice of cancellation to avoid charges, given the court allocation required. Club staff are happy to assist with organising larger bookings and explaining the relevant terms in advance.

10. Package Sessions
Members who have purchased a multi-session package, such as a block of coaching hours or court credits, may cancel individual sessions within the package under the same windows as standard bookings. A cancelled session is simply returned to the package balance for future use rather than refunded separately. Package sessions typically carry their own expiry period, detailed at the time of purchase, and this expiry is not extended by cancellations made along the way. Members should check their remaining balance and expiry date regularly within the app to make full use of their package before it lapses.

11. Weather Cancellations
Outdoor court bookings cancelled due to rain are credited in full to the member account within 48 hours. Credits expire 90 days from issue. Indoor bookings are not eligible for weather credit. Members do not need to submit a claim themselves, as weather-related cancellations are logged automatically by club staff once a court is deemed unplayable. In cases where a member believes a weather credit has been missed, they can raise the matter with the front desk or through the app's support chat, quoting the booking reference for a prompt review.

12. Force Majeure
Beyond weather, bookings may occasionally be affected by circumstances outside the club's reasonable control, including power outages, essential maintenance, public safety advisories, or venue closures directed by relevant authorities. In such cases, affected members receive full wallet credit or, where preferred, a refund to the original payment method upon request. The club will make reasonable efforts to notify members as early as possible through the app, email, or SMS. Baseline Padel is not liable for any indirect losses arising from such disruptions, including travel costs or missed coaching arrangements made around the affected session.

13. Disputes
Any member who believes a cancellation, charge, or credit has been applied incorrectly may raise a dispute through the app's support section or by speaking with club management directly. Disputes should be raised within fourteen days of the booking in question to allow accurate review of session records and payment history. Club management will investigate and respond within a reasonable timeframe, typically within a few working days. Where an error is confirmed, the correct credit or refund will be applied promptly. Baseline Padel aims to resolve all booking disputes fairly, consistently, and in good faith across all clubs.

14. Contact Us
For any questions regarding bookings, cancellations, or this policy more generally, members are welcome to reach out through the in-app support chat, by email, or in person at the front desk of any Baseline Padel club. Our team is available throughout regular opening hours to assist with rescheduling, disputes, package queries, or general booking guidance. Members are encouraged to keep contact details up to date within their profile to ensure timely notifications regarding weather cancellations, coach changes, or other schedule adjustments. We are always happy to help members get the most from their Baseline Padel membership.

title: Booking Windows and Advance Reservations
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how far in advance members and guests may reserve court time across all branches of Baseline Padel, and the conditions attached to those reservations. It applies uniformly to indoor and outdoor courts, coaching slots, and social play sessions booked through the app, the website, or over the phone via a branch reception desk. Where a specific branch or membership tier is subject to different arrangements, this is stated explicitly in the relevant clause below. All timings referenced throughout this document are measured from the moment a booking is confirmed, not from the moment a request is submitted, and members should treat confirmation messages as the definitive record of any reservation.

2. Standard Booking Window
Under standard terms, any member may reserve a court up to seven days ahead of play, calculated on a rolling basis rather than by fixed calendar release dates. This means that a court becomes bookable exactly one week before the intended session time, and slots do not all open simultaneously at a single point each week. Guests booking without an active membership are limited to a shorter window of 72 hours ahead of play, reflecting the priority given to members across all locations. Reception staff cannot override this window manually except in the escalation circumstances described in clause 13.

3. Membership Tiers and Extended Access
Members holding a Premier or Founder-level membership benefit from an extended booking window of fourteen days, allowing them to plan sessions further ahead than standard members. This extended access applies at every branch and is not restricted to a member's registered home branch, meaning a Premier member may reserve a court at any of the eight branches within the same fourteen-day horizon. Corporate membership holders follow the standard seven-day window unless their company account has been specifically upgraded through the membership office, in which case the extended terms apply to all named individuals under that account.

4. Peak and Off-Peak Definitions
Peak hours are defined locally by each branch according to typical demand patterns, but generally fall in the early morning before working hours begin and again in the evening once the working day ends. Off-peak hours cover the remaining daytime slots and late-night sessions where courts are less heavily contested. The booking window itself does not change between peak and off-peak periods, but the likelihood of availability at the moment a window opens is considerably higher for peak slots, and members wishing to secure these are advised to book as close to the opening of their window as practical.

5. Outdoor Branches and Weather-Dependent Adjustments
At outdoor branches, advance bookings remain subject to prevailing conditions during the warmer months, when extreme heat may render certain daytime slots unplayable. In such cases, a branch may suspend new bookings for affected midday and early-afternoon slots without this being treated as a breach of the standard booking window, since the suspension is a safety measure rather than a capacity decision. Members who already hold a confirmed booking in an affected slot will be contacted directly and offered a shifted time, a credit, or a transfer to a covered court where one is available at that branch. Outdoor branches typically extend their bookable hours into the cooler evening period to compensate for reduced midday availability.

6. Same-Day and Last-Minute Bookings
Same-day bookings remain permitted right up until the scheduled start time, provided a court has not already been reserved by another party and the branch's system shows it as open. Last-minute bookings made within two hours of the session start are treated identically to any other confirmed booking in terms of cancellation and no-show consequences, and members should not assume a shorter lead time carries more relaxed obligations. Branches reserve the right to hold back a small number of courts from same-day release during particularly high-demand periods, such as evenings during cooler months, to preserve availability for members exercising their standard window rights.

7. Group and Block Bookings
Groups wishing to reserve multiple courts for the same time slot, such as for a corporate outing or a private social event, must submit the request through the events coordinator at their chosen branch rather than through the standard app flow, and such requests are typically handled within 48 hours of submission. Block bookings spanning multiple consecutive weeks, for example a recurring weekly slot held by the same group of players, may be arranged directly with branch management and are not bound by the standard seven or fourteen day windows, since they are treated as a separate recurring arrangement rather than a single reservation. These recurring blocks are reviewed periodically and may be released back into general availability if attendance drops below an agreed threshold over a sustained period.

8. Cancellation and Rebooking Within the Window
A booking may be cancelled without penalty up to 12 hours before the scheduled start time, at which point the slot is released back into the system and becomes available to any other member within the applicable window. Cancellations made after this 12-hour threshold but before the session start are still processed but may be logged against the member's account for pattern purposes, particularly if repeated frequently. Rebooking the same slot after a cancellation is permitted, but the new reservation is treated as an entirely fresh booking for the purposes of all subsequent clauses, including no-show tracking.

9. No-Show Policy and Its Effect on Future Booking Windows
A member who fails to attend a confirmed booking without cancelling in advance is recorded as a no-show, and a pattern of repeated no-shows across any branch may result in a temporary reduction of that member's booking window, typically shortened to 48 hours ahead of play rather than the standard seven days. This reduced window is reviewed after a period of consistent attendance, generally 30 days, after which standard access is automatically restored. Members who believe a no-show has been recorded in error, for example due to a system fault or a documented emergency, may raise the matter with branch reception for review and possible removal from their record.

10. Coaching and Academy Session Reservations
Coaching sessions and academy programme slots follow a separate advance booking structure to general court play, generally opening 21 days ahead to accommodate structured programme planning and coach scheduling across branches. Cancellations of coaching sessions require at least 24 hours' notice to avoid forfeiting the session, given the resourcing commitments involved in coach availability. Where a coach becomes unavailable due to illness or unforeseen circumstances, the branch will attempt to offer a substitute coach at the same time slot before resorting to rescheduling, and members will always be notified as soon as reasonably possible once such a change is identified.

11. Tournament and Event Blackout Periods
Certain courts at certain branches are periodically withdrawn from general advance booking to accommodate internal tournaments, exhibition matches, or hosted community events. These blackout periods are published on the app and at branch reception at least seven days ahead of the affected dates wherever possible, and any existing bookings that fall within a newly declared blackout will be proactively rearranged by branch staff, with the affected member offered first choice of alternative slots at that branch or a nearby branch. Blackout periods do not affect the underlying booking window calculation for unaffected courts, which continue to operate under standard terms throughout.

12. Waitlist Procedures
Where a desired slot is fully booked, members may join a waitlist through the app, and should a cancellation occur within the applicable window, the system will notify waitlisted members in the order they joined, allowing a limited response period of 15 minutes to confirm the newly available slot before it passes to the next person in the queue. Waitlist entries do not guarantee eventual allocation and expire automatically once the relevant session time has passed. Members are limited to two active waitlist entries at any one time to prevent unnecessary hoarding of slots across multiple branches.

13. System Downtime and Manual Booking Escalation
In the event of a technical outage affecting the booking app or website, branches will revert to manual booking taken over the phone or at reception, applying the same window rules as the digital system to the fullest extent practical. Any booking made manually during an outage will be entered into the system once service is restored, and members will receive a confirmation message at that point rather than immediately. Where an outage causes a member to miss the normal opening of their booking window through no fault of their own, branch management is authorised to grant a short grace period, typically up to 24 hours, allowing that member to book as though the window had opened on schedule.

14. Amendments, Escalation, and Contact
Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend booking window lengths, peak definitions, or blackout procedures at any branch with reasonable notice communicated through the app and in-branch signage. Members who wish to query a specific booking decision, a no-show record, or a window restriction that they believe has been applied incorrectly should first raise the matter with reception staff at the branch concerned, and if unresolved, may escalate the query to the central membership office, which typically responds within three working days. This escalation path applies uniformly across all eight branches regardless of membership tier.

title: No-Show and Late Arrival Policy
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs all court bookings made across Baseline Padel's eight branches, whether reserved through the mobile application, the website portal, over the phone, or in person at reception. It applies equally to members, punch-card holders, corporate account users, and pay-as-you-go guests. The purpose is to ensure fair access to courts during peak demand windows, to reduce revenue loss caused by unused reservations, and to give staff a consistent framework for handling lateness, absence, and disputed charges. Where a specific branch operates under a modified version of this policy due to local circumstances, that variation will be displayed at reception and within the booking confirmation email, and the branch-specific terms take precedence over the general terms described here.

2. Definition of a No-Show
A booking is classified as a no-show when no member of the booking party has checked in at reception, or activated a self-service digital check-in where available, within fifteen minutes of the scheduled start time. It does not matter whether the court itself is occupied by another informal group during that window; the classification is based solely on whether the original booking party registered their arrival through an approved channel. Partial arrival, such as one player from a group of four checking in, is not treated as a no-show and is instead handled under the late-arrival provisions in clause 4.

3. Grace Period
All branches observe a standard grace period of fifteen minutes from the scheduled start time before a booking is deemed forfeited. During this window the court is held exclusively for the booking party and cannot be reassigned, even if other members are waiting on-site. Staff are not obliged to extend this period under normal circumstances, and requests to do so on the basis of general traffic or personal delay will not be honoured. The grace period exists to absorb minor, everyday delays and should not be relied upon as a routine extension of playing time; sessions still end at the originally booked finish time regardless of a late start.

4. Late Arrival Within the Grace Period
When a player or group arrives after the start time but within the fifteen-minute grace period, the session proceeds but is not extended to compensate for lost minutes. For example, a booking made for a sixty-minute slot beginning at a stated time will still conclude sixty minutes after that original start time, not sixty minutes after the player's actual arrival. This rule is applied consistently to avoid disputes over adjacent bookings and to protect the schedule of players waiting for the same court afterwards. Front-of-house staff have no discretion to extend the finish time on a busy day, though see clause 9 for exceptional circumstances that may warrant a goodwill adjustment.

5. Late Arrival Beyond the Grace Period
If no member of the booking party has checked in after fifteen minutes have elapsed, the booking is automatically released back into the available inventory and may be allocated to another player, a walk-in guest, or an internal coaching session, entirely at the discretion of branch staff. Should the original party arrive shortly after this point and the court remains unclaimed, staff may, at their discretion, permit the group to use the remaining time of the original slot without additional charge, but this is offered as a courtesy rather than a guaranteed entitlement, and is more commonly extended at quieter outdoor branches than at high-demand indoor locations.

6. Charges Applied to No-Shows
A confirmed booking that results in a no-show is charged in full, as though the session had been played, regardless of payment method. For members using an allocated monthly or seasonal credit allowance, a no-show consumes one credit from that allowance in the same way a completed session would. For pay-as-you-go bookings paid by card at the time of reservation, no refund is issued. For bookings secured against a corporate or academy account, the no-show is logged against that account and may be reflected in a periodic invoice sent to the account holder rather than charged individually at the time.

7. Repeated No-Shows and Account Flags
Accounts that accumulate three or more no-shows within any rolling ninety-day period are automatically flagged within the booking system. A flagged account may be required to pay for future bookings in advance at the time of reservation, rather than being permitted to hold a court on a pay-later or membership-credit basis. This measure is not intended as a punitive step but as a practical safeguard against courts being held speculatively and then abandoned, which reduces availability for other players attempting to book the same peak slots. The flag is reviewed automatically after a further ninety-day period of consistent attendance and is lifted without the need for the customer to contact support.

8. Cancellations Versus No-Shows
A booking cancelled in advance through the app, website, or by contacting reception is treated entirely differently from a no-show and is governed by the separate Cancellation and Refund Policy. As a general principle, cancellations made outside the minimum notice window specified in that policy are eligible for a credit or refund, whereas a booking simply abandoned without notice is always treated as a no-show and charged accordingly. Customers who realise they cannot attend are strongly encouraged to cancel through the app as early as possible, even shortly before the session, since a late cancellation is still processed more favourably than an unreported absence in almost all cases.

9. Exceptional Circumstances and Discretion
Branch duty managers retain discretion to waive a no-show charge or to extend a grace period in genuinely exceptional circumstances, such as a documented medical emergency, a significant and verifiable public transport disruption, or a facility-side issue such as unexpected court closure or a lighting fault at outdoor branches. Requests for such waivers should be submitted through the app's support section or directly to the branch within seventy-two hours of the missed booking, accompanied by any relevant supporting information. Decisions made under this clause are recorded on the customer's account and are considered on a case-by-case basis; a waiver granted once does not establish a precedent for future requests, and repeated reliance on this clause may itself contribute to an account review under clause 7.

10. Group Bookings and Split Responsibility
Where a court is booked by one individual on behalf of a group, that individual is treated as the responsible party for check-in and charge purposes, regardless of who ultimately attends. If at least one member of the group checks in within the grace period, the booking is not treated as a no-show even if other members fail to arrive. Organisers are encouraged to communicate arrival plans clearly to their group, since responsibility for any no-show charge rests with the account under which the booking was made, not with individual players who may have been delayed independently.

11. Coaching Sessions and Academy Bookings
Private coaching sessions and academy group classes are subject to a shorter grace period of ten minutes, reflecting the structured nature of instructional time and the coach's own scheduling commitments across the day. A student arriving after this point may be permitted to join a group class already in progress at the coach's discretion, but private one-to-one sessions that are missed entirely within this window are treated as delivered and charged in full, since the coach's time has already been reserved and cannot typically be reallocated at short notice.

12. Weather-Related Adjustments at Outdoor Branches
At outdoor branches, where sessions may be affected by rain, extreme heat advisories, or sudden wind conditions, a no-show charge will not be applied if the branch itself proactively cancels or suspends play prior to the scheduled start time. However, if conditions deteriorate only after a session has begun, the original booking is still considered fulfilled and standard charges apply. Customers concerned about forecast conditions ahead of an outdoor booking are advised to check the app's live court-status indicator, which is updated by branch staff whenever conditions are being monitored or a session is at risk of suspension.

13. Disputing a No-Show Charge
Any customer who believes a no-show charge has been applied in error, for instance due to a check-in system malfunction or a staff logging mistake, may raise a dispute through the app's support section within seven days of the charge appearing on their account. Disputes should include the approximate arrival time and, where possible, the name of the staff member who was on duty at reception. Support will review access logs and any available check-in records before issuing a decision, typically within a few working days, and where the dispute is upheld the charge or credit deduction will be reversed in full.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
Baseline Padel reserves the right to review and amend this policy periodically to reflect operational needs across all branches, including changes to grace periods, flagging thresholds, or discretionary provisions. Where a change materially affects how charges are applied, updated terms will be published within the app and displayed at reception in advance of taking effect. Continued use of the booking system following such notice constitutes acceptance of the revised policy, and customers with specific concerns about an upcoming change are encouraged to contact their home branch directly.

title: Group and Block Booking Rules
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs all group and block bookings made across Baseline Padel's eight branches, covering recurring corporate sessions, academy programmes, tournament blocks, social leagues, and one-off group hires of three courts or more. It applies equally to indoor and outdoor branches, though certain seasonal provisions apply only to outdoor courts where weather exposure affects scheduling. Any booking that falls outside these parameters, such as a single-court reservation for a small group, should instead be handled under our standard court booking terms rather than this policy. Where a discrepancy arises between this document and any verbal arrangement made with branch staff, the written confirmation issued through our booking system takes precedence.

2. Definitions of Group and Block Bookings
A group booking is defined as any single reservation covering two or more courts at the same branch during the same time slot, booked under one primary contact. A block booking refers to a recurring reservation held across multiple weeks or months, typically for corporate wellness programmes, junior academies, or private leagues, where the same court or courts are held on a repeating basis. Block bookings are treated as a standing arrangement rather than a one-time transaction, and are subject to the renewal and cancellation terms outlined in clauses 7 and 9 below. Mixed arrangements, where a group books occasional single sessions alongside a recurring block, will be assessed individually by the branch manager and may be split across both booking categories for billing purposes.

3. Eligibility and Minimum Requirements
Group bookings require a minimum of three courts booked simultaneously, or a minimum of twelve participants, whichever threshold is reached first. Block bookings require a minimum commitment of four consecutive weeks at a fixed day and time. Requests falling below these thresholds may still be accommodated at the discretion of the branch, but will not qualify for the discounted rates or priority scheduling described in clauses 5 and 6. Corporate clients requesting bookings on behalf of a company or organisation must provide a named primary contact who holds authority to confirm attendance numbers, amend schedules, and settle invoices; this contact will be the sole point of communication for all matters relating to the booking.

4. Advance Notice and Confirmation Process
All group and block booking requests must be submitted no less than seven days before the intended start date, and ideally further in advance for outdoor branches during periods of high seasonal demand. Requests are provisional until written confirmation is issued by the branch or central booking team, and provisional holds will not be extended beyond 72 hours without a deposit being received. Once confirmed, the primary contact will receive a summary of court allocations, time slots, and any applicable coaching or equipment arrangements. It is the responsibility of the primary contact to circulate this confirmation to all participants, as Baseline Padel does not communicate directly with individual members of a group unless specifically requested.

5. Deposits and Payment Terms
A non-refundable deposit equivalent to 25 percent of the total booking value is required to secure any group booking, with the balance due no later than 48 hours before the first session. For block bookings, payment is typically structured on a monthly or termly basis, with an initial deposit covering the first two weeks of sessions. Failure to settle an outstanding balance within the specified window may result in the booking being released without further notice, and any deposit already paid will be forfeited. Corporate accounts with an approved credit arrangement may be invoiced in arrears, subject to separate terms agreed with our finance team, but this arrangement must be confirmed in writing before the first session takes place.

6. Court Allocation and Branch Preferences
While Baseline Padel will make reasonable efforts to accommodate a preferred branch and court type, allocation is ultimately subject to availability at the time of confirmation. Groups requesting adjacent or paired courts for social play should note this in their initial request, as such arrangements cannot always be guaranteed once other bookings have been placed. Outdoor branches reserve the right to reassign group bookings to covered or indoor courts at short notice in the event of adverse weather, and no refund will be issued where a suitable alternative court has been offered and accepted. Where no alternative can be provided due to full occupancy, the affected session will be rescheduled at no additional cost, or credited to the group's account for future use.

7. Recurring Block Booking Renewals
Block bookings are not automatically renewed at the end of their agreed term. The primary contact will be notified approximately fourteen days before the final scheduled session and invited to confirm a renewal, adjust the day or time, or conclude the arrangement. Renewal requests are treated as new bookings and are subject to current availability and pricing at the time of renewal, which may differ from the original terms if court demand or seasonal rates have changed. Where a branch is unable to continue offering the same recurring slot due to prior commitments from other groups, reasonable alternative slots will be offered, but continuity of the exact time and court cannot be guaranteed indefinitely.

8. Amendments to Confirmed Bookings
Requests to amend a confirmed group or block booking, including changes to court numbers, participant counts, or scheduling, must be submitted in writing to the branch or central booking team as early as possible. Minor amendments, such as reducing the number of courts by one within an existing time slot, are generally accommodated without penalty provided at least 48 hours' notice is given. Amendments requested with less notice, or that significantly alter the scope of the original booking, may incur an administrative adjustment fee and are subject to court availability at the time of the request. Any amendment that increases the total value of the booking will require an updated deposit calculation before the change is confirmed.

9. Cancellations and No-Shows
Cancellations made more than 72 hours before a group session will receive a full refund of any balance paid beyond the initial deposit, which remains non-refundable in all circumstances. Cancellations made within 72 hours will forfeit the full session fee. For block bookings, cancellation of an individual session within the recurring series does not entitle the group to a refund or credit, though branches may offer a one-time rescheduling courtesy at their discretion where advance notice of at least 24 hours is given. Persistent no-shows without notice across a recurring block booking may result in the arrangement being suspended or terminated, at which point any remaining scheduled sessions will be cancelled and no further deposits will be required.

10. Coaching, Equipment, and Additional Services
Group and block bookings that include coaching support, equipment hire, or refreshment packages must specify these requirements at the time of the initial request, as coaching staff availability is arranged separately from court scheduling and cannot always be added at short notice. Where a coach has been confirmed for a session and the group subsequently reduces numbers below the agreed minimum, the coaching fee will still apply in full. Equipment such as rackets or balls provided for group sessions remains the property of Baseline Padel and any loss or damage beyond normal wear will be charged to the primary contact's account. Additional services requested on the day of a session, such as extending court time, are subject to availability and will be billed separately at standard rates.

11. Conduct and Responsibility Within Groups
The primary contact for a group or block booking is responsible for the conduct of all participants during the reserved sessions, including adherence to court etiquette, footwear requirements, and general branch conduct standards. Any damage caused to courts, fixtures, or shared facilities by members of the group will be charged to the primary contact, regardless of which individual was responsible. Repeated disruptive behaviour, whether reported by branch staff or other members using adjacent courts, may result in the booking being suspended without refund and, in serious cases, the group being barred from future bookings across all branches. Branch managers retain full discretion to end a session early where conduct poses a safety concern.

12. Escalation and Dispute Resolution
Any dispute regarding charges, court allocation, or service delivery relating to a group or block booking should first be raised with the branch manager at the location where the booking took place, ideally within seven days of the session in question. If the matter remains unresolved, the primary contact may escalate the issue in writing to the central customer relations team, who will review the booking record and respond within a reasonable working period. Baseline Padel reserves the right to offer resolution in the form of credit, partial refund, or rescheduling as it deems appropriate to the circumstances, and such decisions made at central level are considered final within our internal review process.

13. Force Majeure and Branch Closures
Where a branch is required to close temporarily due to circumstances beyond reasonable control, including but not limited to extreme weather, essential maintenance, or utility disruption, any affected group or block sessions will be rescheduled at no cost or credited to the group's account. Baseline Padel will make reasonable efforts to notify the primary contact as early as possible in such circumstances, though notice periods may be shorter than usual where the closure arises suddenly. No cash refunds will be issued for sessions affected by closures falling under this clause, as credit or rescheduling is considered the appropriate remedy in all such cases.

14. Amendments to This Policy
Baseline Padel reserves the right to update these group and block booking rules from time to time to reflect changes in operational capacity, seasonal demand, or service offerings across branches. Where a change materially affects an existing confirmed block booking, the primary contact will be notified in advance of the change taking effect. Continued use of group or block booking services following such notification constitutes acceptance of the updated terms. The most current version of this policy is available on request from any branch or through the central booking team, and supersedes any previous version in the event of conflict.

title: Court Transfers and Rescheduling
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs all requests to transfer, reschedule, or otherwise amend confirmed court bookings across all eight branches of Baseline Padel, whether the original reservation was made through the mobile application, the website portal, the member services desk, or by telephone. It applies equally to pay-and-play bookings, membership court allocations, academy block bookings, and corporate or event reservations, save where a more specific clause elsewhere in this document states otherwise. Any booking not explicitly addressed here should be treated under the general rescheduling principles set out in clauses two through six, with escalation handled per clause thirteen.

2. Standard Rescheduling Window
Members and guests may reschedule a confirmed court booking free of charge provided the request is submitted no later than four hours before the original start time. Requests made within this window will be processed automatically through the app or by the front desk, and the member will be offered the next three available slots at the same branch, matched as closely as possible to the original court type and duration. Where the exact court type is unavailable, staff will offer the nearest equivalent, such as a similarly surfaced court in an adjoining bay, and will note the substitution on the booking record for transparency.

3. Late Rescheduling Requests
Requests submitted after the four-hour cut-off but before the scheduled start time are treated as late reschedules and incur a handling fee, which is disclosed at the point of request and deducted from any credit balance or charged to the payment method on file. Late reschedules are subject to court availability and are not guaranteed; where no suitable slot exists at the same branch within a reasonable timeframe, the member may instead request a transfer to another branch under clause seven, or convert the booking into a credit under clause nine. Repeated late rescheduling by the same member, defined as more than three occurrences within a rolling thirty-day period, may result in the standard rescheduling window being tightened for that individual, at the discretion of branch management.

4. No-Show Distinguished from Rescheduling
A booking left unattended without any rescheduling request, transfer request, or cancellation notice is classified as a no-show and is not eligible for retroactive rescheduling. Members occasionally contact the club after the fact to request that a missed session be treated as a late reschedule; such requests will only be considered where there is clear evidence of extenuating circumstances, such as a documented medical emergency or a transport disruption affecting a wide area, and even then approval rests solely with branch management, not front-desk staff. Where approved, the outcome is typically a courtesy credit rather than a like-for-like rescheduled slot, and this remains an exception rather than an entitlement.

5. Weather-Affected Outdoor Bookings
Outdoor branches are subject to seasonal conditions, and bookings disrupted by heat advisories, sandstorms, sustained high winds, or unexpected maintenance closures are rescheduled automatically at no cost to the member. In these cases, the club will proactively contact affected members through the app and by message, offering either an immediate transfer to an indoor court at the same branch where capacity allows, or a rescheduled outdoor slot within the following seven days. Members who do not respond to this outreach within twenty-four hours will have their booking converted to a flexible credit, valid for ninety days from issue, to avoid the slot remaining blocked indefinitely.

6. Rescheduling Membership-Allocated Courts
Members whose plans include a fixed weekly or recurring court allocation may reschedule an individual instance of that recurring booking without affecting the standing reservation itself, provided the request follows the standard four-hour window described in clause two. Recurring allocations cannot be permanently moved to a new day or time through the rescheduling function; any permanent change to a recurring booking pattern must be handled as a membership amendment through account services, which operates under separate terms. Members attempting to use single-instance rescheduling repeatedly to effect what is functionally a permanent change will be redirected to account services for a formal amendment.

7. Transfers Between Branches
Court transfers between branches are permitted where availability exists, subject to any differential in court fees between the originating and receiving branch, which will be charged or refunded as applicable. Transfers are most commonly requested by members travelling between branches for work or personal reasons, and the club accommodates this readily provided at least two hours' notice is given before the original start time. Transfers requested with less notice will be treated as late reschedules under clause three and may incur the associated handling fee in addition to any fee differential. Branch transfers are not available for academy block bookings, which are tied to a specific coach and location as described in clause eleven.

8. Group and Multi-Court Bookings
Bookings spanning multiple courts, such as those made for social events, corporate sessions, or tournament warm-ups, require the consent of the original booking holder before any individual court within the group can be rescheduled or transferred. Where the group booking was made through a corporate account, only the nominated account administrator may authorise changes, and requests from individual participants will be declined until administrator approval is confirmed in writing. Partial rescheduling of a multi-court booking, where some courts move and others remain, is permitted but must be requested at least twenty-four hours in advance to allow staff time to reorganise the surrounding schedule without disrupting other members.

9. Conversion to Credit
Where rescheduling is not possible due to lack of availability, or where a member simply prefers not to rebook immediately, the value of the original booking may be converted into an account credit rather than refunded to the original payment method. Credits issued under this policy are valid for ninety days from the date of issue and may be applied toward any court booking, academy session, or eligible retail purchase at any branch. Credits are non-transferable between member accounts and cannot be exchanged for cash under any circumstance; unused credits that lapse beyond the ninety-day window are forfeited, though members may contact the front desk shortly before expiry to request a one-time thirty-day extension, granted at staff discretion.

10. Peak Hours and High-Demand Periods
During peak evening hours and other high-demand periods identified by each branch, rescheduling requests are still accepted within the standard window but may be subject to a shorter list of alternative slots, as courts during these periods are typically fully booked well in advance. Members rescheduling out of a peak slot should be aware that securing an equivalent peak slot on short notice is unlikely, and staff will always disclose realistic alternatives before confirming any change. Branches reserve the right to temporarily suspend free late rescheduling during exceptionally high-demand periods, such as around major internal tournaments, with advance notice posted in the app and at reception no less than seven days beforehand.

11. Academy and Coaching Session Rescheduling
Academy block bookings, private coaching sessions, and clinic enrolments follow a distinct rescheduling path tied to coach availability rather than general court availability. Rescheduling a coaching session requires at least twenty-four hours' notice and is subject to the individual coach's calendar; where a coach is fully booked for the requested alternative period, the session will be added to a waitlist and members will be notified as soon as an opening arises. Academy sessions rescheduled with less than twenty-four hours' notice are recorded as forfeited under the academy's own attendance terms, and no credit is issued, since coaching time cannot generally be resold on short notice the way a general court booking can.

12. Third-Party and Guest Bookings
Where a booking was made on behalf of a guest by a member, only the member of record may request a reschedule, transfer, or credit conversion; guests contacting the club directly will be redirected to the sponsoring member for authorisation. This safeguard exists to prevent disputes over payment responsibility and credit ownership, particularly where the guest is not registered on the club's system. Exceptions are made where the guest booking was paid for independently through a guest checkout flow, in which case the guest may manage the booking directly using the reference number issued at the time of payment.

13. Escalation Path
Members who believe a rescheduling or transfer request has been handled incorrectly, or who wish to dispute a fee applied under this policy, should first raise the matter with the duty manager at the branch where the booking originated. If unresolved within seventy-two hours, the matter may be escalated to the regional operations team through the member services channel in the app, quoting the original booking reference and a summary of prior correspondence. Escalations involving credit disputes, repeated system errors, or safety-related closures are prioritised and typically receive a substantive response within five working days, though complex cases involving multiple branches may take longer to fully investigate.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in operational capacity, seasonal patterns across outdoor and indoor branches, and feedback gathered through member services. Any material changes will be communicated in advance through the app and posted at each branch's reception area, and will not be applied retroactively to bookings made before the change took effect. Where a specific branch requires a temporary variation to this policy, such as during refurbishment or an extended maintenance period, that variation will be clearly signposted at the branch in question and will not alter the standard terms applicable elsewhere.

title: Membership Tiers and Benefits
body:
1. Overview of Membership Tiers
Baseline Padel operates four core membership tiers across all branches: Court, Advantage, Elite and Founders. Each tier is designed around a distinct pattern of play, from occasional weekend bookings through to daily access with premium scheduling rights. Tiers are not merely pricing bands; they determine booking windows, guest allowances, coaching discounts and access to branches outside a member's home location. Every member is assigned a home branch at sign-up, which forms the reference point for tier benefits, though the practical effect of tier differences becomes most visible during peak evening and weekend slots when court demand outstrips supply.

2. Tier Eligibility and Minimum Commitments
Court tier membership carries no minimum commitment and may be joined or left at the end of any billing cycle with the standard notice period described later in this document. Advantage and Elite tiers require a minimum initial commitment of three billing cycles, reflecting the additional infrastructure, coaching hours and priority slots reserved for these members. Founders tier is only available at branches where it was offered at launch and is now closed to new applicants; existing Founders members retain their benefits for as long as their account remains active and in good standing, but the tier cannot be reassigned, transferred, or reopened once cancelled.

3. Court Booking Windows and Priority Access
Booking windows are tier-dependent and apply uniformly across branches unless a specific outdoor branch notice states otherwise due to weather-related court closures. Court tier members may book seven days in advance, Advantage members ten days, and Elite and Founders members fourteen days, with Elite and Founders additionally receiving a two-hour priority window each morning before general release. Where a member holds multiple household memberships under a family plan, only the primary account holder's tier determines the booking window for shared bookings, though each household member retains independent access for solo play within their own tier allowance.

4. Guest Passes and Visitor Policy
Each paying membership includes a monthly allocation of guest passes, ranging from two for Court tier to unlimited, subject to court availability, for Elite and Founders tiers. Guests must be registered at reception or through the app at least two hours before play and are subject to the same code of conduct as members. Guest passes do not roll over between billing cycles and cannot be exchanged for cash, coaching credit or merchandise discounts. Repeated use of guest passes to bring the same individual more than four times within a single billing cycle may prompt a courtesy call from the branch manager to discuss a separate membership for that individual, as passes are not intended to substitute for full membership.

5. Family and Household Memberships
Family memberships link up to five individuals residing at the same address under a single billing account, with one adult designated as the primary holder responsible for payment and booking administration. Children under the age of twelve included on a family plan receive access to junior coaching programmes at a reduced rate but are not permitted to book adult competitive sessions independently. Should a household member wish to upgrade their individual tier while remaining on the family plan, this is possible only where the requested tier is available as an add-on at that member's home branch, and the price difference is charged pro-rata for the remainder of the current billing cycle.

6. Corporate and Group Memberships
Corporate memberships are arranged directly with a branch manager and require a minimum of eight named individuals from the same organisation. These memberships function similarly to Advantage tier for booking purposes but include quarterly usage reporting for the corporate account holder and consolidated invoicing. Named individuals may be substituted no more than twice within any twelve-month period without incurring an administration charge; further substitutions are subject to a fee to cover onboarding and access card reissue. Corporate memberships do not include guest passes by default, though these may be purchased as an add-on package at the time of agreement.

7. Membership Freezes and Suspensions
Members may freeze their account for medical reasons, extended travel, or relocation, subject to supporting documentation being provided within fourteen days of the freeze request. A freeze suspends billing and access simultaneously and may be applied for a minimum of thirty days and a maximum of one hundred and eighty days within any rolling twelve-month period. Freezes requested without documentation for reasons of general convenience are limited to one occurrence per membership year and capped at thirty days. Reactivation occurs automatically at the end of the stated freeze period unless the member requests an extension in writing before that date, subject to the overall cap.

8. Upgrades, Downgrades and Mid-Cycle Changes
Upgrades between tiers take effect immediately upon request and are billed on a pro-rata basis for the remainder of the current cycle, with full-tier billing commencing at the next renewal. Downgrades take effect only at the start of the following billing cycle to avoid mid-cycle disruption to booking rights already exercised. A member who downgrades before completing the minimum commitment period attached to Advantage, Elite or Founders tiers will be liable for the difference between the discounted rate paid and the standard rate for the months already completed, calculated at the point the downgrade is processed. Members disputing this calculation may request a written breakdown from their home branch's membership desk.

9. Renewals and Auto-Renewal Terms
All memberships renew automatically at the end of each billing cycle unless cancelled in accordance with clause ten. Members will receive a renewal notice at least seven days before the charge is applied, detailing any change in fees that may have occurred since the previous cycle. Where a member's stored payment method fails at the point of renewal, a grace period of five days is granted during which court access continues; access is suspended automatically thereafter until payment is successfully processed or updated details are provided.

10. Cancellations and Refunds
Cancellation requests must be submitted through the app or in writing to the home branch at least fourteen days before the next renewal date to avoid being charged for the following cycle. Fees already paid for a current cycle are non-refundable except where a branch closure of longer than seven consecutive days prevents the member from accessing any facility within a reasonable travelling distance, in which case a pro-rata credit is applied to the account. Members who cancel during a minimum-commitment period remain liable for outstanding instalments as described in clause eight, and any attempt to rejoin the same tier within ninety days of cancellation will result in the outstanding balance being settled before a new membership is activated.

11. Cross-Branch Access and Outdoor Branch Considerations
All tiers above Court level include access to every branch in the group, though booking priority always defaults to the member's home branch during peak hours. At outdoor branches, seasonal weather closures during the warmer months may reduce available court hours; members based at an outdoor branch retain full access to any indoor branch during such closures without additional charge, and this access is not treated as cross-branch usage for the purposes of any fair-use monitoring applied to Court tier members visiting branches other than their own.

12. Coaching and Programme Discounts
Membership tier determines the discount applied to group clinics, private coaching and holiday camps, with Court tier receiving a modest reduction on published rates and Elite and Founders tiers receiving the deepest discounts alongside priority booking for limited-capacity programmes such as high-performance squads. These discounts apply only to sessions booked directly through the member's own account and cannot be transferred to a guest or family member unless that individual holds their own qualifying membership. Any promotional coaching rate advertised separately from this policy takes precedence for the duration of that promotion only.

13. Missed Payments and Account Lapses
Where two consecutive payment attempts fail, the membership is automatically downgraded to a lapsed status, access is revoked, and any existing bookings are cancelled without individual notice beyond the automated system alert. Reactivating a lapsed account within sixty days requires settlement of the outstanding balance plus a reactivation charge; after sixty days the account is closed permanently and rejoining is treated as a new membership application, with no continuity of tenure-based benefits such as Founders status or long-service coaching discounts.

14. Escalation and Dispute Resolution
Members who believe a tier benefit, booking priority, or billing charge has been applied incorrectly should first raise the matter with their home branch's membership desk, which is required to respond within three working days. Unresolved matters may be escalated to the regional membership office, which will issue a written decision within fourteen days of receiving all relevant documentation. Where a member remains dissatisfied following this review, the matter may be referred to Baseline Padel's central membership committee, whose decision is final and binding on both the member and the branch in question.

title: Membership Freeze and Transfer
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs the freezing and transferring of membership entitlements across all branches of Baseline Padel, including both indoor and outdoor branches. It applies to all individual, couple, family, and corporate membership tiers unless a specific membership agreement states otherwise. The intent of this policy is to provide members with reasonable flexibility around travel, injury, relocation, or other lifestyle changes, while ensuring that court capacity and coaching resources remain fairly allocated across the membership base. Any provision not explicitly addressed here will be resolved at the discretion of the Membership Services team, with escalation available as described in clause 14.

2. Eligibility for a Freeze
Any member whose account is active and free of outstanding balances may apply for a freeze on their membership. Members must have completed a minimum of 60 days of active membership before their first freeze request is eligible for approval, except where the freeze is requested for medical reasons supported by documentation, in which case the minimum tenure requirement is waived. Corporate and family memberships may freeze the entire plan or nominate specific individuals within the plan to freeze, provided the request clearly identifies which members are affected and which will remain active.

3. Freeze Duration and Frequency
A standard freeze may be applied for a minimum of 14 days and a maximum of 90 days within any rolling 12-month period. Members wishing to freeze for longer than 90 days must submit a renewed request prior to expiry of the original freeze, and such extensions will be assessed individually rather than granted automatically. Members are permitted up to two separate freeze periods within a rolling 12-month period, and combined freeze time across both instances may not exceed the 90-day cap unless approved under the medical or relocation exceptions outlined in clause 6.

4. Application Process
Freeze requests must be submitted in writing through the member portal or in person at any branch reception at least 5 working days before the intended start date. Retroactive freeze requests, meaning those submitted after the freeze period has already begun, will only be considered where the member can demonstrate that circumstances prevented advance notice, such as sudden hospitalisation. Once submitted, requests are typically processed within 48 hours, and members will receive written confirmation before any billing adjustment takes effect. Membership dues are prorated from the confirmed start date of the freeze, not the date of application.

5. Billing During a Freeze
While a membership is frozen, standard monthly or annual dues are suspended and replaced with a nominal account maintenance charge, where applicable, to preserve the member's rate lock and court booking priority. This maintenance charge, where charged, is significantly lower than standard dues and is detailed in the current fee schedule available at reception or on the member portal. Members should note that any previously purchased add-ons, such as bulk coaching sessions or guest passes, do not expire during the freeze period but resume their normal validity countdown once the membership is reactivated.

6. Medical and Relocation Exceptions
Members who provide documentation of a medical condition preventing play, such as a note from a licensed practitioner, are eligible for extended freezes beyond the standard 90-day cap, subject to periodic review every 90 days for the duration of the medical circumstance. Members who are relocating away from the UAE for work or personal reasons may apply for an extended freeze of up to 180 days, provided evidence of relocation, such as an employment letter or lease termination notice, is submitted. In both cases, the member retains their original joining rate and tier upon reactivation, regardless of any pricing changes that may have occurred across branches during the freeze period.

7. Reactivation Procedure
Memberships automatically reactivate on the date specified in the original freeze confirmation unless the member requests an extension in advance. Reactivation restores full access across all branches at the member's original tier, including any court booking windows or guest privileges associated with that tier. Members are encouraged to confirm their reactivation date with Membership Services approximately one week beforehand, particularly if they intend to resume regular coaching sessions, so that preferred coaches and time slots can be reserved where possible.

8. Membership Transfer Between Individuals
Members who can no longer use their membership, whether due to permanent relocation, long-term injury, or other personal circumstance, may request to transfer their membership to another individual. Transfers are permitted once per membership per 12-month period and require both the outgoing and incoming member to complete a transfer form at any branch. The incoming member must meet all standard eligibility requirements, including age restrictions for adult memberships, and will assume the remaining contractual term and rate of the original membership rather than being offered a new joining rate. An administrative transfer fee applies, as set out in the current fee schedule.

9. Transfer Between Branches
Members relocating between emirates or simply preferring a different branch may request to transfer their home branch designation at no additional cost, provided the receiving branch has available capacity in the member's tier. Outdoor branches, which operate seasonal booking patterns during warmer months, may have limited capacity for new transfers during peak demand periods, and members may be placed on a short waiting list in such cases. Branch transfers do not reset any freeze allowances, tenure calculations, or loyalty benefits already accrued under the original branch enrolment.

10. Family and Corporate Plan Adjustments
Within family and corporate plans, individual members may be added, removed, or substituted subject to the terms of the master agreement rather than the individual freeze and transfer rules described above. Requests to substitute one family member for another, such as replacing a departing adult dependent with a new one, are treated as a transfer for administrative purposes but do not require the standard transfer fee if processed within the same billing cycle. Corporate plan administrators must submit substitution requests through their designated account manager rather than through general Membership Services channels.

11. Non-Transferable Elements
Certain benefits are explicitly non-transferable regardless of membership type, including accumulated loyalty points, complimentary guest passes issued as promotional incentives, and any personalised coaching packages purchased at a discounted rate tied to the original member's tenure. These elements are forfeited upon transfer unless a specific promotional term states otherwise. Members should review their original enrolment terms if uncertain whether a particular benefit is transferable, and Membership Services can provide written clarification upon request.

12. Denied or Delayed Requests
Freeze or transfer requests may be delayed or denied where outstanding balances exist on the account, where the request falls within a blackout period tied to a branch-wide tournament or facility closure, or where documentation supporting a medical or relocation exception is incomplete. Members whose requests are denied will receive a written explanation within 5 working days and may resubmit once the underlying issue, such as an outstanding balance, has been resolved. Denials are not treated as permanent refusals but as conditional holds pending further information or payment.

13. Disputes and Escalation
Members who disagree with the outcome of a freeze or transfer request may first raise the matter with the duty manager at their home branch, who will review the decision against this policy within 3 working days. If the matter remains unresolved, the member may escalate in writing to the central Membership Services office, which will issue a final written determination within 10 working days of receiving the escalation. This escalation path applies uniformly across all branches, regardless of whether the original request was made at an indoor or outdoor location.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect operational changes, seasonal booking patterns at outdoor branches, and evolving member needs. Any amendments will be communicated to members in advance of taking effect, through the member portal and, where the change materially affects existing freeze or transfer arrangements, through direct written notice. Members with an active freeze or in-progress transfer request at the time of any policy amendment will continue to be governed by the terms in place at the time their request was originally submitted, unless the amendment is more favourable to the member, in which case the updated terms will apply automatically.

title: Guest Access and Day Passes
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs the terms under which non-members may access Baseline Padel facilities across all branches, whether through a sponsored guest visit, a standalone day pass purchase, or a trial arrangement linked to a membership enquiry. It applies uniformly to indoor and outdoor branches, though certain clauses reference conditions specific to outdoor courts where seasonal or weather factors are relevant. Staff at every branch are expected to apply these rules consistently, and any deviation must be authorised by a duty manager or above. This document is intended to sit alongside, not replace, the general Membership Terms and the Court Booking Policy, both of which remain in force for any matter not explicitly addressed here.

2. Categories of Non-Member Access
Baseline Padel recognises three distinct categories of non-member access: the Sponsored Guest, who attends as the invitee of a full member and is recorded against that member's account; the Day Pass Holder, who purchases standalone access directly through the club app or front desk without any sponsoring member; and the Trial Visitor, who attends as part of a structured introductory session tied to a membership sales enquiry. Each category carries different pricing, booking privileges, and liability arrangements, and reception staff must correctly classify every non-member entry at check-in, as misclassification can affect insurance coverage and revenue reconciliation.

3. Sponsored Guest Allowances
Full members are entitled to bring sponsored guests onto court, subject to a monthly cap that varies by membership tier and is displayed on the member's account dashboard. A sponsoring member must be physically present at the branch for the duration of the guest's court time, save for the limited exception outlined in clause 9. Guest fees are charged to the sponsoring member's account at the point of booking and are non-refundable once the court window has commenced, regardless of whether the guest arrives. Members who repeatedly exceed their guest allowance by attempting to bring additional guests will be charged the prevailing day pass rate for each excess guest, billed retrospectively if not settled at the desk.

4. Day Pass Purchase and Validity
Day passes may be purchased in advance through the app or in person on the day, subject to court availability, and are valid only for the branch and date specified at purchase; they cannot be transferred to another branch or rolled over to a later date. A day pass entitles the holder to one court booking of up to ninety minutes within the operating hours stated for that branch, plus incidental access to changing facilities and the lounge area. Day passes purchased online are confirmed by an email and in-app notification within a few minutes of payment; if confirmation is not received within thirty minutes, the customer should contact the branch directly rather than assume the booking has failed, as duplicate purchases are not automatically refunded.

5. Identification and Check-In Requirements
All non-member visitors, regardless of category, must present a valid form of photographic identification at check-in, which is logged against the booking for security and insurance purposes. Sponsored guests must check in alongside their sponsoring member wherever practicable; where the sponsoring member has already checked in ahead of the guest's arrival, the guest may check in independently provided they can name the sponsoring member and the booking reference. Day pass holders under the age of eighteen must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian at check-in, who will be asked to countersign the standard liability waiver on the minor's behalf.

6. Trial Visitor Sessions
Trial sessions are offered to prospective members as an introduction to the club and are typically arranged through the membership sales team rather than booked independently through the app. These sessions are limited to one per prospective member within any rolling ninety-day period, and attempts to book repeat trials under slightly varied name spellings or contact details will be identified and declined by the membership team. Trial visitors are not permitted to bring their own guests, and the session is non-transferable to a friend or family member if the invited individual cannot attend.

7. Pricing, Promotions, and Blackout Periods
Day pass and guest fees are reviewed periodically and the current rates are always available on the club app and at reception; historical rates quoted verbally or in prior correspondence do not bind the club to honour them. Promotional day pass rates, where offered, are restricted to the terms stated at the time of the promotion and typically exclude peak evening slots and weekend mornings. Certain high-demand periods, particularly around club tournaments or exhibition events, may be designated blackout periods during which day passes and guest access are suspended entirely to preserve court availability for members; these blackout periods are announced with reasonable notice through the app and branch noticeboards.

8. Outdoor Branch Weather Considerations
At outdoor branches, day pass and guest bookings are subject to the same weather cancellation policy applied to member bookings, meaning that sessions affected by conditions deemed unsafe by the duty manager will be rescheduled or refunded at the club's discretion rather than automatically. Because outdoor courts cannot always be swapped for indoor alternatives at short notice, non-member visitors booking at an outdoor branch during periods of uncertain weather are advised to check conditions before travelling; the club does not accept liability for travel costs incurred where a session is cancelled due to weather. Where an indoor court is available at the same branch and can reasonably accommodate the booking, staff will offer this as an alternative before processing any refund.

9. Unaccompanied Guest Exception
While clause 3 requires the sponsoring member's presence throughout the guest's visit, a limited exception exists for members holding a Premium or higher tier membership, who may register up to two named guests annually as Unaccompanied Guests. These individuals may attend and play without the sponsoring member present, provided they have completed an in-person induction with a member of staff at some point in the preceding twelve months. This exception must be set up in advance through account services and cannot be arranged spontaneously at the front desk on the day of a visit.

10. Behavioural Standards and Conduct
Non-member visitors are expected to observe the same code of conduct as full members, including court etiquette, dress standards, and respectful behaviour toward staff and other players. A sponsoring member remains responsible for their guest's conduct for the duration of the visit, and repeated or serious breaches may result in the guest being barred from future visits and the sponsoring member's guest privileges being reviewed or suspended. Day pass holders and trial visitors found in breach of conduct standards may be asked to leave immediately without refund, and a record of the incident will be retained on file should the individual later apply for membership.

11. Refunds, No-Shows, and Late Cancellations
Day pass fees are refundable in full if cancelled at least twenty-four hours before the booked slot; cancellations made within twenty-four hours are refunded at fifty percent, and no-shows forfeit the full fee. Guest fees charged to a sponsoring member's account follow the same window but are credited back to the member's account balance rather than refunded to a card, unless the member specifically requests a card refund through account services. Exceptions to this schedule may be granted by a duty manager in cases of documented medical emergency or significant travel disruption, though supporting evidence may be requested and the decision rests solely with branch management.

12. Facility Access Limitations for Non-Members
Day pass holders and sponsored guests are entitled to use changing rooms, showers, and general lounge seating, but do not have access to member-only areas such as strength and conditioning studios, private lockers, or any branch's members' lounge where one exists. Equipment rental, where available, is charged separately and is not included in the day pass or guest fee. Non-members wishing to purchase food, beverages, or retail items during their visit may do so at standard pricing, and these purchases are settled independently of the court fee.

13. Escalation Path for Disputes
Any dispute regarding guest classification, billing, or access denial should first be raised with the duty manager on site at the time of the incident, as most matters of this nature are resolved more effectively in person and immediately. Where a resolution cannot be reached at branch level, the matter should be escalated in writing to the central membership services team within seven days of the incident, quoting the booking reference and the name of the staff member involved where possible. Central membership services will investigate and respond within a reasonable working period, and their decision represents the final stage of the internal resolution process before any external recourse is considered.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is subject to periodic review to reflect changes in operating hours, pricing structures, or facility offerings across the network of branches, and the version published on the club app should always be treated as the authoritative and current text. Members and prospective visitors are encouraged to review the guest access terms before each visit rather than rely on past experience, as allowances, caps, and pricing structures may be adjusted between visits without individual notification. Any significant change affecting existing guest arrangements, such as the Unaccompanied Guest exception, will be communicated to affected members directly through the app or by email in advance of the change taking effect.

title: Member Code of Conduct
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This Code of Conduct applies to every individual holding an active Baseline Padel membership, including corporate and family sub-members, across all branches. It governs behaviour on court, in shared facilities such as changing rooms and lounges, and in digital spaces including our booking app and official member channels.
