By activating a membership, whether purchased directly or transferred from another holder, the member agrees to be bound by this document as amended from time to time, with updates communicated through the app and displayed at reception areas.

2. Court Booking and Punctuality
Members are expected to arrive within ten minutes of their reserved slot; courts held beyond this window without notice may be reallocated to waitlisted members without refund of any credits used. Repeated late cancellations, defined as three or more within a rolling 60-day period, may result in a temporary suspension of advance booking privileges, reducing the booking window from seven days to 48 hours. Members booking on behalf of guests remain responsible for the guest's conduct and any charges arising from damage or delay, and proxy bookings made purely to circumvent peak-time restrictions are not permitted and may be cancelled without warning.

3. Attire and Equipment Standards
Appropriate sports attire and non-marking court shoes are mandatory on all indoor surfaces; failure to comply may result in a polite request to leave the court until suitable footwear is obtained. On outdoor branches, members should be mindful that open-toed footwear, bare torsos, or unsuitable clothing for a shared social environment are not permitted regardless of temperature. Personal equipment, including rackets and bags, should not be left unattended in communal areas for extended periods, as the club cannot accept liability for loss or damage to items left outside designated storage.

4. On-Court Conduct and Fair Play
All members are expected to play within the spirit of the game, calling lines honestly and resolving disputes calmly. Deliberate racket abuse, aggressive language directed at opponents, partners, or staff, or any conduct that disrupts adjoining courts will be treated as a breach of this Code. A first instance will typically result in a verbal reminder from the duty manager; a second instance within the same membership year may lead to a written warning placed on the member's file, viewable upon request.

5. Respect Toward Staff and Coaching Team
Coaches, receptionists, and maintenance staff across all branches are to be treated with courtesy at all times. Members raising a service concern should do so through the feedback form or directly with the duty manager rather than confronting staff on court or in public areas. Any instance of verbal abuse, intimidation, or discriminatory remarks toward staff will be escalated immediately to branch management and may result in suspension pending review, irrespective of the member's tenure or membership tier.

6. Guest Policy and Liability
Members may bring guests subject to the guest allowance attached to their tier, and all guests must be signed in at reception before accessing courts or facilities. The hosting member assumes full responsibility for their guest's adherence to this Code, including any damages, and repeated misuse of guest privileges, such as bringing the same individual with sufficient frequency to suggest unregistered use of the club, may result in the guest being asked to apply for their own membership or being declined further entry.

7. Health, Safety, and Medical Disclosure
Members participating in play do so at their own risk and are encouraged to disclose any relevant medical conditions to reception prior to intensive sessions, particularly during warmer months when heat-related strain is more likely on outdoor branches. Any injury occurring on premises should be reported to staff immediately so that first aid can be administered and an incident log completed; failure to report at the time may complicate any later claim. Members under the influence of alcohol or any substance impairing coordination will not be permitted to play, and staff reserve the right to decline access on safety grounds without obligation to justify the decision beyond a general safety concern.

8. Children and Family Members
Junior members and accompanied children must remain under adult supervision at all times outside of scheduled junior coaching sessions. Unsupervised children in lounges, pro shops, or car parks are not the club's responsibility, and repeated incidents of inadequate supervision may result in a discussion with the family's primary account holder. Junior members participating in adult social sessions must be approved in advance by the branch manager, taking into account both safety and the enjoyment of other members present.

9. Use of Shared Facilities
Changing rooms, showers, and lounge areas are shared spaces and should be left in a reasonable state for the next member. Photography or filming in changing areas is strictly prohibited under any circumstance, and any breach will be treated as a serious violation warranting immediate suspension pending investigation. Members hosting informal gatherings or celebrations within club premises should notify the duty manager in advance so that noise levels and space allocation can be managed fairly against other bookings.

10. Digital Conduct and Community Channels
Members engaging with official Baseline Padel community groups, leaderboards, or social features within the app are expected to maintain the same standard of respect required on court. Disparaging remarks about staff, other members, or specific branches posted publicly may be removed at the club's discretion, and members repeatedly posting inflammatory content may have their access to social features restricted while retaining full booking rights. Members are also asked not to use official channels to advertise personal coaching services or third-party commercial offers without prior written approval from branch management.

11. Breach Escalation Process
Where a breach of this Code is identified, the general approach follows a graduated path: an informal verbal reminder, followed by a written warning if the behaviour recurs, followed by a formal review meeting with branch management, and in serious or repeated cases, suspension or termination of membership. Certain breaches, including violence, harassment, theft, or serious safety violations, may bypass earlier stages and result in immediate suspension pending a formal review, which will typically be concluded within 14 days of the incident being reported.

12. Appeals and Right of Reply
A member subject to a written warning, suspension, or termination has the right to submit a written appeal within 14 days of notification, addressed to the regional membership office rather than the branch where the incident occurred, to ensure an independent review. The appeal should set out the member's account of events and any supporting evidence such as witness statements or footage where available. A decision on the appeal will typically be communicated within 21 days, and the outcome of this review is considered final within the club's internal process.

13. Membership Suspension and Termination Consequences
Where a membership is suspended, access to all branches is paused for the duration specified in the written notice, and any prepaid sessions or credits are held in abeyance rather than forfeited, to be reinstated upon the member's return to good standing. Where a membership is terminated for cause, no refund will be issued for the remaining term, and the individual may be required to reapply through a standard review process should they wish to rejoin at a later date, with no guarantee of approval. Corporate and family memberships affected by one individual's conduct will be assessed on a case-by-case basis so that other members on the same account are not unfairly penalised for behaviour outside their control.

14. Amendments to This Code
Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend this Code of Conduct periodically to reflect operational needs, seasonal considerations across indoor and outdoor branches, or changes in applicable regulation. Members will be notified of material changes through the app and via signage at reception areas, and continued use of any facility following such notice constitutes acceptance of the updated terms. Members are encouraged to review this document periodically, particularly before the transition between cooler and warmer months when outdoor branch operating hours and related conduct expectations may shift.

title: Renewal, Lapse and Reinstatement
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs how membership at Baseline Padel is renewed, how it lapses when renewal does not occur, and the process by which a lapsed membership may be reinstated. It applies uniformly across all branches, including outdoor branches where seasonal patterns of use may differ. Where a specific membership tier or corporate agreement contains terms that conflict with this policy, the more specific terms will govern, but in all other respects this document represents the standard position for individual, family and corporate memberships alike.

2. Renewal Cycle and Notification
Memberships run on either a monthly or annual cycle depending on the plan selected at enrolment. Members are notified of an upcoming renewal at least fourteen days before the charge date, via the email address and mobile number held on file. It is the member's responsibility to keep contact details current in the app or via reception; Baseline Padel cannot be held responsible for a missed notification caused by outdated information. Notifications will restate the renewal amount, the branch or branches covered, and any changes to benefits taking effect from that cycle.

3. Automatic Renewal and Payment Methods
Unless a member has actively opted out of automatic renewal through their account settings, membership will renew automatically using the payment method stored on file. Members may update their card or bank details at any time before the renewal date. Where more than one payment method is stored, the primary method will be attempted first, with a secondary method attempted only if the first is declined. A successful automatic renewal generates a receipt sent within 24 hours of processing.

4. Grace Period Following Failed Payment
If an automatic renewal payment fails, the member enters a seven-day grace period during which membership benefits continue uninterrupted and repeated payment attempts may be made against the stored method. During this window the member receives reminders encouraging them to update payment details. Bookings made before the failure remain valid, but no new bookings beyond the grace period may be confirmed until payment succeeds. Failure to resolve payment within the seven days results in the membership moving to lapsed status as described in clause 6.

5. Voluntary Non-Renewal
A member wishing not to renew must submit a cancellation request through the app or in writing at any branch at least five days before the next renewal date. Requests received after this point may not prevent the upcoming charge, though the membership will not renew again beyond that cycle. Voluntary non-renewal does not require a reason to be given, and no penalty attaches to a member who chooses not to continue, provided any outstanding balances from prior use of courts, coaching or retail credit are settled first.

6. Lapse of Membership
A membership is deemed lapsed when the grace period in clause 4 expires without successful payment, when a member allows an annual plan to run past its end date without renewing, or when a fixed-term membership simply concludes without a renewal instruction on file. Upon lapse, access to member rates, priority booking windows and any accrued loyalty benefits is suspended immediately. The member's profile remains on the system in a dormant state for a period of twelve months from the date of lapse, after which historical data may be archived in line with standard data retention practice.

7. Reinstatement Within 90 Days
A lapsed membership may be reinstated without a new joining fee if the request is made within 90 days of the lapse date. Reinstatement within this window restores the same tier, the same home branch designation where applicable, and any loyalty tier standing that had been earned, though it does not retroactively restore access to bookings or classes missed during the lapsed period. Reinstatement is processed by settling any outstanding balance from before the lapse and successfully charging the next renewal payment; the new cycle then begins from the date of reinstatement rather than from the original renewal date.

8. Reinstatement After Extended Lapse
Where more than 90 days have passed since the lapse date, reinstatement is still possible but is treated as a fresh enrolment. This means the standard joining fee applicable at the time of reinstatement will be charged, current pricing and tier structures will apply rather than any previously held legacy rate, and loyalty tier standing will not be restored automatically, though members may raise a request with the membership team for discretionary recognition of prior tenure. Requests of this nature are considered on a case-by-case basis and are not guaranteed.

9. Effect of Lapse on Benefits and Bookings
Once lapsed, any court time, coaching sessions or retail credit that formed part of a membership package and remained unused is forfeited and cannot be carried into a reinstated membership, whether reinstatement occurs within 90 days or beyond. Any recurring class enrolments tied to the membership are automatically cancelled at the point of lapse, and the member's place is released to the waiting list. Members intending to travel or take an extended break are strongly encouraged to use the seasonal suspension option described in clause 10 rather than allowing a membership to lapse unintentionally.

10. Seasonal Suspension and Renewal Interaction
Members may request a suspension of between 30 and 90 days once per membership year, most commonly used during the warmer months when outdoor branches see reduced play. A suspension pauses billing and extends the renewal date by the equivalent number of days, and it is treated entirely separately from a lapse; benefits and loyalty standing are preserved throughout. A suspension request must be submitted at least three days before it is due to begin and cannot be applied retroactively to cover a payment that has already failed.

11. Corporate and Family Membership Renewal
Corporate memberships renew on the anniversary of the master agreement rather than on an individual basis, and any lapse affects all linked individual profiles simultaneously unless the corporate administrator has arranged otherwise with the membership office. Family memberships renew as a single unit under the primary account holder; if the primary holder's payment method fails, all linked family profiles enter the grace period together, and reinstatement after a lapse restores the family unit as a whole rather than allowing individual members to be reinstated separately.

12. Fee Adjustments at Renewal
Membership fees are reviewed periodically and any adjustment will be communicated at least 30 days before it takes effect on a member's next renewal. Members who do not wish to accept a fee increase may cancel under the voluntary non-renewal terms in clause 5 without penalty, provided the request is submitted before the new rate is charged. Where a member is part-way through a fixed-term commitment, the previously agreed rate will continue to apply until that term concludes, and any increase will only apply from the following renewal onward.

13. Disputes and Escalation
A member disputing a lapse determination, a charge, or the terms offered for reinstatement should first raise the matter with reception or the app support channel at their home branch. If unresolved within five working days, the matter should be escalated in writing to the central membership office, which will respond within ten working days with a final internal decision. Members remain free to pursue any rights available to them under applicable consumer protections at any stage of this process, and nothing in this policy limits those rights.

14. Exceptional Circumstances
Where a lapse arises from documented exceptional circumstances such as prolonged illness, bereavement, or an unforeseen and verifiable disruption affecting a member's ability to manage their account, Baseline Padel will consider requests to waive the standard 90-day reinstatement window or to reduce a reinstatement fee. Such requests must be supported by reasonable evidence and are assessed individually by the membership office; approval is discretionary and any decision reached will be communicated in writing along with the specific terms of reinstatement offered.

title: Coaching Terms and Conditions
body:
1. Enrolment and Eligibility
All coaching programmes offered across Baseline Padel's eight branches are open to members and non-members alike, subject to available capacity at the relevant branch. Junior programmes require a parent or legal guardian to complete the registration form and accept these terms on the minor's behalf. Participants joining intermediate or advanced groups may be asked to complete a brief on-court assessment so that our coaching staff can confirm suitability; Baseline Padel reserves the right to reassign a participant to a more appropriate group level at any point during the programme.

2. Payment Terms
Coaching fees are payable in full at the time of booking unless a term-based instalment plan has been explicitly agreed in writing with the branch coaching coordinator. Bookings made through the app or website are confirmed only once payment has cleared. Outstanding balances left unpaid beyond 7 days from the invoice date may result in suspension of the participant's place until settled, and repeated late payment may lead to removal from a recurring programme without further notice.

3. Cancellations by the Participant
Participants who wish to cancel a private lesson must provide at least 24 hours' notice to avoid forfeiting the session fee. Group programme places cancelled with less than 48 hours' notice before the start of that week's session will not be refunded or credited, save where clause 11 (Medical and Compassionate Exceptions) applies. Cancellations of an entire term must be requested in writing and are subject to a pro-rated refund calculated from the date the request is received, not the date coaching last took place.

4. Cancellations and Rescheduling by Baseline Padel
Baseline Padel reserves the right to cancel, combine, or reschedule any coaching session where minimum participation numbers are not met, where a coach is unavailable due to illness or unforeseen circumstance, or where court conditions render play unsafe. In such cases, affected participants will be offered a make-up session, a credit to their account, or a suitable alternative time slot at the same or a nearby branch. No cash refunds will be issued for sessions rescheduled at Baseline Padel's initiative unless no reasonable alternative can be arranged within 30 days.

5. Weather-Affected Sessions at Outdoor Branches
Outdoor branches are subject to seasonal weather disruption, particularly during periods of high wind, heavy rain, or extreme heat as determined by branch management using standard club safety thresholds. Where a session is cancelled for weather reasons, participants will automatically be offered a make-up slot within the same programme term. Baseline Padel does not guarantee that make-up sessions will be delivered on covered or indoor courts, though reasonable efforts will be made to relocate affected groups to an indoor branch where capacity allows.

6. Make-Up Sessions
Make-up sessions are offered strictly at the discretion of the coaching team and must generally be used within the same term in which the missed session occurred, unless otherwise agreed in exceptional circumstances. Make-up credits are non-transferable between participants and cannot be exchanged for cash value. A maximum of two make-up sessions may be accrued per participant per term; unused credits beyond this limit will lapse automatically at the end of the term without further entitlement.

7. Private Coaching Bookings
Private and semi-private lessons are booked directly with an assigned coach or through the branch coordinator and are confirmed only once both parties have agreed a fixed time slot. Where a participant is more than 15 minutes late to a private lesson without prior notice, the coach reserves the right to shorten the session accordingly or treat it as forfeited, with the full fee still applying. Requests to change assigned coach for private coaching will be accommodated where reasonably possible but cannot be guaranteed given scheduling constraints across branches.

8. Equipment and Attire
Participants are expected to bring appropriate non-marking court shoes and comfortable sportswear suitable for padel; entry to coaching sessions may be refused where footwear is deemed unsuitable for the court surface. Loan racquets are available at most branches on a first-come basis and should be treated with reasonable care; damage beyond normal wear may be charged to the participant's account. Baseline Padel is not responsible for personal equipment left unattended courtside during coaching sessions.

9. Conduct and Behaviour
All participants, and parents or guardians of junior participants, are expected to conduct themselves respectfully towards coaching staff, fellow participants, and club property throughout every session. Baseline Padel reserves the right to remove any participant from a session or programme, without refund, where behaviour is deemed disruptive, unsafe, or abusive towards staff or other members. Repeated conduct concerns will be escalated to branch management and may result in suspension of coaching privileges across all branches.

10. Injury, Fitness, and Liability
Participants confirm, by enrolling, that they consider themselves fit to participate in padel coaching and agree to inform coaching staff of any relevant medical condition, injury, or pregnancy prior to the start of a session. Coaches are not medical professionals and cannot be held responsible for injuries sustained during normal play where reasonable safety practices have been followed. Any participant who sustains an injury during a session should report it to staff immediately so that an incident record can be logged; this record may be required for any subsequent insurance or liability review.

11. Medical and Compassionate Exceptions
Where a participant is unable to attend coaching due to documented illness, injury, or a compassionate circumstance, Baseline Padel may, at its discretion, offer a credit, pause, or partial refund outside the standard cancellation terms outlined in clause 3. Requests of this nature should be submitted in writing to the branch coordinator along with any relevant supporting documentation within 14 days of the missed session, and each case will be assessed individually rather than under a fixed formula.

12. Programme Pauses and Transfers
Participants who need to pause a coaching programme for an extended period, such as travel or injury recovery, may request a term freeze rather than a cancellation, subject to coordinator approval and available capacity upon return. Transfers between branches are permitted where the destination branch runs an equivalent programme at a comparable level, though participants should be aware that coaching style, group composition, and available time slots will vary from branch to branch and cannot be guaranteed to match the original booking.

13. Coach Changes and Programme Continuity
Baseline Padel structures its coaching programmes around consistent staffing where possible, but reserves the right to substitute or reassign coaches due to leave, relocation between branches, or operational need. Such changes do not constitute grounds for refund or cancellation under these terms, as programme content and level progression remain the responsibility of the branch coaching team as a whole rather than any single individual.

14. Complaints and Escalation
Any concern regarding coaching quality, billing, or conduct should first be raised with the relevant branch coordinator, who will aim to respond within 3 working days. Where a matter remains unresolved, it may be escalated in writing to Baseline Padel's central coaching management, who will conduct a review and issue a final written response within 21 days of the escalation being received. Decisions reached at this stage represent Baseline Padel's final position on coaching-related disputes unless new evidence is subsequently presented.

title: Coach Session Cancellation
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs the cancellation, rescheduling, and forfeiture of privately booked and small-group coaching sessions across all branches of Baseline Padel, including both indoor and outdoor courts. It applies to all coaching formats offered by the club, including one-to-one lessons, duo and trio sessions, junior development blocks, and clinic-style group coaching sold in multi-session packages. It does not apply to open social play, ladder matches, or court-only bookings, which are covered under separate club policies. Where a member has purchased a coaching package that spans multiple branches, the terms below apply uniformly regardless of which location the session was originally scheduled at.

2. Standard Notice Period
Members and guests wishing to cancel or reschedule a confirmed coaching session must provide at least 24 hours' notice ahead of the scheduled start time. Notice given within this window allows the session to be moved to another available slot within the validity period of the member's package, at no additional charge, subject to coach availability. Notice provided outside this window, including same-day cancellations, will typically result in the session being marked as used, with the associated credit or session count deducted from the member's account as though the lesson had taken place.

3. Late Cancellation Charges
Where a session is cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice and no package credit is available to absorb the loss, a late cancellation charge equivalent to the full session rate will be applied to the member's account. This charge reflects the coach's reserved time and the opportunity cost of a court slot that could otherwise have been offered to another member. Repeated late cancellations, defined as three or more within a rolling 60-day period, may result in a review of the member's coaching privileges by the branch coaching lead, who may require sessions to be prepaid in full going forward rather than drawn from a flexible package.

4. No-Show Policy
Failure to attend a scheduled session without any prior communication is treated as a no-show and is subject to the same charges as a late cancellation, with no exceptions for traffic, weather at outdoor branches, or last-minute scheduling conflicts. Coaches are required to wait no more than 15 minutes past the scheduled start time before marking a session as a no-show and releasing the court. Members arriving after this window may request to continue for the remaining time at the coach's discretion, but the session will still be logged as attended for billing and package purposes.

5. Coach-Initiated Cancellations
Where a session is cancelled by the club due to coach illness, unforeseen unavailability, or an operational issue at the branch, the member will not lose any session credit and will be offered a choice between rescheduling at the earliest mutual availability or receiving the session back into their package with an extended expiry date to compensate for the disruption. In cases where a member's regular coach is unavailable for an extended period, such as during injury recovery or extended leave, the branch coaching lead will offer a suitable substitute coach of comparable level wherever possible, and members are not obliged to accept the substitute if they would prefer to pause and resume with their original coach once available.

6. Weather-Related Disruption at Outdoor Branches
At outdoor branches, sessions affected by rain, excessive heat advisories, or other conditions deemed unsafe for play by the duty manager will be cancelled without penalty to the member, regardless of the notice period otherwise required. In such cases, staff will attempt to contact the member as early as practical, and where courts are covered but conditions remain unsuitable for coaching intensity work, the coach retains discretion to shorten or convert the session into a lighter format rather than cancel outright, with member agreement. Members who prefer not to proceed under marginal conditions may decline the modified session without losing their credit, provided this preference is communicated before the session begins.

7. Package and Block Booking Cancellations
Members who have purchased a multi-session coaching block and wish to cancel the block entirely, rather than an individual session, must submit a written request to the branch reception or via the club's member portal. Refunds for unused sessions within a block are calculated based on the number of sessions actually delivered, charged at the higher single-session rate rather than the discounted block rate, with the remaining balance returned as account credit within 14 days of the request being processed. Cash or original payment method refunds are only issued in cases of demonstrated medical incapacity or relocation away from all branch service areas, supported by appropriate documentation submitted to the membership office.

8. Junior Coaching Cancellations
Cancellations for junior development sessions follow the same 24-hour notice requirement, but parents and guardians are given an additional courtesy allowance of one same-day cancellation per term without charge, in recognition of the unpredictability of school and family schedules. This allowance does not carry over between terms and is tracked automatically against the family's account. Persistent late cancellations for junior sessions will be addressed directly with the parent or guardian by the junior programme coordinator rather than through automated charges, given the coaching relationship's long-term nature.

9. Group Clinic Cancellations
For coach-led group clinics involving three or more participants, an individual participant's cancellation does not cancel the session for the remaining group, and the cancelling member's slot may be offered to a waitlisted member at the branch's discretion. Where fewer than the minimum required participants remain following cancellations, typically three for adult clinics and four for junior clinics, the club reserves the right to cancel the clinic entirely and notify remaining participants as early as possible, offering either a full credit or placement in an alternative clinic of equivalent level.

10. Rescheduling Limits
Sessions rescheduled under the standard notice period may be moved no more than twice before the original booking is considered forfeit, in order to maintain fairness across coach schedules and prevent indefinite deferral of paid sessions. Exceptions to this limit may be granted by the branch coaching lead in cases involving documented medical circumstances, bereavement, or comparable hardship, and such exceptions should be requested in writing rather than assumed.

11. Membership Freezes and Coaching Credit
Members who place their overall club membership on freeze, whether for travel, injury, or personal reasons, will have any associated coaching package credit frozen in parallel, with the expiry date extended by the equivalent freeze period upon reactivation. Coaching sessions cannot be used during an active freeze period even if the member remains physically present at a branch, as the freeze applies to the account as a whole rather than to individual services.

12. Disputes Over Charges
Members who believe a late cancellation or no-show charge has been applied in error, for instance where notice was given through a channel not properly logged by staff, should raise the matter with branch reception within 7 days of the charge appearing on their account. Disputes raised after this window may still be considered but are less likely to succeed given the difficulty of verifying communication records retrospectively. All disputes are reviewed by the branch coaching lead in the first instance, with escalation to regional coaching management available if the member remains unsatisfied with the outcome.

13. Escalation Path
Where a member's concern extends beyond a single charge, such as a pattern of coach unavailability, repeated administrative errors, or dissatisfaction with how a substitute coach was assigned, the matter should be escalated in writing to the regional coaching management team via the member portal or branch reception. Regional management will acknowledge escalations within 3 working days and aim to provide a substantive response within 10 working days, which may include goodwill credit, a formal apology, or a review of branch-level coaching procedures where systemic issues are identified.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically by club management to reflect changes in coaching operations, branch capacity, and member feedback, and any amendments will be communicated to members through the club portal and in-branch notices ahead of taking effect. Continued use of coaching services following such notice constitutes acceptance of the updated terms, and members with active packages at the time of any material change will have existing sessions honoured under the terms in place at the time of purchase unless the change is required for safety or regulatory reasons.

title: Academy Levels and Progression
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how players are assessed, placed, and progressed through the Baseline Padel Academy structure across all branches. It applies to junior and adult participants enrolled in group coaching programmes, whether on indoor or outdoor courts, and is designed to ensure that a player assessed at one branch receives a comparable standard of coaching and progression logic at any other branch within the group. It does not apply to private one-to-one lessons, which are governed separately, though private coaching outcomes may feed into academy level reviews as described in clause 10.

2. The Level Framework
The academy operates a six-tier framework: Foundation, Improver, Intermediate, Advanced Intermediate, Advanced, and Performance. Foundation and Improver focus on core technique, court movement, and rule literacy. Intermediate and Advanced Intermediate introduce tactical structure, shot selection under pressure, and doubles positioning. Advanced and Performance are reserved for players demonstrating consistent match-level execution and are typically the pathway into club competitive squads or tournament preparation groups. Every branch runs sessions against this same six-tier structure, though not every branch will run every tier in every timetable slot, particularly at smaller outdoor branches where court availability is limited during peak season.

3. Initial Placement Assessment
All new academy participants must complete an initial placement assessment before joining a group. This typically takes the form of a supervised hitting session lasting between thirty and forty-five minutes, during which a coach observes grip, movement, shot consistency, spatial awareness, and general match understanding. Players transferring from another padel programme outside Baseline, or returning after a long absence, are also required to sit this assessment regardless of any prior level claimed elsewhere. Self-declared levels are never accepted without observation, as experience has shown that perceived ability and observed ability frequently diverge, particularly among players who have learned informally.

4. Placement Outcomes and Provisional Status
Following assessment, a player is placed into a level on a provisional basis for their first four to six sessions. Provisional status exists because a single assessment session cannot fully capture how a player performs in a live group dynamic over successive weeks. During this provisional period, the assigned coach may recommend an adjustment up or down one tier without requiring a full reassessment, and will communicate this recommendation directly to the player or, for juniors, to the parent or guardian, along with a brief written rationale available on request from reception.

5. Progression Criteria
Movement between levels is never based purely on time served or number of sessions attended, although a minimum attendance threshold of seventy percent within a given term is required before any progression will be considered. Coaches evaluate progression against a published set of technical and tactical benchmarks specific to each tier, covering consistency of groundstrokes, volley control, lob and bandeja execution, net presence, and decision-making in doubles formation. A player must demonstrate these benchmarks reliably across multiple sessions and, where possible, in at least one supervised match-play scenario, before a coach will recommend advancement.

6. Formal Review Points
Each term includes a formal review point, generally in the final one to two weeks before the term ends, during which every academy participant's progress is assessed by their assigned coach and, where the coach deems it useful, a second coach for an independent view. Outcomes are communicated in writing within seven days of the review and fall into one of three categories: progression to the next tier, continuation at the current tier for a further term, or, in rare cases, a recommended step down where a player has been struggling significantly or has had an extended absence that affected retained ability. Step-down recommendations are always discussed directly with the player or guardian before being actioned, never applied unilaterally.

7. Coach Consistency and Cross-Branch Recognition
Because players occasionally train at more than one branch, or relocate between branches due to travel or relocation, a level assigned at one branch is recognised at all others without requiring a full reassessment, provided the level was confirmed within the preceding twelve months. Coaches receiving a transferring player are nonetheless encouraged to observe them for at least one session and may flag a discrepancy through the academy coordinator if the player's demonstrated ability seems significantly misaligned with their recorded level. This safeguard exists because informal coaching standards can vary slightly session to session even within a consistent framework, and the priority is always to place a player in a group where they can be appropriately challenged without being overwhelmed.

8. Junior Pathway Considerations
Junior progression follows the same six-tier structure but is assessed with additional weight given to physical development stage, coordination, and attention span appropriate to age, rather than adult-equivalent technical polish. Junior coaches conduct reviews slightly more frequently, generally every six to eight weeks rather than by term, in recognition of how quickly younger players can develop or, conversely, plateau due to growth spurts affecting coordination. Parents and guardians are given more detailed verbal feedback at each review point than is standard for adult groups, and are welcome to request a short observation window at the end of any session to watch their child's group in action, subject to coach availability and not disrupting the session in progress.

9. Outdoor Branch and Seasonal Adjustments
At outdoor branches, extreme heat during the warmer months can materially affect session intensity, court time, and therefore the pace of technical development. Academy coordinators at these branches are permitted to extend provisional assessment periods or delay formal review points by up to two weeks where sessions have been repeatedly shortened, rescheduled to early morning or evening slots, or cancelled due to heat protocols. This adjustment is applied at branch level and communicated to affected participants; it is not intended to disadvantage outdoor branch players relative to indoor branch players, and coordinators are expected to document any such delay so that cross-branch comparisons remain fair.

10. Interaction with Private Coaching
Players who supplement academy group sessions with private one-to-one coaching may have observations from their private coach considered as supporting evidence during a formal review, provided the private coach submits brief written notes to the academy coordinator at least three days before the review point. This is supplementary only; private coaching notes cannot substitute for the academy coach's own direct observation, and a player cannot progress on the basis of private coaching alone without having attended the required minimum number of group sessions in that term.

11. Plateauing and Extended Non-Progression
Where a player remains at the same tier for three consecutive terms without meaningful progress being noted, the academy coordinator will schedule a dedicated review conversation separate from the standard end-of-term process. This conversation exists to identify whether the plateau is technical, tactical, physical, or motivational in nature, and may result in recommendations such as a temporary switch to a different coach, a short block of private lessons, a change of session time to a more suitable group dynamic, or, in some cases, a candid conversation about realistic expectations for further advancement. Plateauing is not treated as a failure on the player's part; it is treated as a signal that the current approach needs adjusting.

12. Fast-Track Progression
On occasion a player demonstrates ability well beyond their assigned tier, whether through prior competitive experience, rapid natural development, or a background in a closely related racket sport. In such cases the assigned coach may recommend a fast-track progression of more than one tier at a time, but this requires sign-off from the branch's senior coach or academy coordinator, plus a short trial session at the proposed higher tier to confirm the player can keep pace without disrupting that group's dynamic. Fast-tracking into the Performance tier additionally requires an informal conversation about competitive expectations, as this tier often overlaps with tournament preparation commitments.

13. Disputes and Reassessment Requests
A player or guardian who disagrees with a placement or review outcome may request a reassessment through the branch reception or academy coordinator within fourteen days of being notified. Reassessment requests are free of charge on the first occasion within any twelve-month period; subsequent requests within the same period may incur a nominal administrative fee to discourage repeated informal challenges to coach judgement. Reassessments are conducted by a coach other than the one who made the original recommendation wherever staffing allows, to ensure an independent perspective, and the outcome of a reassessment is treated as final unless new circumstances arise, such as a documented injury that affected the original session.

14. Escalation Beyond the Branch
If a dispute cannot be resolved at branch level, either because a player disagrees with the outcome of a reassessment or because there is a concern about how a policy has been applied, the matter may be escalated in writing to the group's central academy office. Escalations are acknowledged within three working days and typically resolved within fifteen working days, during which the player continues training at their most recently confirmed level rather than being held out of sessions. This escalation path exists as a final safeguard and is used infrequently, as the overwhelming majority of placement and progression matters are resolved satisfactorily through direct conversation with the assigned coach or branch coordinator.

title: Private and Semi-Private Lessons
body:
1. Scope and Eligibility
This policy governs all private and semi-private coaching sessions delivered across Baseline Padel's eight branches, whether held on indoor or outdoor courts. It applies to members and non-members alike, though non-members must complete a one-time registration at reception before their first booking. Private lessons are limited to a single player and one coach, while semi-private sessions accommodate two to four players sharing a coach at a reduced per-head rate. Junior players under the age of twelve must be accompanied by a guardian for the duration of the session unless the guardian has provided written consent on file at the branch.

2. Booking Procedures
All coaching sessions must be booked through the Baseline Padel app or directly with the branch coaching desk, subject to coach and court availability. Bookings are confirmed only once payment or a valid credit has been applied to the reservation; provisional holds are released automatically if not confirmed within a set window shown at the time of booking. Members with active coaching packages should quote their package reference to avoid duplicate charges. Same-day bookings are accepted where a coach's schedule allows, but priority is always given to sessions booked at least 24 hours in advance.

3. Coach Selection and Allocation
Players may request a specific coach, though availability cannot be guaranteed across all branches, particularly during peak evening slots or the cooler months when demand for outdoor coaching rises sharply. Where a requested coach is unavailable, the branch will offer a comparable alternative matched by playing level and coaching specialism. Baseline Padel does not permit players to book a coach for a branch other than where that coach is contractually based, except where a temporary cross-branch arrangement has been pre-approved by the regional coaching manager.

4. Semi-Private Group Composition
Semi-private lessons are intended for players of broadly similar ability, and the coaching team reserves the right to decline a booking or suggest a private session instead where the skill gap between participants would compromise the quality or safety of the lesson. Groups formed independently by players are responsible for ensuring all participants have registered individually before the session; the club does not act as an intermediary for payment disputes between members of a self-organised group. Where a participant withdraws from a semi-private group after confirmation, the remaining players are jointly responsible for either finding a replacement or absorbing the balance of the fee.

5. Session Duration and Structure
Standard sessions run for sixty minutes, with ninety-minute sessions available on request subject to court and coach scheduling. Coaches are expected to begin and conclude sessions promptly to avoid disruption to the following booking. Extensions beyond the booked duration are only possible where the subsequent court slot is unoccupied and must be arranged directly with the coach and confirmed at the front desk, with any additional time charged at the standard hourly rate.

6. Pricing, Packages, and Validity
Pricing for private and semi-private lessons varies by coach seniority, branch, and time of day, with full rate cards available at each reception and within the app. Multi-session packages purchased in advance typically offer a discount against single bookings but are subject to a validity period, usually 90 days from the date of purchase, after which unused sessions are forfeited without refund. Package sessions are non-transferable between players except in the case of immediate family members registered under the same household account.

7. Cancellations and Rescheduling
Cancellations made more than 24 hours before a scheduled session may be rescheduled or credited back to a package without penalty. Cancellations made within 24 hours are subject to a cancellation charge equivalent to the full session fee, reflecting the coach's reserved time, except in cases of documented medical emergency or where the branch itself cancels the session. Repeated late cancellations may result in a requirement to prepay for future bookings in full at the time of reservation.

8. Late Arrivals and No-Shows
Players arriving late to a confirmed session will still be charged for the full booked duration, as the coach's time has been reserved regardless of actual court time used. A player who fails to arrive within fifteen minutes of the scheduled start time without prior notice will be marked as a no-show, forfeiting the full session fee or package credit. Coaches are not obliged to extend a session to compensate for a late arrival.

9. Weather and Outdoor Branch Considerations
At outdoor branches, sessions may be postponed or relocated to an available indoor court where extreme heat, high winds, or sandstorm conditions present a safety concern, at the sole discretion of the duty manager or coach. Where no indoor court is available and the session cannot proceed, players will be offered a full credit or complimentary rescheduling rather than a cash refund. Baseline Padel encourages players booking outdoor sessions during the warmer months to select early morning or evening slots where possible, though this remains a matter of personal preference rather than club obligation.

10. Equipment, Court Fees, and Inclusions
Court hire is included within the price of all private and semi-private lessons booked through the coaching desk, though players are responsible for their own racquets unless a rental has been separately requested and paid for. Balls are supplied by the coach as standard. Any additional services requested during a session, such as video analysis or extended footage review, may incur a supplementary charge disclosed before the session begins.

11. Coach Unavailability and Substitution
In the event that an assigned coach becomes unavailable due to illness, injury, or unforeseen circumstance, the branch will attempt to offer a substitute coach of comparable standing with reasonable notice. Where no suitable substitute can be arranged, the affected player will be offered a full credit toward a future session or a refund processed within a reasonable period from the date the cancellation is confirmed. Baseline Padel does not accept liability for indirect costs, such as travel arrangements, arising from a coach cancellation.

12. Conduct, Safety, and Suitability
All players are expected to conduct themselves respectfully toward coaches and fellow participants throughout a session. Coaches retain the right to pause or end a session early where a player's conduct is unsafe, abusive, or otherwise unsuitable for continuation, without entitlement to a refund for the unused portion. Players with pre-existing medical conditions or injuries are strongly encouraged to disclose relevant details to their coach before the session begins so that the lesson plan can be adjusted accordingly.

13. Complaints and Escalation
Any concerns regarding coaching quality, conduct, or billing should first be raised directly with the branch coaching desk, where the majority of issues can be resolved within a short timeframe. Where a matter remains unresolved, players may escalate the complaint in writing to the regional coaching manager, who will review the matter and respond within a reasonable period. Baseline Padel treats all coaching-related complaints as confidential and will not disclose details to third parties beyond those necessary to investigate and resolve the issue.

14. Policy Amendments
Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend this policy from time to time to reflect operational, seasonal, or regulatory changes across its branches. Updated versions will be made available through the app and at branch reception, and continued use of coaching services following such updates constitutes acceptance of the revised terms. Players with an active package at the time of any material change will have existing entitlements honoured for the remainder of that package's validity period.

title: Coaching Standards and Conduct
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out the standards of coaching practice, professional conduct, and accountability expected of every coach engaged by Baseline Padel, whether employed directly, contracted on a freelance basis, or delivering sessions under a guest arrangement at any of our eight branches. It applies equally to head coaches, assistant coaches, academy leads, and any visiting professional invited to deliver clinics or private lessons on our courts. Where a coach operates across multiple branches, the standards in this document travel with them and are not diluted by local custom or informal arrangements agreed at branch level. Members and guests are entitled to expect a consistent standard of instruction, communication, and behaviour regardless of which branch they attend or which coach they are paired with.

2. Qualification and Accreditation Requirements
All coaches delivering paid instruction, whether group clinics, private lessons, or junior programmes, must hold a recognised coaching qualification appropriate to the level being taught, along with valid safeguarding and first aid certification current at the time of delivery. Copies of certification are held on file by the coaching department and are subject to periodic audit; a coach whose documentation lapses is suspended from the timetable until renewal is confirmed, with no exceptions made for popularity, waiting lists, or member requests. Coaches transitioning from playing careers into coaching roles are required to complete the same accreditation pathway as any other applicant; prior competitive standing does not substitute for formal certification. Trainee or apprentice coaches may shadow and assist under direct supervision but may not deliver unsupervised paid sessions until sign-off is recorded by a head coach.

3. Session Preparation and Punctuality
Coaches are expected to arrive with sufficient time to prepare the court, equipment, and any session plan before the scheduled start, and to be present and ready at least ten minutes ahead of group clinics involving juniors. Persistent lateness, cancellation with insufficient notice, or repeated failure to prepare adequately for a booked session is treated as a conduct matter rather than a scheduling inconvenience, and will be addressed through the escalation path outlined later in this policy. Where a coach is genuinely unable to attend due to illness, family emergency, or travel disruption, the branch coaching coordinator must be notified at the earliest possible opportunity so that members can be offered a substitute coach, a rescheduled session, or an appropriate credit rather than discovering the cancellation on arrival.

4. Duty of Care and Supervision Ratios
Coaches are responsible for the safety and welfare of every participant under their instruction for the duration of the session, including the period immediately before and after court time when players are gathering equipment or leaving the facility. Group sessions must not exceed the maximum participant-to-coach ratio set for the relevant age group and format, and this ratio is non-negotiable even where a member requests an exception or where a branch is unusually busy. Junior sessions carry additional safeguarding obligations, including maintaining visual supervision at all times and never being alone with a single minor in an enclosed space without another adult present or visible. Any injury, near-miss, or safeguarding concern arising during a session must be logged with the branch duty manager before the coach leaves the premises that day, regardless of how minor the incident may appear.

5. Professional Conduct on Court
Coaches represent Baseline Padel at all times while on our premises, whether actively coaching, observing, or socialising between sessions, and are expected to conduct themselves with the same courtesy and professionalism as they would in a formal interview setting. Raised voices, sarcasm directed at participants, visible frustration with a player's progress, or language that could reasonably be perceived as demeaning is not acceptable under any circumstances, including in high-performance or competitive junior programmes where standards are naturally more demanding. Coaches must not smoke, vape, or consume alcohol immediately before or during a coaching session, and must not coach while under the influence of any substance that could impair judgement or reaction time. Mobile phone use during active instruction should be limited to genuine emergencies; a coach checking messages while participants wait on court reflects poorly on the club and undermines the value members are paying for.

6. Personal Relationships and Boundaries
Coaches must maintain clear professional boundaries with members and, in particular, with junior participants and their families. Private contact details should not be exchanged with minors without a parent or guardian directly included in the communication, and coaches are expected to route all scheduling, feedback, and billing conversations through official club channels rather than personal messaging apps wherever possible. Romantic or intimate relationships between a coach and a current adult student are strongly discouraged while the coaching relationship is active, and must be disclosed to branch management if they occur, as continuing to coach that individual without disclosure represents a conflict of interest. Gift-giving beyond token, occasional gestures is discouraged in both directions, and coaches should decline any gift that could reasonably be perceived as an attempt to secure preferential treatment, extra court time, or favourable scheduling.

7. Private Lesson Conduct and Payment Handling
All private lessons must be booked and paid for through official club systems; coaches are not permitted to arrange off-book private coaching on club courts or to accept direct cash payment in place of the standard booking process. A coach found to be circumventing the booking system, whether to avoid commission, taxation, or simply for convenience, will face disciplinary action regardless of how long the arrangement has been in place or how satisfied the member may be with the outcome. Coaches delivering private lessons should confirm the agreed focus of the session with the member beforehand and provide brief, honest feedback afterwards; overstating a player's progress to encourage further bookings is a misrepresentation of the service and will be treated as a conduct issue if identified.

8. Use of Club Equipment and Facilities
Demonstration racquets, ball baskets, target cones, and other coaching equipment remain club property and must be returned to designated storage after each session rather than left courtside or removed from the premises for personal use. Coaches wishing to trial or recommend specific equipment to members should do so based on genuine suitability rather than any personal arrangement with a supplier, and must disclose to branch management any sponsorship, discount, or commission relationship with an equipment brand that could influence such recommendations. Outdoor branches present particular equipment demands, including faster wear on balls and grips due to heat and surface conditions, and coaches at these locations are expected to flag deteriorating equipment promptly rather than continuing to use it past a reasonable standard.

9. Feedback, Grievances, and Member Complaints
Members who have a concern about a coach's conduct, competence, or communication style are encouraged to raise it directly with the branch coaching coordinator in the first instance, either verbally or in writing. All complaints are logged and reviewed regardless of how minor they may initially appear, and the coach concerned will be informed of the substance of the complaint and given a fair opportunity to respond before any action is taken. Anonymous or informal complaints raised through social channels rather than official ones will still be investigated where they contain specific, actionable detail, though members are encouraged to use formal channels to ensure a proper record and response. A pattern of similar complaints against the same coach across different branches or time periods is treated more seriously than an isolated incident, even where no single complaint alone would warrant escalation.

10. Escalation Path for Conduct Concerns
Minor conduct issues, such as a single instance of lateness or a lapse in communication, are typically addressed through an informal conversation between the coach and their branch coaching coordinator, with the outcome noted on file. Repeated or more serious concerns are escalated to a formal review involving the head of coaching, where the coach is entitled to present their account and, if desired, bring a colleague for support. Where a safeguarding concern, safety breach, or serious professional misconduct is alleged, the coach may be suspended from the timetable with immediate effect pending investigation, regardless of seniority or tenure, and the matter will be handled in line with the club's wider safeguarding and disciplinary procedures rather than this policy alone. Coaches who disagree with the outcome of a formal review may request a single further review by a senior manager not previously involved in the case, submitted in writing within a reasonable period from the date of the original decision.

11. Confidentiality and Data Handling
Coaches routinely hold sensitive information about members, including contact details, medical notes relevant to participation, and, in junior programmes, information shared by parents in confidence. This information must not be discussed with other members, shared on personal devices beyond what is operationally necessary, or used for any purpose outside the coaching relationship. Coaches leaving the club, whether by resignation, non-renewal of contract, or termination, are required to return or delete any member data held on personal devices and must not retain contact lists for the purpose of soliciting members to a competing facility.

12. Outdoor Branch Considerations
Coaches delivering sessions at outdoor branches carry additional responsibilities around heat management, hydration reminders, and session pacing during warmer periods, and must be prepared to shorten, adapt, or postpone a session where conditions present a genuine risk to participant welfare, particularly for junior or beginner groups. A coach who continues a full-intensity session in conditions that clearly warrant modification will be considered to have breached duty of care obligations under clause four, even if no participant is visibly harmed. Coaches at outdoor branches should also monitor court surface conditions after rain or dust, and are expected to flag any surface hazard to the duty manager before allowing play to continue.

13. Ongoing Development and Review
All coaches are expected to take part in periodic internal reviews, which may include observed sessions, member feedback summaries, and a short conversation with the head of coaching. These reviews are developmental rather than punitive in the first instance and are intended to maintain a consistent standard across all branches rather than to catch coaches out. Coaches are encouraged to raise their own development needs, including interest in further qualifications or specialisation in areas such as junior pathway coaching or adult beginner programmes, and the club will support reasonable requests where operationally feasible.

14. Policy Amendments
This policy may be updated from time to time to reflect changes in safeguarding guidance, club operations, or lessons learned from previous incidents. Coaches will be notified of any material changes ahead of implementation, and continued delivery of coaching services after such notice constitutes acceptance of the updated terms. Where any clause in this document conflicts with a specific written agreement held by an individual coach, the more protective standard for member and participant welfare will apply.

title: Facility Rules and Court Etiquette
body:
1. Scope and Application
These Facility Rules and Court Etiquette guidelines apply to every member, guest, junior player, and visiting coach across all branches, whether indoor, outdoor, or mixed-format. By booking a court, attending a session, or entering any Baseline Padel premises, individuals agree to abide by the standards set out below. Branch managers retain discretion to apply supplementary local rules where site-specific conditions require it, such as additional guidance for rooftop courts or shared-access facilities, provided these do not contradict the principles established here.

2. Court Access and Booking Conduct
Courts must only be occupied by the individuals named on the confirmed booking, plus any additional players registered at check-in. Arriving more than fifteen minutes after the scheduled start time without notifying the front desk may result in the slot being released to a waiting member, with no obligation on the club to offer a substitute time. Players are asked to vacate the court promptly at the end of their session to allow cleaning and turnover, particularly during peak evening hours when back-to-back bookings are common. Repeated late vacation may lead to a formal reminder and, if unresolved, a temporary booking restriction.

3. Footwear and Court Surface Protection
Only non-marking padel or tennis shoes with appropriate tread are permitted on court. Running shoes, football boots, or any footwear with studs, spikes, or heavily patterned soles that risk damaging synthetic turf or glass panelling are strictly prohibited. Staff are authorised to refuse court access to anyone wearing unsuitable footwear, and no refund or credit will be issued in such cases. Members are encouraged to keep a dedicated pair of court shoes in their kit bag, as outdoor branches in particular can accumulate dust and debris that accelerates wear on unsuitable soles.

4. Attire and Personal Presentation
Active sportswear appropriate to padel is required at all times; this includes shirts for all players, with vest tops permitted but bare-chested play not allowed regardless of weather conditions. Denim, sandals, and open-toed footwear are not appropriate for court use under any circumstances. During cooler months, outer layers are permitted provided they do not restrict movement or pose a safety risk when swung near the glass or netting. Branch staff may politely decline entry to court for attire deemed unsafe or unsuitable, and this decision is final for that session.

5. Glass and Fencing Etiquette
Padel's enclosed court design means glass and mesh fencing form part of active play, but they remain structural fixtures rather than equipment to be struck deliberately outside of normal shot-making. Kicking, punching, or hanging from the glass, fencing, or door frames is prohibited and may result in immediate suspension of play. Any player who notices a crack, loose panel, or damaged door mechanism should stop play and report it to the front desk immediately rather than continuing on a potentially unsafe court. Courts flagged for structural review will be closed until an inspection confirms they are safe for use again.

6. Noise, Language, and Conduct Between Players
Padel is a social sport and a reasonable level of enthusiasm, including calling scores or celebrating points, is entirely normal and welcomed. However, excessive shouting, abusive language, racket throwing, or conduct intended to intimidate opponents or neighbouring courts will not be tolerated. Staff have the authority to issue a verbal warning in the first instance; a second incident within the same session may result in the booking being terminated without refund. Persistent complaints from other members about a particular individual's conduct will be escalated to branch management for review under clause 13.

7. Spectators and Non-Playing Guests
Spectators are welcome to watch matches from designated viewing areas but are not permitted to enter the court itself, coach from the sidelines during another party's paid session, or leave personal belongings courtside where they may obstruct play. Children accompanying spectators must remain seated and supervised at all times, particularly at outdoor branches where courts are positioned close to walkways. Any spectator whose behaviour distracts players or breaches general club conduct standards may be asked to relocate to the lounge or clubhouse area.

8. Equipment, Balls, and Loan Rackets
Baseline Padel provides balls for standard bookings unless otherwise stated at the time of reservation; players wishing to use their own brand are free to do so provided the balls meet standard padel specifications. Loan rackets are available at select branches on a first-come basis and must be returned in the same condition, with any damage beyond normal wear charged to the member's account. Players are asked not to use rackets to strike the court surface, walls, or fencing in frustration, as this is a leading cause of equipment and facility damage across all branches.

9. Weather Conditions at Outdoor Branches
Outdoor branches remain subject to prevailing weather, and courts may be closed temporarily during periods of strong wind, heavy rain, or extreme heat advisories issued by branch management for player safety. Where a session is interrupted or cancelled due to weather within the first fifteen minutes of play, members will be offered a rebooking credit rather than a partial refund. Members are encouraged to check the app or contact the branch ahead of a booking during unsettled weather periods, as courts may be closed with limited notice for safety reasons beyond the club's control.

10. Junior Players and Supervision Requirements
Players under the age of twelve must be accompanied by a parent, guardian, or registered coach at all times while on club premises, including in communal areas such as the café and viewing lounge. Junior-specific sessions run under qualified coaching supervision are exempt from this requirement during the scheduled programme itself, though guardians must remain contactable and on-site unless otherwise agreed with the coaching team in advance. Unsupervised minors found on court outside of a booked and supervised session will be asked to wait in the reception area until a guardian is located.

11. Food, Drink, and Court Cleanliness
Food and glass containers are not permitted on court at any branch; water in resealable bottles and standard sports drinks are the only beverages allowed courtside. Members are asked to dispose of wrappers, tape, and other litter in bins provided rather than leaving them courtside for staff to clear, as this affects turnover time for the next booking. Any spillage on court, particularly on outdoor artificial turf, should be reported immediately so staff can clean the area before it becomes a slip hazard for subsequent players.

12. Coaching, Private Sessions, and Court Sharing
Members wishing to bring an external coach onto Baseline Padel premises must register that coach with the branch in advance; unregistered coaching activity may be paused by staff pending verification. Court sharing between an in-house lesson and a separate booking is not permitted unless expressly agreed with the front desk, as this creates safety risks from overlapping play. Coaches, whether club-affiliated or external, are expected to model the same etiquette standards as members, and repeated disregard for these rules by a visiting coach may result in that individual being restricted from future bookings at any branch.

13. Escalation and Disciplinary Process
Minor first-time issues, such as footwear or attire concerns, are typically resolved informally by on-duty staff without further action. Repeated or more serious breaches, including damage to facilities, abusive conduct, or safety violations, will be logged against the member's account and reviewed by branch management, who may issue a formal written warning. A third substantiated incident within a rolling twelve-month period, or any single severe incident such as deliberate property damage or threatening behaviour, may result in suspension of membership privileges across all branches pending a review meeting. Members retain the right to present their account of events before any suspension is finalised.

14. Reporting Concerns and Facility Feedback
Any member who witnesses a breach of these rules, notices a facility fault, or has a general concern about court conditions is encouraged to raise it with the front desk at the time or via the club's member support channel within a reasonable period afterward. Feedback is reviewed on a rolling basis by branch management, and where a pattern emerges across multiple branches, it is escalated to the wider facilities team for a coordinated response. Baseline Padel views these rules as a living framework and reserves the right to update them periodically to reflect operational experience, with any material changes communicated to members in advance of taking effect.

title: Equipment Hire and Pro Shop
body:
1. Scope and Purpose
This policy governs the hire of padel racquets, balls, footwear, and ancillary equipment across all eight Baseline Padel branches, together with the operation of pro shop retail counters located at each site. It applies to members, walk-in guests, tournament entrants, and coaching clients alike, and is intended to ensure consistency of pricing, condition standards, and accountability regardless of which branch a booking is made at. Where a specific outdoor branch or indoor branch has a variation due to court surface or climate control, this is noted explicitly; otherwise all provisions apply uniformly across the group.

2. Racquet Hire Availability
Every branch maintains a rotating stock of demo and hire racquets spanning beginner, intermediate, and advanced profiles, sourced from a small number of approved equipment partners. Hire racquets are issued on a first-come basis at the front desk and cannot be reserved more than 24 hours in advance except for coaching blocks or academy sessions, where the coach may pre-select a racquet on the player's behalf. Outdoor branches typically carry a slightly larger hire fleet given higher walk-in volume during cooler months, while indoor branches rotate stock more frequently to manage wear from continuous climate-controlled play. Any player unable to find a suitable racquet in their preferred grip size should ask reception to check availability at a neighbouring branch, as informal transfers between nearby sites can sometimes be arranged same-day.

3. Hire Fees and Payment
Standard racquet hire is charged per session and billed to the member account or settled by card at the point of collection; cash is accepted at select branches only. Ball cans used during hire sessions are charged separately unless included in a package booking, and courts booked as part of a social or ladder match typically bundle one can per four players. Fees are reviewed periodically and any adjustment will be displayed at the front desk and on the booking app at least 14 days before it takes effect. Members holding an active monthly or annual plan may be entitled to discounted or complimentary hire depending on their tier, and staff will apply this automatically provided the membership is verified as current at check-in.

4. Condition Checks and Damage Liability
All hire racquets are inspected before and after each session by front desk staff, who log visible frame cracks, string tension loss, or grip wear using the standard equipment checklist. A hirer is liable for damage beyond normal wear, including cracked frames from mishits against walls or glass, provided the damage is identified at return and not already noted at issue. Where liability is disputed, the duty manager will review any available court camera footage before a charge is applied, and the hirer will be notified of the outcome within 48 hours. Deliberate misuse, such as using a racquet to strike the ball outside normal play or leaving equipment exposed to rain at outdoor branches, will result in full replacement cost being charged regardless of membership tier.

5. Ball Hire and Pressurisation Standards
Balls used for hire and retail are stored in pressurised cans and rotated on a defined shelf-life cycle to maintain bounce consistency, which is checked more rigorously at outdoor branches due to heat exposure affecting internal pressure. Opened cans used during a single session are not eligible for return or exchange, but an unopened can purchased in error may be exchanged within the same visit provided the seal is intact. Tournament and academy play uses a separate, higher-grade ball stock that is not available through standard hire, and any player wishing to purchase this grade for personal use should ask the pro shop team, as it is held in limited quantity per branch.

6. Footwear and Apparel Hire
A small number of branches offer padel shoe hire in common sizing to accommodate first-time players who arrive without appropriate footwear, though this service is not guaranteed at every location and should be confirmed by phone or app before travelling to a branch specifically for this reason. Hired footwear is sanitised between uses following the standard hygiene protocol, and any player with a known skin sensitivity should inform staff so that alternative arrangements, including a discounted retail purchase, can be offered instead. Apparel such as visors, wristbands, and gloves is available for retail purchase only and is not part of the hire fleet under any circumstance.

7. Pro Shop Retail Scope
Each branch operates a pro shop counter stocking racquets, balls, footwear, apparel, and accessories from the club's approved supplier range. Stock levels vary by branch size, with flagship branches carrying a fuller range including premium and limited-edition racquet lines, while smaller branches focus on essentials and fast-moving consumables. Members are encouraged to use the app to check indicative stock before travelling for a specific item, though live inventory cannot be guaranteed and a reserved item not collected within 48 hours of confirmation may be released back to general stock.

8. Returns, Exchanges, and Warranty Claims
Unused retail items in original packaging may be returned or exchanged within a set number of days from the date of purchase as printed on the receipt, provided proof of purchase is presented at any branch. Racquets carry a manufacturer warranty against structural frame defects, which Baseline Padel will facilitate on the customer's behalf by liaising with the relevant supplier, though this process may take several weeks and the customer will be updated periodically on progress. Wear and tear from normal play, including string fraying or grip degradation, is explicitly excluded from warranty and is instead addressed through the restringing and regripping service described below. Sale items and clearance stock are typically sold as final and this will be clearly stated at the point of purchase.

9. Restringing and Regripping Services
