Most branches offer an in-house or partner-facilitated restringing service, with turnaround typically ranging from same-day to a few working days depending on branch workload and whether the racquet is a common or specialist model. Customers are asked to specify their preferred string tension at the time of drop-off, and where no preference is given, staff will apply the standard house tension appropriate to the racquet's category. Regripping is generally a faster service and can often be completed while the customer waits during quieter periods. Any racquet left uncollected beyond 30 days from the date the service is completed will be logged as unclaimed property and handled under the club's general lost property procedure.

10. Personal Equipment Storage and Lockers
While not strictly part of hire or retail, many branches provide lockers for personal equipment storage during a session, and members are reminded that these are for same-day use only unless a long-term locker rental has been separately arranged. Baseline Padel does not accept liability for personal racquets, bags, or valuables left in communal areas or unlocked lockers, and members are strongly advised to use paid lockers where available, particularly at busier outdoor branches during peak evening hours.

11. Group Bookings and Tournament Equipment Allocation
For group bookings, corporate events, and internal tournaments, equipment is allocated in advance based on the numbers confirmed at the time of booking, and any late increase in participant numbers cannot be guaranteed additional hire stock on short notice. Tournament organisers should coordinate directly with the branch's events coordinator no less than seven days before the event to confirm racquet and ball quantities, particularly where a specific ball grade is required for sanctioned play. Any shortfall identified on the day will be addressed on a best-efforts basis, which may include sourcing spare stock from a nearby branch where feasible.

12. Staff Discretion and Escalation Path
Front desk and pro shop staff are authorised to resolve routine hire disputes, minor damage assessments, and standard exchanges without further approval. Matters involving disputed liability above a nominal threshold, suspected deliberate damage, or repeated equipment loss by the same individual should be escalated to the duty manager, who may involve the branch general manager for cases involving suspension of hire privileges. Any customer dissatisfied with a resolution at branch level may request a formal review through the central customer relations channel, which will respond within a stated service window and has final authority over goodwill gestures such as fee waivers or replacement credit.

13. Lost, Stolen, or Non-Returned Equipment
Hire equipment not returned by the end of the booked session is treated as overdue, and a grace period applies before additional charges accrue, after which the customer may be charged the full replacement value if the item is not returned within a reasonable window. Equipment reported stolen from a locker or court-side area should be reported to staff immediately so that an incident log can be raised, which may be required for any insurance claim the customer wishes to pursue independently, as Baseline Padel does not itself insure personal or hired items against theft.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in supplier arrangements, seasonal demand patterns between outdoor and indoor branches, and feedback gathered through member surveys and front desk incident logs. Any material change to hire fees, warranty handling, or damage liability terms will be communicated through the app and displayed at branch reception ahead of the change taking effect, and continued use of hire or pro shop services after that point constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.

title: Lockers, Changing Rooms and Showers
body:
1. Scope and Application
This policy governs the use of lockers, changing rooms and shower facilities at all branches of Baseline Padel, including both indoor and outdoor sites. It applies to members, pay-and-play guests, junior players attending academy sessions, and any accompanying visitors who make use of these facilities before, during or after a booked court session. Where a specific branch has additional local rules due to layout or capacity constraints, these will be displayed at the entrance to the changing area and will take precedence over general provisions where a direct conflict arises.

2. Locker Allocation and Duration of Use
Lockers are provided on a day-use basis and are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis unless a branch operates a reservation system linked to court bookings. Members should expect to vacate lockers within two hours of their session ending, and staff reserve the right to open any locker left in use beyond this window if the branch requires the space for incoming players. Season-long or monthly locker rental, where offered, is arranged separately through the front desk and is subject to availability, which varies by branch and by time of year due to differing footfall between the cooler months and warmer months.

3. Locks and Security of Belongings
Members are strongly encouraged to bring their own padlock or use a coin or card-operated lock where fitted. Baseline Padel does not provide locks as standard at every branch, and where locks are available for loan at reception, a small refundable deposit may be required. Under no circumstances should valuables such as passports, large sums of cash, or jewellery be left in changing areas, even inside a locked locker. Baseline Padel accepts no liability for loss, theft or damage to personal property left in lockers, changing rooms or shower areas, regardless of whether a lock was fitted or supplied by the club.

4. Overnight and Extended Storage
Lockers are not intended for overnight storage at any branch. Any item left in a locker after closing hours will be removed by duty staff, logged in the lost property register, and held in accordance with clause 9 below. Exceptions may be granted for competitive players participating in multi-day tournaments hosted at a branch, in which case a designated secure storage area will be arranged in advance through the events team rather than through standard locker facilities.

5. Changing Room Access and Conduct
Changing rooms are separated by gender at all branches, with a small number of branches also offering a unisex or family changing option for parents accompanying young children. Appropriate conduct is expected at all times, including reasonable noise levels, respect for the privacy of other users, and prompt vacating of shower cubicles and changing benches during busy periods. The use of changing rooms for filming, photography, or livestreaming of any kind is strictly prohibited, and any member found doing so may be asked to leave the premises and could face suspension of membership pending review.

6. Shower Facilities and Water Usage
Shower facilities are available at all branches, though the number of cubicles and operating hours may differ between larger flagship sites and smaller satellite locations. Members are asked to be mindful of water usage and to limit shower time to a reasonable duration during peak hours, particularly in the early evening when court bookings and changing room demand are typically at their highest. Outdoor branches, where showers may be partially exposed to the elements or fed by a separate water system, occasionally experience temporary reductions in water pressure or temperature during periods of high demand or scheduled maintenance; staff will post notices where disruption is expected to last beyond a single day.

7. Hygiene Standards and Cleaning Schedule
Changing rooms and shower areas are cleaned multiple times daily, with a deeper clean carried out outside of operating hours at every branch. Members are asked to dispose of used razors, plasters and other personal hygiene items in the bins provided rather than in sinks or shower drains, as this causes blockages that can take facilities out of service for extended periods. Any member who notices a hygiene issue, blocked drain, or malfunctioning fixture is asked to report it to reception immediately rather than to a member of coaching staff, so that it can be logged and actioned by the correct maintenance channel.

8. Towels and Amenities
Towel hire is available at reception at most branches for a nominal fee, and members holding certain premium membership tiers may receive complimentary towel service as part of their package benefits. Fresh towels should be collected before entering the changing area, and used towels must be returned to the designated bins near the changing room exit rather than left on benches or hooks. Branches may also stock basic amenities such as shower gel or hairdryers, though the range and availability of these extras is not guaranteed and should not be relied upon in place of bringing personal toiletries.

9. Lost Property
Any item found within lockers, changing rooms or shower areas is logged by duty staff and held at the branch reception for a period of thirty days from the date it was found. Members who believe they have left an item behind should contact the branch directly, providing a reasonable description, rather than visiting in person to search unattended, as staff are not permitted to allow members into the lost property store without supervision. Items of significant value, such as electronic devices or jewellery, may be held for a longer period at the discretion of branch management, while low-value items such as single socks or toiletries are typically disposed of or donated after the standard holding period if unclaimed.

10. Access Hours and Out-of-Hours Restrictions
Changing rooms and showers follow the same operating hours as the branch itself and cannot be accessed outside these times, even by members holding a court booking that begins shortly after opening or ends shortly before closing. Members arriving very close to closing time should be aware that staff may reasonably ask them to expedite their use of the facilities so that the branch can complete its closing procedures on schedule. Requests for extended access due to tournaments, private events or coaching clinics must be arranged in advance with branch management and are not guaranteed as a standard courtesy.

11. Children, Families and Supervision
Children under a certain age, as specified locally at each branch, must be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times while using changing rooms and shower facilities, including in family or unisex changing areas where available. Parents are responsible for supervising their children's belongings and conduct throughout, and staff are not able to assume responsibility for unaccompanied minors in these areas under any circumstances. Academy sessions for junior players typically include a short supervised changing window immediately before and after coaching, coordinated by academy staff rather than general reception.

12. Accessibility Provisions
All branches provide at least one accessible changing space and shower cubicle designed to accommodate members with mobility requirements, though the specific layout and equipment may vary between indoor and outdoor sites due to differences in building structure. Members who require additional support, such as assistance with equipment or advance notice of accessible facility availability, are encouraged to contact the branch ahead of their visit so that appropriate arrangements can be confirmed. Any accessibility concern that cannot be resolved at branch level should be escalated to the regional facilities team through member services.

13. Maintenance, Closures and Temporary Restrictions
From time to time, part or all of a changing room or shower area may be closed for essential maintenance, refurbishment, or repair following a reported fault. Where such closure is expected to last longer than a single day, the branch will display advance notice at reception and, where practical, provide details of alternative facilities within the same branch or a nearby branch. Members inconvenienced by an unplanned closure during their visit may request a short-notice adjustment to their booking or a facility credit through reception, subject to review by duty management.

14. Complaints and Escalation
Any concern relating to cleanliness, security, staff conduct, or the general condition of lockers, changing rooms or showers should first be raised with the duty manager on site, who is able to resolve most issues directly or arrange an immediate remedy. Where a member feels the matter has not been satisfactorily addressed at branch level, or where the concern relates to a pattern of recurring issues, the matter should be escalated in writing to member services, who will investigate and respond within a reasonable timeframe. Baseline Padel treats all facilities-related feedback seriously and uses it to inform the ongoing maintenance and improvement schedule across all branches.

title: Parking and Site Access
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs vehicle parking, pedestrian access, and general site movement across all eight branches of Baseline Padel. It applies to members, pay-and-play guests, coaching clients, spectators, delivery contractors, and staff. Where a specific branch has structural limitations that require a variation from this policy, such variations will be posted at reception and at the relevant access point, and will be treated as an addendum rather than a replacement to the clauses below. Members are expected to familiarise themselves with the layout of any branch they visit, particularly where that branch differs from their home club in terms of gated access, level changes, or shared-use arrangements with neighbouring facilities.

2. Parking Allocation and General Use
Parking bays at all branches are provided on a first-come, first-served basis unless a bay has been explicitly reserved under clause 4 or clause 7. No member or guest holds a permanent right to a specific bay, regardless of membership tier, tenure, or frequency of visit. Vehicles must be parked wholly within marked bay lines, and any vehicle that occupies more than one bay, blocks a fire route, or obstructs a shared access lane may be reported to site management and, where necessary, to the relevant municipal authority for removal. Baseline Padel does not guarantee the availability of parking at any given time and recommends arriving with sufficient margin before a booked court time, particularly during peak evening hours or during organised events.

3. Outdoor Branch Considerations
At outdoor branches, parking areas are generally uncovered and subject to prevailing weather conditions. Members should take reasonable precautions with vehicles during periods of high wind or sand exposure, including securing loose items and, where practical, avoiding leaving vehicles beneath overhead netting or lighting rigs for extended periods. Baseline Padel is not responsible for damage arising from environmental conditions in outdoor parking areas, including but not limited to sand accumulation, surface heat damage to tyres left stationary for long durations, or debris carried by wind. Where an outdoor branch experiences temporary closure of its car park due to maintenance or resurfacing, alternative overflow arrangements will be communicated in advance where possible via the branch noticeboard or booking app.

4. Accessible Parking
Each branch maintains a minimum of two designated accessible bays positioned nearest to the main entrance or lift access point. These bays are reserved exclusively for vehicles displaying a valid accessibility permit and must not be used for short-term loading, coaching drop-off, or overflow parking under any circumstance. Any member requiring temporary accessible parking due to injury or short-term mobility limitation should speak to branch reception, who can issue a temporary dashboard notice valid for a period specified at the time of issue. Misuse of accessible bays by unauthorised vehicles will result in a written warning in the first instance and may affect continued access privileges on repeat occurrence.

5. Loading, Drop-Off, and Short-Stay Zones
Where a branch has a marked loading or drop-off zone, this area is intended for stays of no longer than ten minutes and must not be used for full-session parking. These zones exist primarily to support families dropping off junior players for academy sessions, deliveries to the pro shop or café, and short equipment collection. Vehicles left unattended in a drop-off zone beyond the permitted window may be asked to relocate by staff, and repeated disregard for this request may result in the vehicle being reported to site security or, at larger branches with shared commercial parking, to the managing landlord's enforcement contractor.

6. Motorcycles, Bicycles, and Micro-Mobility
Motorcycle parking is available at designated bays at most branches and is clearly marked with appropriate signage; motorcycles should not be parked within standard vehicle bays or along pedestrian walkways. Bicycle racks are provided at the majority of branches near the main entrance, and cyclists are asked to use these racks rather than securing bicycles to railings, glass balustrades, or court fencing. Personal micro-mobility devices such as scooters or e-boards may be brought on site but must be stored in designated racks during play and are not permitted inside court areas, viewing galleries, or the café seating zone.

7. Coaching, Academy, and Event Parking
During academy sessions, junior clinics, or organised tournaments, a portion of the car park may be temporarily reserved for coaching staff, event officials, or participating teams. Such reservations will be signposted at least the day before where feasible, and standard members are asked to respect temporary cones or signage even where a bay appears empty. Any member inconvenienced by event-related parking changes should raise this with branch reception, who can advise on nearby overflow parking or alternative branch options for that day. Persistent disregard for event signage may result in a vehicle being relocated at the owner's risk by on-site staff.

8. Multi-Use and Shared-Site Branches
Certain branches operate within a larger shared development, such as a community centre, hotel complex, or mixed-use retail site, and parking at these locations may be governed jointly by Baseline Padel and the site landlord. In these cases, members must observe both this policy and any posted landlord rules, including time-limited parking, validation requirements, or barrier-controlled entry. Baseline Padel will make reasonable efforts to arrange parking validation for members at shared sites where this service exists, but cannot be held responsible for landlord-imposed penalty charges arising from a member's failure to validate or from overstaying a landlord-imposed limit.

9. Site Access Hours and Out-of-Hours Entry
General site access follows the operating hours displayed at each branch, which may vary between weekdays, weekends, and the cooler or warmer parts of the year. Members with a booking that begins close to opening time or ends close to closing time should not assume early entry or late exit is guaranteed; access outside posted hours is at the discretion of on-duty staff and is not a standing entitlement. Where a branch offers extended-hours access via key fob or app-based entry for eligible membership tiers, this access is personal to the member, must not be shared or lent, and may be suspended immediately if used to admit unregistered guests outside supervised hours.

10. Security, CCTV, and Vehicle Liability
All branch car parks are monitored by CCTV for the safety of members and staff, and footage may be reviewed in the event of an incident, dispute, or reported theft. Baseline Padel does not accept liability for damage, theft, or loss of personal property from any vehicle parked on site, and members are encouraged to remove valuables and ensure vehicles are locked. Any incident involving damage to a vehicle while on Baseline Padel premises should be reported to reception within 24 hours so that CCTV footage can be reviewed before routine overwrite; delayed reporting may limit the club's ability to assist with any subsequent investigation or insurance claim.

11. Pedestrian Routes and Court-Side Access
Pedestrian access from the car park to the courts is via marked walkways only, and members should avoid cutting across live court areas, ball-collection zones, or maintenance access paths, particularly during active play on adjacent courts. At branches with elevated or terraced court layouts, handrails are provided on all stairways and should be used at all times, especially when carrying equipment bags or during periods of wet flooring following cleaning or rainfall. Children accompanying adult members must remain under direct supervision while moving between the car park and the court area, and should not be permitted to run ahead unsupervised through shared vehicle routes.

12. Deliveries, Contractors, and Service Vehicles
Delivery and contractor vehicles are asked to use designated service access points where these exist, rather than the main member car park, in order to reduce congestion during peak hours. Any contractor requiring extended access for maintenance work, resurfacing, or equipment installation must coordinate timing with branch management in advance, and such work will typically be scheduled outside of peak playing hours where practical. Members are asked to give way to marked service vehicles within shared access lanes and to avoid parking in a manner that blocks loading bay access, even temporarily.

13. Non-Compliance and Escalation
Where a member or guest is found to be in repeated or serious breach of this policy, including persistent misuse of accessible bays, disregard for event signage, or unauthorised sharing of out-of-hours access credentials, branch management may issue a formal written notice outlining the specific breach and any corrective action required. Continued non-compliance following a written notice may result in suspension of parking privileges at that branch, and in serious cases, referral to Baseline Padel's central membership team for a wider review of the member's account standing. Members who believe a parking-related decision has been applied incorrectly may request a review by submitting details to branch management within 14 days of the incident, and a response will typically be provided within 10 business days.

14. Policy Review and Local Variations
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in branch layout, landlord arrangements at shared sites, or operational learning from incident reports. Any local variation implemented at a specific branch will be clearly signposted at that branch's main entrance and referenced on the branch's page within the booking app. Members with questions about parking or access arrangements at a branch they do not regularly attend are encouraged to contact that branch directly ahead of their visit, particularly if travelling with a vehicle requiring accessible parking, towing a trailer, or arriving outside standard operating hours.

title: Cafe, Food and Drink on Court
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how food, drink and cafe services operate across all eight Baseline Padel branches, including the specific rules that apply to consumption on or around the court surface itself. It applies to members, pay-and-play guests, coaching clients, spectators and anyone attending a private event on site. The intention is to protect the playing surface, reduce injury risk from spillages, maintain a pleasant environment for all users, and give clarity to cafe staff and duty managers on what is and is not permitted. Where a specific branch has additional local rules, for example due to a smaller court-side seating area or a shared outdoor terrace, those local rules will be displayed at reception and will supplement, not override, this policy.

2. General Principle on Court Surfaces
No food or drink other than water in a sealed or resealable container is permitted on the actual playing surface at any time, including during warm-up, coaching sessions, casual matches, tournaments and exhibition play. This applies regardless of whether the court is indoor, outdoor, air-conditioned or open-air. The rule exists primarily to protect the artificial turf and glass surrounds from staining, stickiness and slip hazards, all of which shorten the lifespan of the court and create a genuine risk of injury during fast lateral movement. Coaches and duty managers are authorised to pause a session and ask players to remove any non-water item from the court immediately.

3. Water and Approved Hydration
Still water in the club-branded reusable bottle, a personal sports bottle with a secure lid, or a sealed bottle purchased from the cafe is always welcome courtside and on the bench areas immediately adjacent to the court. Electrolyte tablets and powders may be added to personal bottles. Sports drinks in their original sealed packaging are permitted in bench areas but should be finished or removed before re-entering play, since sugary residue on grips and surfaces is a recurring source of complaints from the following booking. Reception can advise on refill points, which are available at all branches and are the preferred option for members looking to reduce single-use plastic.

4. Snacks and Light Food Around the Court
Light snacks such as energy bars, fruit and pre-match nutrition are permitted in the designated bench or seating area beside the court, but not on the court itself, and players are asked to clear wrappers and peel before their next game begins. Hot food, strong-smelling dishes and anything requiring cutlery is not permitted courtside under any circumstance, including at outdoor branches where seating is close to the court fencing. This is partly a courtesy issue, since the smell of hot food can be distracting to players on neighbouring courts, and partly a cleanliness issue, given the proximity of shared equipment such as ball baskets and rebound nets. Members wishing to eat a full meal before or after their session are directed to the cafe seating or terrace area provided at every branch.

5. Cafe Service Hours and Ordering
Each branch operates a cafe counter with service hours aligned to the club's opening times, though last orders for hot food typically fall earlier than the club's closing time to allow for kitchen wind-down. Members can order at the counter, through the club app where table service is available, or via a court-side scan code at branches that have installed one. Orders placed through the app during a live booking are delivered to the cafe collection point or, at select branches with waiter service, brought directly to the seating area adjoining the courts. Any delay in preparation during peak evening hours will be communicated by cafe staff, and members are welcome to check estimated wait times at the counter rather than assuming an order has been missed.

6. Alcohol Service and Restrictions
Where a branch holds the relevant licence to serve alcohol, service is restricted to the cafe and terrace areas and is never permitted courtside, in the bench area, or within the fenced playing zone under any circumstance. Alcohol service hours follow local regulatory requirements and may vary by branch and by time of year; current hours are posted at the cafe counter and on the app. Coaches, duty managers and reception staff reserve the right to decline service to any player scheduled to return to court, and to refuse further service to anyone who appears to be intoxicated, regardless of membership tier. Players who have consumed alcohol are asked to allow a reasonable interval before resuming play, both for their own safety and out of consideration for opponents.

7. Private Events and Catered Bookings
Members hosting a private event, corporate booking or celebration may arrange catering through the branch's events coordinator, who can advise on approved caterers, setup areas and timing. Catered food for private events is confined to designated function space, terraces or private lounges and is not brought onto adjoining courts, even if those courts have been reserved as part of the same booking. Any request to bring an external cake, dessert or celebratory item is generally accommodated with advance notice, though the cafe kitchen reserves the right to decline last-minute requests that could not reasonably be prepared or plated safely on short notice. A cleaning fee may apply if catering spills or residue extend beyond the agreed function area.

8. Children, Family Areas and Spillage Risk
Family and junior sessions often bring younger children courtside, and parents are asked to keep snacks and drinks for children within the designated family seating rather than the bench area directly beside active play. Spilled food or drink near a court should be reported to staff immediately rather than left for the next group to discover, since a delay increases both slip risk and the chance of permanent staining on artificial turf. Baseline Padel provides spill kits at each reception desk and duty managers are trained to respond within minutes of a report. Parents remain responsible for supervising children's food and drink at all times; cafe and coaching staff are not responsible for monitoring what a child brings courtside.

9. Personal Coolers, Outside Food and Deliveries
Members may bring personal cooler bags containing their own food and drink for consumption in general seating areas, though these items are subject to the same courtside restrictions as cafe-bought items and must not be taken onto the court. Third-party food delivery is accepted at reception during standard hours at most branches, though outdoor branches with limited indoor waiting space may ask couriers to leave orders at a designated collection point rather than entering the facility. Baseline Padel does not accept liability for delivery orders left unattended at a collection point beyond a reasonable holding period, typically indicated on a sign near reception. Members are encouraged to time deliveries around their session rather than mid-match, both for their own convenience and to avoid congestion at the entrance.

10. Dietary Requirements and Allergen Information
Allergen information for all cafe menu items is available on request at the counter and is also listed within the app's cafe ordering section. Members with a known allergy are encouraged to inform cafe staff directly when ordering rather than relying solely on printed information, since recipes and suppliers can change between seasons. While every reasonable precaution is taken to avoid cross-contamination, the cafe kitchens are not certified allergen-free environments and members with severe allergies should exercise their own judgement accordingly. Special dietary requests for private events, including vegetarian, vegan or specific cultural requirements, can usually be accommodated with a minimum of a few days' notice through the events coordinator.

11. Cleanliness, Waste and Court Handover
All bench areas, seating and terraces must be left reasonably tidy at the end of a booking to allow smooth handover to the next group. Cafe staff conduct periodic sweeps of court-side areas throughout the day, but the primary responsibility for clearing personal rubbish rests with the player or booking holder. Recycling and general waste points are clearly marked at every branch, and members are asked to separate items where facilities allow. Persistent failure to clear food or drink waste from a booked court, particularly where it results in a delay to the following group, may be noted on the member's account and referenced if the issue recurs.

12. Staff Authority and On-the-Spot Decisions
Duty managers, coaches and cafe supervisors are authorised to make immediate, reasonable decisions to enforce this policy, including asking a player to remove an item from the court, pausing a session briefly for a spill to be cleared, or declining to serve an item that poses a particular risk given the day's conditions, such as very hot weather affecting melting or spoilage. These on-the-spot decisions are made in good faith to protect the surface, other players and the wider club environment, and are not intended as a personal judgement on any individual member. Members who disagree with a specific decision are welcome to raise it calmly with the duty manager at the time, or to follow the escalation route described below if they feel the matter warrants further review.

13. Exceptions and Special Circumstances
Occasional exceptions may be granted for medical reasons, such as a player needing a specific food item at a specific time due to a health condition; these should be flagged to reception in advance where possible so that appropriate arrangements, such as a permitted item stored safely near the bench, can be agreed with the duty manager. Tournament organisers running sanctioned events may request temporary adjustments to standard cafe or seating arrangements, such as extended hydration station access, and these requests are handled case by case through the branch events team rather than under the standard walk-in policy. Any exception granted at one branch does not automatically apply at another, given differences in court layout, seating proximity and local licensing conditions.

14. Feedback and Escalation
Members wishing to give feedback on cafe service, raise a concern about how this policy was applied, or report a repeated issue such as recurring spillage on a particular court are asked to contact the branch duty manager in the first instance, either in person or through the app's support channel. If the matter is not resolved to the member's satisfaction, it can be escalated to the regional facilities team, who aim to respond within a few working days. Baseline Padel reviews this policy periodically to reflect changes in court surfacing, licensing conditions and member feedback, and any material update will be communicated through the app and displayed at reception ahead of taking effect.

title: General Safety and Emergency Procedures
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out the general safety and emergency procedures applicable across all branches of Baseline Padel, including both indoor and outdoor courts, reception and lounge areas, changing facilities, car parks, and any adjoining walkways under club management. It applies to members, guests, casual bookers, coaching staff, contractors, and visiting spectators. Individual branches may issue supplementary guidance to reflect local layout, climate exposure, or building configuration, but no branch-level notice may reduce the protections or reporting obligations described here. Where a conflict exists between local signage and this document, the more cautious instruction takes precedence until club management resolves the discrepancy.

2. Duty Manager Authority
Every operating shift at every branch has a designated duty manager whose authority on safety matters is final during that shift, overriding coaching staff, front-of-house staff, and any verbal arrangement made by booking or membership teams. The duty manager may suspend play on any court, close any part of a facility, or refuse entry to any individual where they judge there to be a credible risk to health or safety, and no refund dispute or scheduling inconvenience shall be grounds to challenge that judgement in the moment. Members and guests are expected to comply immediately with directions from a duty manager or any staff member acting on their behalf, with formal complaints or appeals to be raised afterwards through normal customer channels rather than contested on site.

3. Reporting an Incident
Any injury, near-miss, equipment failure, or safety concern must be reported to reception or the duty manager as soon as practicable, and in any case before the person involved leaves the branch, unless emergency circumstances require immediate departure to seek medical care. Staff will complete an incident log capturing time, location, persons involved, and any first aid or intervention provided, and a copy or reference number will be offered to the reporting party on request. Failure to report at the time does not prevent a later claim being considered, but delayed reporting may make it harder for the club to investigate fully, and this will be taken into account in good faith when reviewing any subsequent complaint.

4. First Aid Provision
All branches maintain at least one trained first aider on site during operating hours, and larger branches with multiple simultaneous bookings maintain more than one across peak periods. First aid kits are located at reception and at a marked point courtside, and their location is signed in the immediate vicinity of every court. Staff administering first aid will do so only to the level of their training and will not attempt procedures beyond that level; where an injury appears to exceed basic first aid capability, staff are instructed to call for emergency medical services without delay rather than attempt improvised treatment. Any member or guest with a known medical condition that could require urgent intervention during play, including but not limited to cardiac conditions, severe allergies, or epilepsy, is strongly encouraged to inform reception confidentially at check-in so that staff can respond appropriately if needed.

5. Emergency Contacts and Escalation
Each branch displays local emergency service numbers and the direct line for the duty manager at reception, in changing areas, and courtside. Staff are trained to call external emergency services directly for any incident judged serious, rather than routing through head office first, and to notify club management only once emergency responders are engaged or the immediate situation is stabilised. For incidents involving a minor, staff will attempt to contact the registered guardian or emergency contact on file immediately, and where that contact cannot be reached within a reasonable period, the duty manager will make welfare decisions in the child's best interest until a guardian is reached.

6. Heat and Weather Precautions at Outdoor Branches
Outdoor branches are subject to additional precautions given the region's climate, and courts may be closed or bookings shortened at the duty manager's discretion during periods of extreme heat, high humidity, or poor air quality, irrespective of any advance booking. Water stations at outdoor branches are checked and refilled throughout the day, and staff are authorised to pause play for hydration breaks during longer sessions without needing prior member consent. Members are advised to seek indoor courts, where available at their home branch or a nearby branch, during the hottest parts of the year, and the club accepts no liability for heat-related discomfort where reasonable precautions and warnings have been provided and a member has chosen to proceed with play against staff advice.

7. Severe Weather and Site Closure
In the event of severe weather such as electrical storms, high winds, or sandstorms, all outdoor courts will be closed immediately and players instructed to move to designated indoor or sheltered areas without exception. Indoor branches may also suspend operations where severe weather affects safe travel to and from the site or where building systems such as power or climate control are compromised. Where a closure occurs with less than two hours' notice, affected bookings will be rebooked or credited according to the club's standard cancellation policy, and members will be notified through the booking app or by direct message as soon as the closure decision is made.

8. Fire Safety and Evacuation
All branches maintain marked fire exits, assembly points, and extinguishing equipment in accordance with facility design, and these are checked on a routine schedule by site management. In the event of a fire alarm, staff will direct all persons to the nearest marked exit and onward to the assembly point, and no personal belongings, including car keys or valuables left in lockers, should be retrieved during an evacuation. Staff conduct a headcount against sign-in and booking records once at the assembly point, and the duty manager retains responsibility for confirming with emergency services that the building is clear before anyone is permitted to re-enter.

9. Equipment and Court Surface Hazards
Members and guests must not use courts, nets, or fixed equipment that appear damaged, and should report any defect, including torn netting, loose glass panels, uneven surface patches, or faulty lighting, to staff immediately rather than continuing play. Staff will close the affected court pending inspection and, where necessary, arrange repair before the court is returned to the booking schedule. The club periodically inspects surfaces and fixtures across all branches on a rolling basis, but relies on prompt reporting from users as an essential part of maintaining safety between scheduled inspections, and no liability is accepted for hazards that were not reported despite being reasonably observable to the player.

10. Coaching Sessions and Group Safety
During coaching sessions, group clinics, or junior programmes, the assigned coach holds primary responsibility for the immediate safety of participants on court, including pacing of drills, ball feed control, and appropriate supervision of junior players at all times. Coaches are required to pause or end a session where weather, participant fatigue, or equipment issues create unacceptable risk, and this decision is not subject to override by parents, guardians, or participants in the moment. Any injury occurring during a coached session follows the same reporting obligations set out in clause 3, with the coach responsible for initiating that report before the session is considered formally closed.

11. Restricted Access and Behaviour
Access to plant rooms, maintenance areas, staff-only corridors, and rooftop or external mechanical zones is prohibited to members, guests, and visiting spectators at all branches, and any breach may result in immediate removal from the premises and suspension of membership pending review. Running, climbing on court dividers or netting, or using court equipment for purposes other than play is not permitted, and staff are authorised to intervene and stop such behaviour regardless of whether an incident has yet occurred, on the basis of preventing foreseeable harm.

12. Alcohol, Medical Fitness, and Fitness to Play
Members and guests who appear to be under the influence of alcohol or otherwise medically unfit to play, whether due to visible injury, illness, or evident impairment, may be refused court access by the duty manager, and this decision is final for that visit regardless of any prior booking confirmation. Where a person insists on proceeding to play against staff advice and subsequently sustains injury, the incident will still be logged and first aid provided as normal, but the club reserves the right to consider the individual's disregard of staff advice when responding to any later claim.

13. Data and Privacy During Incident Handling
Information collected during an incident, including names, contact details, and any medical information volunteered, is used solely for the purposes of managing the incident, informing emergency services or guardians where relevant, and maintaining internal safety records, and is handled in line with the club's separate data protection policy. Incident logs may be retained for a period sufficient to satisfy insurance, regulatory, or legal requirements, and members may request a copy of any log entry naming them by contacting the branch or the central member services team.

14. Policy Review and Local Variation
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect operational learning, regulatory updates, and changes to facilities across the group, and the version displayed at each branch and within the booking app should be treated as current. Where a branch introduces temporary local variations, such as during renovation works or seasonal closures of specific courts, these will be communicated through on-site signage and app notifications, and this general policy remains in force for all matters not explicitly addressed by the temporary variation.

title: Injury, First Aid and Medical Incidents
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel manages injuries, first aid provision and medical incidents across all branches, including both indoor and outdoor courts, coaching sessions, academy programmes and social play. It applies to members, guest players, junior participants, coaching staff and any visiting spectators present on site. The intention is to ensure a consistent standard of care regardless of which branch a person is using, while recognising that outdoor branches carry additional exposure to heat and weather-related conditions that require specific handling described later in this document.

2. First Aid Provision and Trained Personnel
Every branch maintains at least one member of staff trained in basic first aid during all opening hours, and larger branches with multiple court clusters maintain trained personnel on each level or wing of the facility. First aid kits are located at the reception desk, within the coaches' office, and at a fixed point near the court corridors, all clearly signed. Staff carrying out first aid duties are not required to hold advanced medical qualifications and will always seek to escalate to professional emergency services where an injury exceeds minor cuts, sprains or bruising. Members should not assume that any staff member present is a qualified paramedic; first aid on site is a bridging measure, not a substitute for professional medical treatment.

3. Reporting an Incident
Any injury occurring on Baseline Padel premises, however minor it may appear at the time, must be reported to a staff member before the injured person leaves the branch. This applies equally to injuries sustained during organised coaching, casual bookings, tournaments and social events. Staff will complete an incident log noting the time, location, nature of the injury, any treatment given, and the names of witnesses where available. Failure to report an incident at the time may limit the club's ability to assist with any subsequent insurance claim or medical follow-up, as there will be no contemporaneous record to support the account given later.

4. Minor Injuries and On-Site Treatment
Minor injuries such as small cuts, grazes, bruising, muscle strain or blisters will typically be treated on site using the first aid kit, with the injured party free to continue or withdraw from play at their own discretion once basic treatment has been given. Staff will offer a reasonable seating area away from active courts for anyone needing to rest before deciding whether to continue their session. Where an injury appears more significant than first assessed, staff reserve the right to recommend the player stop play immediately, and this recommendation should be treated seriously even where the player feels able to continue.

5. Serious Injuries and Emergency Response
Where an injury is judged serious, meaning suspected fracture, head injury, loss of consciousness, breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe bleeding or any incident causing visible distress beyond what basic first aid can address, staff will contact emergency medical services without delay. Play on the affected court and adjacent courts will be paused where necessary to allow safe access for responders. A designated staff member will remain with the injured person until professional help arrives or until the person is handed into the care of a companion, and another staff member will manage communication with emergency services and any necessary access arrangements at the entrance.

6. Head Injuries and Suspected Concussion
Any blow to the head, whether from a ball, racket, fall or collision with the glass surround, is treated with particular caution regardless of how minor the impact appears. The affected player will be removed from play and monitored for a minimum period before any decision is made about resuming activity that day. Where there is any loss of consciousness, confusion, vomiting, or persistent headache, staff will strongly advise the player seek immediate medical assessment and will not permit the player to resume play on the same visit. Coaches running academy or junior sessions apply an even more conservative approach, and any junior player suspected of a head injury will not return to court that day under any circumstances, with parents or guardians contacted directly.

7. Outdoor Branch Heat and Weather Considerations
Outdoor branches carry additional risk during periods of high heat and humidity, and staff at these branches are trained to recognise signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke including dizziness, nausea, confusion, cramping and reduced sweating. During particularly warm periods, outdoor branches may post advisory notices recommending shorter session lengths, increased hydration breaks, or rescheduling of midday bookings, though the final decision to play rests with the member unless conditions are judged to present an immediate safety risk, in which case staff may pause outdoor courts entirely until conditions improve. Members with known sensitivity to heat, including certain cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, are encouraged to disclose this informally to staff so that appropriate monitoring can be offered during their session.

8. Pre-Existing Medical Conditions
Baseline Padel does not require members to disclose pre-existing medical conditions as a condition of booking, but strongly encourages anyone with a relevant condition, such as a heart condition, severe allergy, epilepsy or asthma, to inform staff at the time of booking or upon arrival so that this information can be noted and made available to first aid staff in the event of an incident. This disclosure is entirely voluntary and stored only for safety purposes; it is not shared beyond the branch team and coaching staff directly involved in a session. Where a member chooses not to disclose a known condition, Baseline Padel's ability to respond appropriately in an emergency may be limited, and this should be understood as a shared responsibility between the club and the individual.

9. Medical Clearance After Significant Injury
Where a member has sustained a significant injury on site, whether requiring hospital treatment or extended rest, Baseline Padel may request written medical clearance before permitting the member to resume high-intensity coaching programmes or competitive league fixtures, primarily to protect the member from re-injury rather than to create unnecessary administrative burden. This requirement is applied at the discretion of branch management and is more commonly enforced within academy and junior programmes than for casual social bookings, given the structured and progressive nature of those sessions.

10. Third Party and Spectator Injuries
Spectators, family members and other visitors present at a branch but not actively playing are also covered by this policy in the event of an injury, such as a slip on a wet floor or an accidental collision near the court surrounds. The same reporting and incident logging procedures apply, and staff will offer first aid assistance regardless of whether the injured person is a paying member. Where a spectator injury arises from a hazard within the club's control, such as a maintenance issue, this will be recorded separately for facilities review, addressed further in the club's general liability documentation rather than this policy.

11. Coaching Staff Responsibilities During Sessions
Coaches running group or private sessions are responsible for pausing a session immediately upon any injury within their group, assessing the situation, and either administering basic first aid themselves if trained to do so or summoning reception staff without delay. Coaches are expected to use reasonable judgement in modifying drills or session intensity where a participant appears to be struggling physically, particularly in junior sessions where players may be reluctant to report discomfort themselves. Any injury occurring during a private lesson is documented by the coach in addition to standard reception reporting, given the more direct duty of supervision involved.

12. Insurance and Liability Limitations
Baseline Padel maintains public liability cover appropriate to its operations, but this policy document does not constitute a guarantee of compensation for any injury sustained on site. Members participating in physical activity do so with an inherent acknowledgement of the risks involved in a fast-paced racket sport, including collisions, falls and impact from balls or equipment. Any claim arising from an incident will be assessed on its individual facts, and members are encouraged to hold their own personal accident or health insurance appropriate to their level of play, particularly those participating in competitive leagues or high-intensity coaching programmes.

13. Escalation and Management Review
Any incident resulting in emergency service attendance, hospital admission, or a formal complaint regarding the standard of care provided will be escalated to senior management for review, typically within a short window following the incident. This review considers whether the response followed established procedure, whether any facility or process issue contributed to the incident, and whether any changes to staffing, signage or session structure are warranted. Members involved in a significant incident may be contacted afterwards, not to reopen the incident unnecessarily, but to confirm recovery and address any outstanding questions about what occurred.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in facility layout, staffing arrangements, or guidance from relevant health and safety bodies, and may be amended without prior notice where such changes are required for member safety. The most current version is available at any branch reception and applies in full at the time of any incident, superseding any earlier version regardless of when a member last read it.

title: Heat, Humidity and Outdoor Play
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel manages the risks associated with heat and humidity for members, guests, coaching staff and tournament participants across all outdoor branches. It applies to every outdoor court, whether fully exposed or partially shaded, and operates alongside our general court safety rules and our coaching code of conduct. Indoor and fully air-conditioned courts, where these exist within a branch, are not subject to the suspension thresholds described below, though staff are still expected to encourage sensible hydration practices year-round.

2. Monitoring Responsibility
Each branch designates a duty manager on every shift who is responsible for monitoring ambient temperature, humidity and any heat advisories issued by relevant local authorities. Monitoring is carried out using centrally provided digital readings supplemented by on-site instruments where installed. Duty managers log conditions at the start of each shift and again at any point where conditions appear to be deteriorating, particularly during the warmer months when readings can shift markedly within a single afternoon.

3. Temperature and Heat Index Thresholds
Outdoor play is subject to review once ambient temperature combined with humidity produces a heat index at or above the threshold set out in our internal operations manual, currently aligned with recognised regional guidance for outdoor exertion. Once this threshold is reached, the duty manager must assess whether play should continue with modified conditions, be limited to shorter sessions with mandatory breaks, or be suspended entirely. This is a judgement call informed by wind conditions, shade coverage, time of day and the physical exertion level of the activity taking place, not a purely mechanical reading of a single number.

4. Suspension of Outdoor Play
Where conditions are judged to present a genuine risk of heat-related illness, the duty manager has full authority to suspend outdoor bookings at that branch with immediate effect, regardless of prior confirmations or coaching schedules. Members affected by a suspension will be notified through the booking app and by on-site signage, and will automatically be offered a choice between rebooking at no charge, transferring to an indoor court where available at the same branch or a neighbouring branch, or receiving credit to their account. Suspensions are never treated as a cancellation attributable to the member and carry no penalty of any kind.

5. Peak Hours Guidance
During the warmer months, all outdoor branches operate under a standing peak hours guidance that discourages competitive or high-intensity play during the middle part of the day. Branches may choose to close outdoor courts entirely during this window, reduce court allocation to allow for extended recovery time between bookings, or restrict play to coached sessions with a qualified instructor present who can supervise pacing and hydration. Members wishing to play during restricted hours should check the app for branch-specific guidance, as approaches vary depending on court orientation and shade availability.

6. Coaching Sessions and Academy Programmes
Coaches are required to adjust session intensity in line with prevailing conditions and to build in additional water breaks beyond the standard schedule whenever the heat index approaches the review threshold. For junior academy sessions, coaches apply a more conservative standard than for adult sessions, given the reduced ability of children to regulate body temperature effectively, and will shorten or split sessions accordingly. Parents and guardians will be informed in advance where a scheduled academy session is likely to be shortened or moved indoors, and any resulting partial refund or credit is handled automatically without a formal request being necessary.

7. Tournaments and Organised Events
Tournament organisers must submit a heat contingency plan as part of any event proposal for an outdoor branch, covering rescheduled start times, additional shaded rest areas, extended change-of-ends breaks and an on-site first aider briefed specifically on heat-related symptoms. Where conditions on the day exceed the threshold described in clause 3, the tournament director has authority to delay matches, reduce match format, or move fixtures to an indoor court at the same or a nearby branch, even where this affects broadcast, sponsor or spectator arrangements. Player welfare takes precedence over the completion schedule in every case.

8. Member Responsibilities
Members and guests are expected to exercise personal judgement about their own fitness to play in prevailing conditions, particularly if they have underlying cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, are unaccustomed to outdoor exertion, or are taking medication that affects heat tolerance. Staff will not prevent an adult member from playing in conditions below the suspension threshold purely on the basis of personal risk, but reception and coaching staff are trained to offer guidance if asked and to flag concerns discreetly where a member appears unwell. Members are strongly encouraged to bring their own water and to make use of the complimentary chilled water stations provided courtside at every outdoor branch.

9. Recognising Heat-Related Illness
All customer-facing staff receive periodic training in recognising the early signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke, including excessive sweating or its sudden absence, confusion, nausea, dizziness and rapid heartbeat. Any staff member who observes these signs in a member, guest or colleague is authorised to stop play immediately and to escalate to the on-site first aider without needing management approval first. This authority applies regardless of the affected person's seniority, membership tier, or position within an ongoing match or tournament fixture.

10. First Aid and Escalation Path
Every branch maintains at least one first aider on duty during all opening hours, with equipment including cooling towels, oral rehydration supplies and a shaded recovery area separate from active courts. Where symptoms are mild, the first aider will move the individual to shade, encourage fluid intake and monitor recovery for a minimum period before permitting any return to activity. Where symptoms are moderate or severe, including confusion, vomiting, or loss of consciousness, the first aider will contact emergency medical services immediately and notify the branch general manager, who in turn informs the regional operations lead within the hour so that the incident can be logged and reviewed centrally.

11. Post-Incident Review
Every heat-related incident requiring first aid intervention beyond basic water and shade is logged in the central incident system and reviewed by the health and safety committee within a short period of the event. Reviews consider whether existing thresholds, staffing levels or shade provision at the branch in question were adequate, and any resulting recommendations are circulated to all outdoor branches rather than being treated as isolated to the branch where the incident occurred. Repeated incidents at a single branch trigger a mandatory facilities review, which may result in additional shade structures, revised court scheduling, or adjusted peak hours guidance specific to that location.

12. Court Surface and Equipment Considerations
High surface temperatures can affect both footing and ball behaviour, and duty managers are expected to factor this into their assessment alongside air temperature and humidity readings. Where court surface temperature is judged likely to pose a burn risk to bare skin or unsuitable footwear, signage is displayed advising against prolonged contact with the surface and members are reminded that appropriate court shoes are required at all times. Equipment such as ball machines and rebound walls may also be temporarily withdrawn from use if extreme heat is affecting their safe operation, with alternative equipment offered where available.

13. Exceptions for Private Bookings and Corporate Events
Private bookings and corporate events are subject to the same suspension authority described in clause 4, and no contractual arrangement, deposit paid, or advance planning overrides the duty manager's judgement on the day. Where a private event is disrupted by a heat suspension, the branch will work with the organiser to reschedule within a reasonable period or to relocate the event indoors at the same or a nearby branch, and standard cancellation fees are waived in full for weather-related disruption of this kind.

14. Policy Review and Communication
This policy is reviewed on a rolling basis in light of updated regional guidance, operational experience, and feedback gathered from members and coaching staff across all branches. Any material changes to thresholds, peak hours guidance or escalation procedures are communicated to members through the booking app and to staff through mandatory briefings before taking effect, with a reasonable notice period provided wherever the change is not driven by an immediate safety concern requiring same-day implementation.

title: Liability, Insurance and Personal Property
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out the terms under which Baseline Padel manages liability exposure, insurance provisions and the handling of personal property across all branches, including outdoor branches and those operating within shared leisure or hospitality developments. It applies to members, pay-and-play guests, junior participants, coaching clients, spectators, corporate booking parties and any visitor entering a Baseline Padel facility, whether or not that individual is actively playing. Where a specific branch operates under a modified arrangement due to shared tenancy with a hotel, residential community or retail development, the host site's own conditions of entry may apply in addition to this policy, and the more restrictive term will generally take precedence.

2. Assumption of Risk
Padel is a physical sport involving rapid movement, close proximity to glass and mesh enclosures, and shared court space with other players. By entering any court area, all participants acknowledge and accept the inherent risks of the sport, including but not limited to collisions with other players, contact with racquets or balls, falls on court surfaces, and incidental contact with fixed structures such as glass walls, posts and netting. Baseline Padel does not accept liability for injuries arising from the ordinary and foreseeable risks of play where courts, equipment and surfaces have been maintained in accordance with our standard inspection schedule. This clause does not remove liability arising from negligence on the part of Baseline Padel staff or contractors.

3. Facility Maintenance and Duty of Care
All branches undergo routine inspection of court surfaces, glass panels, lighting rigs, netting tension and surrounding walkways, with outdoor branches subject to additional checks following periods of heavy rainfall, sandstorm activity or extreme heat that may affect surface grip or structural fittings. Any defect identified through inspection or reported by a member will be logged and the affected court withdrawn from the booking system until remedied. Members and guests are asked to report visible hazards immediately to reception or via the in-app support channel rather than continuing play, since continued use of a known hazard may affect the outcome of any subsequent claim.

4. Personal Injury Reporting
Any injury occurring on Baseline Padel premises, however minor it may appear at the time, should be reported to the duty manager on-site before the individual leaves the venue wherever practicable. A written incident report will be completed jointly with the affected party, capturing the court number, time of incident, witnesses present and a description of events. Where an individual is unable to remain on-site due to the severity of the injury, a family member, coach or fellow player should notify staff as soon as reasonably possible, and in any case within 48 hours, to allow the incident to be logged accurately. Failure to report an injury within a reasonable timeframe may limit our ability to investigate the circumstances and may affect eligibility for any goodwill consideration.

5. Coaching and Programme Liability
Participation in group clinics, private lessons, junior academy sessions or club tournaments is subject to the same assumption of risk principles outlined above, with the additional condition that participants must disclose any relevant medical condition, injury history or physical limitation to the coaching staff prior to the session commencing. Coaches reserve the right to modify or decline participation in a drill where a disclosed condition presents a heightened risk. Parents or guardians booking junior sessions confirm at the point of booking that the child is medically fit to participate and that any allergies or conditions requiring emergency intervention have been communicated in writing to the branch.

6. Equipment Use and Hire
Racquets, balls and other equipment hired or borrowed from any branch are provided on an as-available basis and are inspected periodically for wear. Members using personally owned equipment do so entirely at their own risk, and Baseline Padel accepts no responsibility for equipment failure, including racquet breakage, grip degradation or string snap, occurring during play. Where hired equipment is found to be defective and this defect contributes materially to an injury, the matter will be escalated to branch management for internal review and, where appropriate, referral to our insurers.

7. Insurance Coverage Overview
Baseline Padel maintains public liability insurance across all branches, covering claims arising from proven negligence in the operation, maintenance or staffing of our facilities. This insurance does not extend to cover loss or damage to personal property, nor does it function as personal accident or medical insurance for members or guests. Members and guests engaging in regular play, particularly those participating in competitive leagues or tournaments, are strongly advised to hold independent personal accident insurance or ensure their existing health cover extends to recreational sporting injury, since Baseline Padel's coverage is not a substitute for individual protection.

8. Personal Property Disclaimer
Baseline Padel branches provide lockers, changing facilities and, at most locations, supervised reception storage for valuables during play. Notwithstanding these provisions, Baseline Padel does not accept liability for the loss, theft or damage of personal property left in changing rooms, on court-side benches, in car parks or anywhere else on the premises, except where such loss arises directly from proven negligence by a staff member acting within the course of their duties. Members are strongly encouraged to use locker facilities where available and to avoid leaving valuables, including phones, wallets, jewellery and car keys, unattended at any point during their visit.

9. Lost Property Handling
Items found on-site by staff or reported as lost by members will be logged in the branch lost property register and held securely for a period of 30 days from the date of discovery. After this period, unclaimed items of nominal value may be donated to a nominated charitable partner, while items of higher value will be retained for a further 60 days pending claim before disposal. Claimants must provide a reasonable description of the item and, where possible, proof of purchase or a matching booking record for the date in question before an item is released. Baseline Padel is not responsible for the condition of items by the time they are claimed, particularly perishable goods, electronics left uncharged, or items exposed to changing room humidity.

10. Vehicle and Car Park Liability
Where car parking is provided on-site, whether within a dedicated Baseline Padel car park or a shared facility car park at a hosted branch, this is offered as a convenience to members and not as a supervised or insured service. Baseline Padel accepts no liability for damage to vehicles, theft of vehicle contents, or loss arising from use of these car parks, and members are advised to secure valuables out of sight and lock vehicles at all times. Any incident involving a vehicle should still be reported to branch staff so that CCTV footage, where available, can be reviewed and shared with the relevant authorities if requested.

11. Third-Party and Contractor Liability
Events, external coaching bodies, corporate activation days and third-party tournament organisers operating within any branch are required to hold their own public liability insurance and to provide evidence of this cover prior to the event taking place. Baseline Padel's own liability framework does not automatically extend to cover injuries or losses arising from activities run by external parties on our premises, and any claim relating to such an event should be directed in the first instance to the organising body, with Baseline Padel facilitating introduction of the relevant contact details on request.

12. Exclusions and Limitations
This policy does not cover losses arising from acts of God, extreme weather events affecting outdoor branches, power outages beyond our reasonable control, or injuries resulting from a member's own reckless conduct, intoxication, or deliberate disregard of posted safety notices and staff instruction. Claims involving alleged negligence must be supported by the incident report referenced in Clause 4, and claims submitted without a corresponding on-site report will be considered on their individual merits but may be more difficult to substantiate. Baseline Padel reserves the right to request supporting documentation, including medical reports or independent witness statements, before any liability determination is made.

13. Escalation and Dispute Resolution
Members wishing to raise a formal liability or property claim should submit details in writing to their home branch manager, who will acknowledge receipt within 5 working days and aim to provide a substantive response within 21 days, extended where insurer involvement or external investigation is required. Where a member is dissatisfied with the branch-level outcome, the matter may be escalated to the regional operations office for independent review. Baseline Padel encourages resolution through this internal process before any external legal action is pursued, though nothing in this policy restricts a member's statutory right to pursue a claim through appropriate legal channels.

14. Policy Review and Communication
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in insurance arrangements, facility upgrades, or operational learning arising from incident trends across all branches. Material changes will be communicated to members via the booking app, branch noticeboards and email notification ahead of taking effect, and continued use of any Baseline Padel facility following such notice constitutes acceptance of the updated terms. Members are encouraged to review this policy periodically and to raise any questions with branch reception staff, who can also direct enquiries to the central member services team for matters requiring further clarification.

title: Incident Reporting and Escalation
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how incidents of any nature occurring on Baseline Padel premises, whether during organised play, open booking sessions, coaching clinics, social events, or general use of communal areas, are to be reported, recorded, and escalated. It applies to all branches, including outdoor branches where exposure to weather and open-air conditions introduces additional risk factors. It covers members, guests, junior players, coaching staff, maintenance contractors, and any visitor present on site at the time an incident occurs. The intent is not to assign blame but to ensure that every incident, however minor it may first appear, is captured consistently so that patterns can be identified and corrective action taken before a similar event recurs.

2. Definition of a Reportable Incident
A reportable incident includes any injury to a person, any near-miss that could reasonably have caused injury, damage to club or personal property, a safeguarding concern involving a minor or vulnerable adult, an altercation between players or spectators, equipment or court surface failure, a fire or evacuation event, and any situation requiring the attendance of emergency services. Reports are not limited to physical harm; verbal abuse, harassment, or conduct that breaches the club's code of behaviour must also be logged under this policy, even where no physical contact occurred.

3. Immediate Duty of the Person Present
Any member of staff, coach, or duty manager who witnesses or is made aware of an incident must attend the scene without delay, assess whether the situation requires first aid or emergency service intervention, and secure the immediate area to prevent further harm. This may mean closing a court, cordoning off a wet or damaged surface, or asking bystanders to move back. Staff are expected to remain calm, avoid speculative comment about cause or fault, and focus first on the wellbeing of those involved before turning to administrative steps.

4. First Aid and Medical Escalation
Where an injury has occurred, a trained first aider on duty must be summoned immediately. If the injury appears serious, involves loss of consciousness, suspected fracture, heavy bleeding, or any symptom that a first aider cannot confidently manage, emergency medical services must be called without waiting for management authorisation. No member of staff should attempt to move an injured person unless leaving them in place presents a greater risk. Once the immediate medical need has been addressed, the duty manager on site must be informed within minutes, not at the end of a shift, so that the wider escalation process can begin promptly.

5. Written Report Within 24 Hours
Every reportable incident, regardless of severity, must be recorded in writing using the club's standard incident report form within 24 hours of the event. The report should include the date and time relative to the shift in which it occurred, the names and contact details of those involved and any witnesses, a factual description of what happened, and any immediate action taken. Reports should avoid subjective judgement about fault; the purpose of this stage is to capture what was observed and done, not to reach a conclusion about responsibility.

6. Escalation to Branch Management
Once the initial report is filed, the duty manager must escalate it to the branch general manager before the end of the same operating day. Incidents involving suspected serious injury, safeguarding concerns, police involvement, or significant property damage must be escalated immediately by phone or direct message rather than waiting for the end of the shift. The branch general manager is responsible for reviewing the report, determining whether further action such as court closure, equipment inspection, or contact with the affected party's family is needed, and confirming that appropriate first steps have already been taken.

7. Escalation to Group Level
Certain categories of incident must be escalated beyond the branch to group management within 48 hours. These include any incident resulting in hospital attendance, any safeguarding concern involving a minor, any incident attracting police or media attention, and any incident where a member has indicated intent to pursue a formal complaint or legal action. Group management maintains oversight across all branches so that recurring issues, whether related to a particular type of court surface, a recurring hazard at outdoor branches during certain weather conditions, or a pattern of behaviour by a specific individual, can be identified and addressed at a policy level rather than treated as isolated events.

8. Outdoor Branch Weather and Environmental Incidents
Outdoor branches carry additional risk from heat exposure, sudden wind, surface water following rainfall, and reduced visibility during low-light conditions. Any incident linked to these factors, including heat-related illness, a slip on a wet surface, or an injury caused by wind-blown equipment, must be reported using the same process but should additionally note the prevailing conditions at the time, whether posted warnings or temporary closures were in effect, and whether the affected court had received a pre-session safety check.
