Where a pattern of weather-related incidents emerges at a given outdoor branch, the branch manager must review scheduling and shading arrangements and report findings to group management.

9. Incidents Involving Minors
Any incident involving a player under eighteen requires the immediate notification of a parent or guardian, regardless of the apparent severity of the injury or issue. Where the incident raises any safeguarding concern, however minor it may seem, it must be escalated directly to the designated safeguarding lead at group level within the same day, bypassing the standard 48-hour window that applies to other categories. Staff must never attempt to resolve a safeguarding concern informally or agree to keep it confidential from management at a parent's or child's request; all such matters must be documented and escalated regardless of any wish expressed by those involved.

10. Disputes Between Members or Guests
Incidents arising from disagreements over court bookings, scoring disputes, or conduct during social play should be de-escalated on the spot wherever possible by the duty manager or coach present. Where a dispute cannot be resolved informally, or where one party alleges harassment, discrimination, or threatening behaviour, a full incident report is required and the matter must be escalated to branch management for review under the club's code of conduct. Repeated incidents involving the same individual, whether as a subject of complaint or otherwise, should be flagged in the report so that a pattern can be identified across visits and, where relevant, across branches.

11. Property Damage and Equipment Failure
Where an incident involves damage to club property, such as a cracked glass panel, a failed net mechanism, or a damaged racket loaned by the club, the item involved must be removed from service immediately and retained for inspection rather than discarded or repaired before review. This allows maintenance staff or, where necessary, an external technician to determine the cause of failure and assess whether other equipment of the same type across other branches should be inspected as a precaution. Any incident where equipment failure is suspected to have caused or contributed to an injury must be escalated to group level regardless of the severity of the injury itself.

12. Data Handling and Confidentiality
Incident reports frequently contain personal and sometimes medical information about those involved. Reports must be stored securely, accessible only to relevant management and, where applicable, insurers or legal advisers, and retained for the period required by the club's data retention schedule before secure disposal. Details of an incident should not be discussed with staff who have no operational reason to know them, and information should never be shared with other members, on social media, or in casual conversation, irrespective of how well known the individuals involved may be within the club community.

13. Insurance and External Notification
Where an incident may give rise to an insurance claim, whether relating to injury, property damage, or third-party liability, the branch general manager must notify the group's insurance contact within the timeframe specified in the relevant policy documentation, typically within a small number of days of the event, to avoid prejudicing any claim. Where an incident involves suspected criminal conduct, contact with the police is not contingent on internal escalation being completed first; staff should contact the appropriate authorities as the situation demands and inform management as soon as practicable afterwards.

14. Non-Compliance and Review
Failure by any member of staff to report an incident in accordance with this policy, whether through omission, delay, or deliberate underreporting, will be treated as a serious conduct matter and may result in disciplinary action. Branch management is required to review all incident reports on a recurring basis to identify trends, and group management will periodically audit reporting practices across all branches to confirm that timeframes and escalation paths set out in this policy are being followed consistently. This policy itself will be reviewed periodically to reflect changes in operational practice, facility layout, or regulatory guidance, with updates communicated to all staff before they take effect.

title: Child Supervision and Drop-Off
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel manages the supervision, drop-off, and collection of children across all eight branches, including both indoor and outdoor courts, academy programmes, holiday clinics, and casual play sessions. It applies to every junior member, guest, or visiting child under the age of sixteen who attends a branch either for coached activity or as an accompanying family member. The intent is to ensure that responsibility for a child's welfare is always clearly defined between the parent or guardian and Baseline Padel staff, with no ambiguous handover periods during which nobody is accountable for a minor's whereabouts.

2. Minimum Age for Unaccompanied Attendance
Children aged twelve and above may be dropped off and left unaccompanied for booked academy sessions, provided a signed consent form is on file and a contactable guardian number is registered in advance. Children under twelve must be accompanied onto the premises by a parent, guardian, or a nominated adult of at least eighteen years, who must remain within the club premises or confirm an agreed collection window with reception before departing. Coaches and duty managers are not permitted to accept responsibility for a child under twelve without this documented handover, regardless of how familiar the child may be to staff.

3. Registration and Consent Documentation
Before any junior participates in a session, a guardian must complete a registration form covering emergency contact details, any relevant medical conditions, authorised collection adults, and photography or filming consent where applicable. This documentation must be refreshed periodically, and branches reserve the right to refuse participation where records are missing, illegible, or older than twelve months. Verbal assurances at the front desk do not substitute for written consent, and staff are trained to decline last-minute drop-offs where paperwork cannot be located within a reasonable time.

4. Drop-Off Procedure at Reception
All drop-offs must be logged at the reception desk of the relevant branch, noting the time of arrival, the name of the accompanying adult, and the session the child is attending. Guardians are asked to wait until a coach or supervising staff member has visually acknowledged the child before leaving the building. This clause exists specifically to prevent situations where a child is left in a communal area, such as a café or viewing gallery, under the mistaken assumption that general staff presence constitutes supervision.

5. Collection Procedure and Authorised Adults
Collection must be made by a guardian or an adult explicitly named on the registration form. Reception staff are instructed to request identification if the collecting adult is not recognised from previous visits, and a child will not be released to anyone who cannot be verified against the authorised list, even if the child recognises them. Where a guardian anticipates a change in the collecting adult, written or messaged notice to the branch in advance is required; informal notice given verbally by the child is not accepted as sufficient authorisation.

6. Late Collection
Sessions have a defined end time, and guardians are expected to arrive punctually. Where a child remains uncollected fifteen minutes after a session concludes, staff will attempt to contact the registered guardian numbers in sequence. If no contact is established within a further fifteen minutes, the duty manager will be notified and the child will be kept within a supervised reception or lounge area, never left alone in a car park, changing room, or outdoor court area. Repeated late collection, defined as three or more occurrences within a rolling period, may result in a review of the family's booking privileges and a formal conversation with the branch manager.

7. Non-Collection and Emergency Escalation
In the rare event that a child remains uncollected beyond one hour past session end, and all registered contacts remain unreachable, the branch will escalate to local authorities in line with standard child welfare procedure, as staff cannot retain sole responsibility for a minor indefinitely outside of programmed hours. This escalation path is a last resort and is documented internally, with guardians informed of the full sequence of contact attempts once reunited with their child. Branches strongly encourage guardians to list at least two independent emergency contacts precisely to avoid this scenario.

8. Supervision During Sessions
During coached academy sessions, the ratio of coaches to children is maintained according to age group and court capacity, with younger age bands supervised more closely than teenage groups engaged in advanced drills. Supervision is limited to the duration and location of the booked activity; it does not extend to communal areas such as pro shops, cafés, or car parks before or after the session unless a staff member has been specifically briefed to do so. Guardians who wish for supervision to extend informally, for instance while they run a brief errand nearby, must arrange this explicitly with the duty manager rather than assuming it is covered by default.

9. Siblings and Non-Participating Children
Siblings who are not enrolled in the session but accompany a family to the branch remain the full responsibility of the accompanying guardian at all times. They may not be left in viewing areas, play corners, or lounges under the assumption that general staff presence equates to supervision. Outdoor branches in particular carry additional risks from open court surrounds and equipment storage areas, and guardians are asked to keep non-participating children within direct sight rather than relying on club premises being inherently child-safe.

10. Medical Incidents and First Aid
Should a child require first aid or become unwell during a session, staff will administer basic first aid where trained to do so and will contact the registered guardian immediately. For anything beyond minor first aid, branches will contact emergency medical services without waiting for guardian confirmation, given the priority of the child's welfare over procedural sequencing. Guardians are asked to ensure that any pre-existing medical conditions, allergies, or medication requirements are clearly noted on the registration form, as incomplete medical disclosure can materially affect the speed and appropriateness of any response.

11. Behavioural Expectations and Removal from Session
Children are expected to follow coach instructions and observe standard court safety rules, including appropriate footwear and equipment use. Where a child's behaviour poses a safety risk to themselves or others, a coach may pause their participation and, if necessary, contact the guardian to collect them early. This is treated as a safety measure rather than a disciplinary one in the first instance, though repeated incidents may be referred to the branch manager for a longer-term decision regarding continued enrolment.

12. Photography, Filming, and Data Privacy
Where a guardian has not provided consent for photography or filming, staff will take reasonable care to exclude that child from promotional images or video captured during sessions, camps, or events. Guardians should note that this cannot be guaranteed in wide shots of shared courts or group activities, and any concerns should be raised with the branch before the session begins rather than after material has been captured. Requests for removal of existing footage will be handled through the branch's general data query process.

13. Holiday Camps and Extended Programmes
Full-day holiday camps and multi-day clinics follow this same drop-off and collection framework but include additional midday handover points, such as lunch breaks, where guardians may be asked to reconfirm collection arrangements. Because these programmes often run for several consecutive days, registration details should be checked at the start of the programme rather than assumed to carry over accurately from a prior term, particularly where contact numbers or authorised adults have changed.

14. Policy Review and Guardian Responsibility
This policy is reviewed periodically and may be updated to reflect operational changes across the group; the current version is always available at reception and via the membership portal. Ultimately, the safety of a child on Baseline Padel premises depends on close cooperation between guardians and staff, and guardians are asked to treat registration accuracy, punctual collection, and clear communication as shared obligations rather than administrative formalities.

title: Safeguarding and Staff Vetting
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel protects children and young people under the age of eighteen who take part in coaching sessions, holiday camps, academy programmes, birthday events, and any other activity run across all branches, whether indoor courts or outdoor branches exposed to seasonal scheduling changes. It applies to every member of staff, contracted coach, temporary freelance instructor, intern, volunteer, and any third-party supplier who may come into contact with minors on our premises. Parents, guardians, and members are entitled to expect that safeguarding is treated as a continuous operational priority rather than a once-a-year training exercise, and this document should be read alongside our Code of Conduct and our Incident Reporting Procedure.

2. Recruitment and Right-to-Work Verification
All individuals applying for a role that involves supervising or coaching minors undergo a structured recruitment process that includes identity verification, confirmation of right-to-work status, and validation of any coaching qualifications or certifications claimed on their application. No candidate is permitted to begin unsupervised work with children until their documentation has been checked against the original issuing source wherever practically possible. Where a qualification was obtained overseas, the People and Culture team will seek independent confirmation from the awarding body before the certificate is accepted as valid, and any delay in this confirmation results in the candidate being restricted to shadowed, non-contact duties only.

3. Background Screening Requirements
Every candidate for a children's coaching or supervisory position must complete a background screening check appropriate to their country of prior residence, covering at minimum the preceding five years. Where a candidate has lived or worked in multiple countries during that period, equivalent checks are sought from each relevant jurisdiction, and the recruitment file is not closed until either satisfactory clearance is received or a documented decision is made by a senior manager explaining why an exception was granted. Screening is refreshed on a rolling basis no less than every three years for continuing staff, and immediately upon any change of role that increases a staff member's access to minors.

4. Ratios and Supervision Standards
Academy and camp sessions maintain a minimum coach-to-child ratio appropriate to age group, typically no more than one coach to eight children for participants aged six to eleven, and one coach to twelve for participants aged twelve and above, though outdoor branches may apply tighter ratios during periods of high heat when additional welfare monitoring is required. A qualified coach must never be left as the sole adult supervising a group without a second staff member or duty manager present within the facility, and lone-working arrangements involving a single adult and a single child are prohibited except where a parent or guardian remains within direct line of sight throughout the session.

5. Photography, Filming, and Digital Media
Parents or guardians must provide explicit written consent before any photograph or video featuring their child is used in marketing materials, social media posts, or internal training content. Consent preferences are recorded against the child's membership profile and must be checked by staff before any content involving that child is published externally. Personal devices belonging to coaches or staff may not be used to photograph or film children under any circumstances; only club-issued equipment, logged and stored on secured internal systems, may be used, and any breach of this rule is treated as a serious disciplinary matter regardless of intent.

6. Changing Rooms, Facilities, and Physical Contact
Changing areas and washroom facilities are monitored by periodic staff presence checks rather than continuous supervision, and coaches are instructed to remain outside these spaces except in the case of a genuine welfare emergency, which must then be logged and reported to a duty manager within the same shift. Physical contact between staff and minors should be limited to what is necessary for demonstrating technique, correcting posture, or providing first aid, and must always be visible, brief, and proportionate. Any contact outside these boundaries, or any contact a child appears uncomfortable with, must be reported by the observing staff member regardless of the seniority of the person involved.

7. Communication with Minors Outside Sessions
Staff members are prohibited from contacting children directly through personal phone numbers, personal social media accounts, or private messaging applications for any reason connected to coaching, camps, or club activities. All communication regarding scheduling, progress updates, or behavioural matters must be directed to the parent or guardian through official club channels, and any staff member who receives unsolicited contact from a minor must forward it unanswered to their branch manager and document the occurrence. Exceptions for organised group communication, such as a parent-managed team messaging group for a tournament squad, must be approved in advance and include at least one parent representative at all times.

8. Reporting a Concern
Any staff member who observes, suspects, or receives a disclosure of harm involving a child must report it the same day to their branch's designated Safeguarding Lead, using the standard concern form, and must never attempt to investigate the matter independently or confront the individual concerned. If the Safeguarding Lead is unavailable, the report escalates automatically to the duty manager on site, who holds temporary responsibility for initiating the response. Reports are treated as confidential and shared only with those who need to know in order to keep the child safe or to meet a legal obligation, and staff will not face any detriment for raising a concern in good faith, even if it is later found to be unsubstantiated.

9. Escalation to Senior Leadership and External Authorities
Where a concern indicates a risk of serious harm, the branch Safeguarding Lead must notify the Group Safeguarding Officer within twenty-four hours, and where the concern suggests a criminal matter, the appropriate authorities are contacted without waiting for internal sign-off. Baseline Padel does not delay external reporting in order to protect its own reputation or commercial interests, and any staff member found to have suppressed or delayed a report for such reasons will face disciplinary action up to and including dismissal. A written record of every escalation, including timestamps and the names of those informed, is retained in the confidential safeguarding file maintained separately from general HR records.

10. Managing Allegations Against Staff
Where an allegation is made against a staff member, that individual is immediately removed from all duties involving direct contact with minors pending review, without this action being treated as an admission of guilt or a formal disciplinary sanction. The Group Safeguarding Officer coordinates any necessary parallel processes, including internal investigation, engagement with external authorities where warranted, and support for both the child involved and the staff member, who retains the right to be informed of the general nature of the allegation and to respond to it. Reinstatement occurs only once the review has concluded and senior leadership has confirmed there is no ongoing risk.

11. Third-Party Coaches, Guest Instructors, and Partner Programmes
Where a visiting coach, guest instructor, or partner organisation delivers a session on Baseline Padel premises, that individual or organisation must provide evidence of equivalent background screening before being granted access to minors, and a Baseline Padel staff member with safeguarding training must remain present throughout the session. Partner programmes operating under a co-branded arrangement are contractually required to adopt safeguarding standards no lower than those set out in this policy, and any partner unable to demonstrate compliance will have their access suspended until the matter is resolved.

12. Recordkeeping and Confidentiality
All safeguarding records, including screening documentation, concern forms, and escalation logs, are stored securely with access restricted to the Group Safeguarding Officer, branch Safeguarding Leads, and senior leadership on a need-to-know basis. Records are retained for a period sufficient to satisfy legal and regulatory requirements and are never disclosed to a parent, guardian, or third party except where required by law or where doing so is necessary to protect a child from harm. Requests from parents for information about an ongoing safeguarding matter involving another family's child will not be fulfilled, regardless of the relationship between the families.

13. Staff Training and Refresher Requirements
All staff with contact with minors complete safeguarding induction training before their first unsupervised session and refresh this training at intervals set by the Group Safeguarding Officer, typically annually. Training covers recognising signs of harm, understanding reporting obligations, appropriate use of physical contact and communication, and the specific procedures outlined in this policy. Attendance is recorded, and any staff member who falls overdue on refresher training is restricted to supervised duties only until the requirement is met.

14. Policy Review and Amendment
This policy is reviewed periodically by the Group Safeguarding Officer in consultation with branch management to ensure it remains aligned with best practice and any applicable regulatory guidance. Amendments are communicated to all staff and, where relevant to their rights or expectations, to parents and guardians through official club channels, and continued participation in Baseline Padel programmes following such notice constitutes acknowledgement of the updated terms.

title: Junior Academy Enrolment
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs enrolment into the Baseline Padel Junior Academy programme across all eight branches, covering age eligibility, registration procedures, fees, conduct expectations, and the handling of disputes or exceptional circumstances. It applies to all juniors aged four to seventeen participating in structured coaching sessions, holiday camps, and pathway squads, whether booked as a term-long commitment or as part of a short-term intensive block. Parents and legal guardians are considered the primary point of contact for all administrative matters relating to a junior's enrolment, regardless of who physically brings the child to sessions.

2. Age Groups and Placement
Juniors are placed into one of four developmental bands: Mini Padel (four to six years), Junior Foundation (seven to nine years), Junior Development (ten to thirteen years), and Junior Performance (fourteen to seventeen years). Placement is determined primarily by age at the time of enrolment, though head coaches at each branch retain discretion to move a child up or down a band following an initial assessment session if physical coordination, confidence, or prior experience warrants it. Any such reassignment will be communicated to the guardian in writing before the child's second session, and guardians may request a review of the placement within seven days if they disagree with the coach's recommendation.

3. Registration Requirements
Enrolment is only considered complete once a guardian has submitted a signed registration form, an emergency contact record, and a declaration of any relevant medical conditions or allergies. Outdoor branches additionally require a sun and heat acknowledgement form during the warmer months, confirming that the guardian understands session timings may be adjusted for the child's wellbeing. Incomplete registrations will not secure a place on a waitlisted programme, and academy staff are not permitted to allow a junior onto court without a completed medical declaration on file, even for a trial session.

4. Trial Sessions
Every new junior is entitled to one paid trial session prior to committing to a full term. Trial sessions are charged at the standard single-session rate and are non-refundable once attended, though they are fully creditable towards a term enrolment if the guardian confirms sign-up within seven days of the trial. Where a branch's academy is fully subscribed, trial sessions may be offered at an alternative branch or placed on a waitlist; guardians will not be charged until a confirmed slot is available.

5. Term Enrolment and Payment
Term enrolment is billed in advance for the full block of sessions and may be settled by card, bank transfer, or approved corporate account where applicable. A non-refundable registration fee applies to first-time enrolments only and is waived for siblings enrolling in the same term. Instalment arrangements may be requested for terms exceeding eight weeks, subject to approval from the branch academy coordinator, but instalments do not alter the guardian's liability for the full term fee should the child withdraw partway through.

6. Missed Sessions and Make-Ups
Baseline Padel does not offer refunds for individual missed sessions within a term, as coaching slots are reserved and staffed in advance. However, one make-up session per term may be arranged where a child misses a session due to documented illness, provided the guardian notifies the branch before the missed session begins. Make-up sessions are scheduled at the branch's discretion, subject to space in an equivalent age band, and cannot be carried forward into a subsequent term. Persistent unexplained absences may result in the junior's place being reallocated to a waitlisted child after two consecutive unnotified absences.

7. Withdrawal and Refunds
Guardians wishing to withdraw a child from a term programme must provide written notice to the branch at least fourteen days before the next billing cycle. Withdrawals made with proper notice are eligible for a pro-rated refund of unused sessions, calculated from the date notice is received rather than the date of the guardian's final attendance. Withdrawals made without the required notice period are not eligible for a refund of the current billing cycle, though no further charges will be applied beyond that cycle. Refunds, where due, are processed to the original payment method within a reasonable number of business days and cannot be issued as cash under any circumstance.

8. Conduct, Discipline and Safeguarding
All coaching staff assigned to junior programmes have undergone background screening appropriate to working with minors, and a designated safeguarding lead is available at every branch during academy hours. Juniors are expected to follow reasonable instructions from coaches, treat peers and equipment with respect, and refrain from behaviour that endangers themselves or others on court. A first instance of disruptive behaviour will typically result in a verbal warning and a note to the guardian; repeated or serious incidents, including bullying or deliberate damage to facilities, may lead to a formal meeting with the academy coordinator and, in severe cases, suspension or removal from the programme without refund. Any safeguarding concern raised by a guardian, coach, or third party will be escalated immediately to the branch safeguarding lead and handled in accordance with Baseline Padel's separate child protection procedures.

9. Medical Conditions and Emergencies
Guardians are responsible for keeping medical declarations current and must notify the branch promptly of any change in a junior's health status, including new allergies, injuries, or medication requirements. In the event of an injury during a session, on-site staff will administer basic first aid and contact the guardian using the details provided at registration; where the injury appears serious, staff are authorised to call emergency services without waiting for guardian consent. Baseline Padel reserves the right to request a written medical clearance before allowing a junior to return to court following a significant injury or illness, and coaches may decline to let a child participate on a given day if they appear visibly unwell or unfit for physical activity.

10. Weather and Session Adjustments
At outdoor branches, sessions scheduled during periods of extreme heat or adverse weather may be shortened, relocated to a covered court where available, or rescheduled entirely at the discretion of the branch manager. Guardians will be notified of any changes as early as reasonably possible, typically through the same channel used for original booking confirmations. No refund is due where a session proceeds in an adjusted format, but a full make-up session will be offered where a session is cancelled outright due to weather and no reasonable alternative slot exists within that week.

11. Photography and Promotional Use
Baseline Padel may photograph or film junior sessions for internal coaching review and, separately, for promotional materials such as the club website or social channels. Guardians may opt out of promotional use at the time of registration by indicating this clearly on the registration form; this preference will be respected across all branches and does not need to be repeated each term. Internal coaching footage used solely for staff training and player development purposes is not subject to opt-out, as it is not shared externally.

12. Transfers Between Branches
A junior enrolled at one branch may request a transfer to another branch's academy programme, subject to space availability in the equivalent age band at the receiving branch. Transfers requested mid-term will carry forward any remaining pro-rated fee balance, and no additional registration fee applies provided the transfer is completed within the same membership year. Guardians should be aware that coaching styles, group sizes, and session timings may vary slightly between branches, and the receiving branch's head coach reserves the right to conduct a brief reassessment to confirm appropriate band placement.

13. Pathway and Performance Squad Selection
Juniors demonstrating strong progress within the Junior Development or Junior Performance bands may be invited to trial for a branch's pathway squad, which involves additional weekly sessions and periodic inter-branch fixtures. Selection is based on coach recommendation following observed performance and is not guaranteed by tenure or age alone. Guardians of juniors not selected in a given assessment cycle may request feedback from the head coach and are welcome to reapply at the next assessment window without prejudice to the child's standing in the general academy programme.

14. Escalation and Complaints
Any concern regarding coaching quality, billing discrepancies, or the handling of an incident should first be raised with the branch academy coordinator, who will aim to acknowledge the matter within a reasonable number of business days. Where a guardian remains unsatisfied with the outcome, the matter may be escalated in writing to the regional academy manager overseeing that branch, and, as a final step, to Baseline Padel's central customer relations team. All escalations are logged and reviewed to ensure consistency of outcome across branches, and guardians will receive written confirmation of the resolution reached at each stage.

title: Birthday Parties and Kids Events
body:
1. Scope and Applicability
This policy governs all birthday parties, junior social events, holiday camps with a celebratory component, and any private booking involving guests under the age of sixteen across all eight branches of Baseline Padel. It applies equally to indoor and outdoor branches, though certain clauses below carry additional conditions specific to outdoor courts where weather and shade provision must be factored into planning. Any party booking that includes court hire, coaching activity, or use of communal party areas falls under this document rather than the general facility hire terms, and where a conflict arises between this policy and our standard booking conditions, this policy takes precedence for kids events specifically.

2. Booking Windows and Lead Times
Birthday parties and kids events must be booked no fewer than fourteen days in advance to allow for coach allocation, equipment preparation, and catering coordination where applicable. Requests made within this window will be accommodated only where court availability, staffing, and catering capacity genuinely allow, and branches reserve the right to decline late requests without this being treated as a service failure. Peak weekend afternoon slots, which are the most requested across all branches, are typically booked out well ahead of the fourteen-day minimum during school holiday periods, so families are strongly encouraged to enquire as early as three months out for these preferred windows.

3. Age Groups and Group Sizing
Parties are organised into two broad age bands: juniors aged five to nine, and juniors aged ten to fifteen, as court activities, ball types, and net heights differ meaningfully between these groups. A standard party package accommodates up to twelve children on court at any one time, split across two courts where group size exceeds eight, with a qualified coach or activity leader assigned per court. Groups exceeding twelve children require either an additional court booking or a split-session format, and branches will advise on the most workable configuration based on their own court count and layout, since outdoor branches with fewer covered courts may have narrower options during hot months.

4. Adult Supervision Requirements
At least one parent or designated guardian must remain on site for the full duration of any kids event involving children under eight, and must be reachable within the venue for events involving older children. Baseline Padel coaching and activity staff are responsible for on-court safety and structured play, but are not a substitute for parental supervision during free play, food service, or gift-opening segments held in communal areas. Where a guardian leaves the premises without notifying venue staff, the branch reserves the right to pause the event until a responsible adult is confirmed present, and this pause will not be treated as time owed back to the booking.

5. Catering and Food Allergies
Where catering is arranged through Baseline Padel's approved party packages, the organising guardian must submit a full allergy and dietary requirement list at least seven days before the event date. Branches will make reasonable accommodation for common allergens including nuts, gluten, and dairy, but cannot guarantee an entirely allergen-free environment given shared kitchen and storage facilities at most sites. Families wishing to bring outside catering, including celebration cakes, are welcome to do so at all branches, though any outside food must be declared in advance and consumed in designated party areas rather than on court or in general café seating during busy periods.

6. Decorations and Personal Items
Organisers may bring balloons, banners, and table decorations, though helium balloons are not permitted inside indoor court halls at any branch due to ceiling clearance and air handling considerations; they may be used freely in outdoor party areas subject to wind conditions on the day. Confetti, glitter, and silly string are not permitted anywhere on court surfaces or in communal seating areas, as residue causes both slipping hazards and surface damage that falls outside normal wear covered by facility upkeep. Any decoration left behind after the booked slot ends will be removed and disposed of by venue staff, and Baseline Padel accepts no liability for personal items, gifts, or decorations left unattended before, during, or after the event.

7. Weather Contingencies at Outdoor Branches
Parties booked at outdoor branches during the warmer months are subject to heat management protocols, which may include shifting on-court activity to shaded or indoor areas, shortening active play segments, and increasing hydration breaks, all at the discretion of the duty coach. Where extreme heat, dust conditions, or unseasonal rain make outdoor play genuinely unsafe, the branch will offer to relocate the event to an available indoor court at the same or a nearby branch where capacity allows, or to reschedule the booking without penalty. Families booking outdoor slots during peak heat periods are encouraged to select morning or early evening windows, and branches may proactively recommend such adjustments at the time of booking.

8. Cancellations and Rescheduling
Cancellations made more than seven days before the event date receive a full refund of any deposit paid. Cancellations made between three and seven days before the event are eligible for a fifty percent refund or a full credit toward a rescheduled date within ninety days of the original booking. Cancellations made within seventy-two hours of the event, including no-shows, forfeit the deposit entirely, reflecting the coaching, catering, and court allocation already committed on the branch's side. Rescheduling due to a child's illness will be handled sympathetically and does not automatically fall under the cancellation fee structure provided reasonable notice is given and supporting context is offered to the branch team.

9. Behavioural Expectations and Coach Authority
The coach or activity leader assigned to a party retains full authority over on-court conduct for the duration of the booked session, including the right to pause activity, remove equipment, or end a segment early where behaviour poses a safety risk to participants or damage risk to facilities. This authority extends to birthday guests as well as the host child, and parents should be aware that favouritism toward the birthday child does not override safety protocols. Repeated disregard for coach instructions, including from accompanying adults who attempt to override on-court decisions, may result in the session being curtailed with no refund owed for the unused portion.

10. Photography, Filming, and Privacy
Branches permit personal photography and filming by parents and guardians for private use during kids events, but any content intended for social media or public sharing that includes children other than the organiser's own must have consent from the other children's guardians present. Baseline Padel staff may take incidental photographs for internal marketing archives during events, and organisers who do not wish their child to appear in such material should notify the branch team in writing prior to the event so that this can be flagged to on-duty staff. Branches are not able to guarantee that a request made verbally on the day will reach every staff member involved in the event.

11. Injuries, Incidents, and First Aid
All branches maintain first aid trained staff on site during operating hours, and any injury occurring during a kids event will be logged in an incident report regardless of severity, with a copy offered to the guardian on request. Minor injuries such as scrapes or knocks common to active play will be treated on site; anything requiring further medical attention will prompt staff to contact the guardian immediately and, where the guardian cannot be reached within a reasonable window, to contact emergency services directly rather than delay care. Parents are asked to disclose any relevant medical conditions, including asthma or allergies with physical reaction risk, at the time of booking so that coaching staff can plan activities appropriately.

12. Non-Member and Walk-In Guests
Birthday parties frequently include guests who are not existing Baseline Padel members, and this is entirely permitted under standard party packages; no separate guest membership or day-pass purchase is required for children attending as invited guests of a paying booking. However, any adult accompanying a non-member child who wishes to use adjacent courts, the gym, or café facilities independently of the party will be subject to standard visitor terms and, where relevant, walk-in pricing, which sits outside the scope of the party booking itself.

13. Facility Damage and Liability
Organisers are financially responsible for any damage to court surfaces, nets, glass walls, or furniture caused deliberately or through clear negligence during a booked kids event, distinct from normal wear expected during active children's play. Baseline Padel carries public liability cover for incidents arising from facility condition or staff conduct, but does not extend cover to personal belongings, outside equipment brought by guests, or vehicles parked on site. Any dispute regarding damage assessment or charges should be raised with branch management within seven days of the event so that photographic evidence and staff accounts can still be reasonably gathered.

14. Escalation and Complaints
Any concern arising before, during, or after a kids event, whether relating to coaching quality, catering, facilities, or billing, should first be raised with the duty manager at the branch on the day where possible, as many issues can be resolved immediately with on-site adjustment. Where a matter remains unresolved, guardians may escalate in writing to the regional events team, who will respond within five working days with either a resolution or a clear explanation of next steps. Formal complaints regarding safety incidents are escalated as a priority and reviewed by branch management within forty-eight hours of being logged, independent of the standard complaints timeline.

title: Junior Equipment and Court Sizing
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel manages racket sizing, court dimensions, and associated equipment provisions for junior members and guests across all branches, including both indoor and outdoor branches. It applies to all coached sessions, open-play bookings involving juniors, junior academies, holiday camps, and any junior tournament fixtures hosted on club premises. The policy is designed to protect younger players from equipment-related strain injuries, to ensure consistency of experience across the group, and to give parents, guardians, and coaching staff a clear reference point when questions of sizing or suitability arise. Where this document is silent on a specific scenario, branch duty managers should default to the safety-first principle underpinning every clause below.

2. Age-Banded Racket Sizing
Junior rackets are issued according to four standard age bands: under 8, 8 to 10, 11 to 13, and 14 to 16, with each band corresponding to a specific racket length and weight profile held in branch equipment stores. Under-8 players are issued rackets no longer than 36 centimetres with a lightweight foam or reduced-density core, the 8 to 10 band moves to a slightly longer frame with a soft-touch face, and the 11 to 13 and 14 to 16 bands progress toward adult specification while still remaining lighter than standard adult rackets. Age bands are a starting point rather than a rigid rule, and coaching staff are expected to adjust upward or downward based on a child's height, grip strength, and prior playing experience, provided any deviation is noted on the player's junior profile within the booking system.

3. Height and Strength Override
Where a junior's physical development sits noticeably outside their age band, for example a tall 9-year-old or a smaller-framed 13-year-old, branch coaching staff have discretion to override the standard age-banded racket in favour of a size better suited to the individual. This override must be authorised by a qualified coach present at the session, not by front-of-house staff issuing equipment from the counter, and should be recorded so that future bookings automatically reflect the adjusted sizing. Parents requesting an override on behalf of a child who is not currently enrolled in coaching should be directed to a short assessment with the duty coach before any change is made permanent on the system.

4. Court Dimensions for Junior Play
All branches maintain access to reduced-dimension courts or adjustable court markings suitable for junior-format play, typically used for players in the under-8 and 8 to 10 bands. These courts feature a shortened playing area and lowered effective net height achieved through club-approved net straps, allowing younger players to sustain rallies without being overwhelmed by the full adult court footprint. Full-size courts remain available and are, in fact, the default setting for the 11 to 13 and 14 to 16 bands, though coaches may book a reduced court for skill-specific drills such as volleying practice or wall-rebound work regardless of the player's age band.

5. Booking Reduced Courts
Reduced-dimension court configurations must be booked through the junior programmes section of the booking system rather than the standard adult court calendar, as this ensures the correct net height and boundary markers are set up in advance by facilities staff. Where a branch has only one convertible court, priority is given first to scheduled academy sessions, second to junior camps, and third to ad hoc family bookings, with any conflict resolved by the duty manager on a first-confirmed basis. Members wishing to convert a standard court themselves, without staff supervision, are not permitted to do so, as incorrect net tensioning has historically been a source of avoidable equipment strain and minor injury.

6. Equipment Loan and Try-Before-Buy
All branches hold a rotating stock of loan rackets across the junior sizing bands, available at no charge to registered junior members attending coached sessions, and at a nominal hire fee for casual or guest bookings. Loan equipment is inspected for grip wear, frame cracking, and string tension before and after each use, and any racket failing this check is withdrawn from circulation immediately rather than left for the next junior to collect. Families considering a purchase are encouraged to trial two or three sizes across separate sessions before committing, and pro shop staff at branches with a retail counter can apply a modest credit toward a purchase made within a short window of a paid trial hire, subject to the receipt being presented.

9. Exceptions for Elite or Fast-Tracked Juniors
A small number of juniors identified through the academy pathway as playing significantly above their age band may be approved to use adult-specification rackets and full-size courts ahead of the standard progression schedule. This exception requires sign-off from the head coach at the relevant branch, supported by a brief written rationale placed on the player's file, and is reviewed periodically to confirm the arrangement remains appropriate as the child continues to grow and develop. Fast-tracked status does not exempt a junior from the club's general supervision and safeguarding requirements, and such players remain subject to all other clauses in this policy including equipment inspection and court booking protocols.

10. Damaged or Ill-Fitting Equipment During a Session
Where a racket is found to be damaged, warped, or clearly ill-fitting once a session is already underway, coaching or front-of-house staff must swap the equipment immediately rather than allowing play to continue for the remainder of the booking. A brief pause of this kind is not deducted from session time, and where no suitable replacement is available on-site, the family is entitled to reschedule the affected portion of the session at no extra cost within a reasonable period. Persistent equipment shortages at a given branch should be escalated by the duty manager to the regional equipment coordinator rather than resolved informally on a repeated basis, since recurring gaps usually indicate a stock ordering issue rather than a one-off oversight.

11. Outdoor Branch Weather Considerations
At outdoor branches, junior sessions and reduced-court configurations are subject to additional discretion during periods of strong wind, direct heat, or surface dampness, since lighter junior rackets and lowered nets can behave unpredictably in adverse conditions. Duty managers at outdoor branches are authorised to suspend or relocate a junior booking to an indoor court where one is available, or to offer a rescheduled slot at no charge where it is not, and this decision should never be left to the judgement of the junior players themselves or to a parent unfamiliar with the branch's specific court layout. Coaches running outdoor academy sessions during the warmer months should also factor in more frequent hydration breaks, which may modestly extend total session time without additional charge to the family.

12. Parental Disputes Over Sizing Decisions
Where a parent or guardian disagrees with a coach's sizing recommendation, whether that be a racket judged too small, too large, or a court configuration felt to be inappropriate for their child, the first point of resolution is a direct conversation with the coach involved, ideally immediately following the session while details are fresh. If the matter remains unresolved, the parent may request a short review with the branch's head coach, who will observe the junior in a subsequent session before confirming or amending the original recommendation. Only where this second review fails to resolve the disagreement should the matter be escalated to the regional junior programmes manager, and such escalations should be raised within a reasonable period following the disputed session rather than after an extended lapse of time.

13. Safeguarding and Supervision Interaction
This policy operates alongside, and does not override, Baseline Padel's separate safeguarding and supervision policy, meaning that any equipment or court sizing decision must still be carried out within an appropriately supervised environment for the junior's age group. Staff issuing equipment or setting up reduced courts should never do so as a substitute for proper supervision, and any concern arising during an equipment fitting or court setup that touches on safeguarding should be raised through the standard safeguarding reporting channel rather than logged solely as an equipment matter. Cross-referencing between the two policies is expected of all coaching staff, particularly those newer to the group who may not yet be familiar with how the two documents interact in day-to-day sessions.

14. Policy Review and Local Adaptation
This policy is reviewed periodically by the group's junior programmes team, with input gathered from head coaches across all branches to ensure the age bands, court configurations, and loan equipment provisions remain fit for purpose as playing standards and typical junior heights evolve over time. Individual branches may propose minor local adaptations, for example where a particular branch layout makes certain court conversions impractical, but any such adaptation must be submitted for approval centrally before being adopted rather than implemented informally at branch level. Members will be notified of material changes to this policy with reasonable advance notice through the usual club communication channels, and the version in effect at the time of a session is the version applied, regardless of any earlier arrangement a family may have previously been accustomed to.

title: Tournament Entry and Eligibility
body:
1. Scope and Application
This policy governs entry, eligibility, and conduct for all tournaments, leagues, and ranked ladder events organised under the Baseline Padel banner across all eight branches, whether hosted at indoor or outdoor facilities. It applies equally to member-only competitions, open invitational events, and any corporate or junior tournaments run in partnership with third parties. Where a specific event has its own published rules, those rules take precedence only where they do not conflict with the provisions set out here; in all other respects this policy remains the governing framework.

2. Eligibility Criteria
Entry is open to all current Baseline Padel members in good standing, meaning accounts free of unresolved disciplinary action, outstanding fees, or suspended access. Non-members may enter designated open events subject to payment of the applicable non-member surcharge, provided they hold valid identification and, where required by the event category, proof of a recognised external ranking. Players under eighteen years of age must be registered by a parent or legal guardian, who assumes responsibility for the player's conduct and any liability arising from participation. Staff members and coaches employed directly by Baseline Padel may compete only in categories explicitly designated as open to staff, to preserve competitive fairness for members.

3. Player Categorisation and Ranking Tiers
Tournaments are divided into categories reflecting playing standard, typically ranging from social and intermediate divisions through to advanced and open tiers. Category placement is determined by a combination of self-declared experience at first entry and subsequent internal ranking points accumulated through prior sanctioned play. Any player found to have materially misrepresented their standard to gain entry into a lower division may be reassigned to the correct category at the discretion of the tournament committee, and any results achieved under the incorrect classification may be voided. Players moving between branches retain their accumulated ranking points, which are held centrally rather than locally to any single facility.

4. Registration Process and Entry Windows
Registration opens on a published date ahead of each event and closes once either the entry cap is reached or the stated deadline passes, whichever occurs first. Entries must be submitted through the official booking channel; entries made informally through branch staff, verbal agreement, or messaging platforms are not valid and will not secure a place in the draw. Draws are typically finalised within 48 hours of the registration deadline, after which changes to entrant names are treated as substitutions rather than new registrations. Applicants are strongly advised to confirm receipt of their entry through the confirmation notice issued automatically upon successful payment, as unconfirmed entries cannot be guaranteed a place should demand exceed capacity.

5. Entry Fees and Payment Terms
Entry fees vary by category and event tier and must be paid in full at the time of registration to secure a place; unpaid entries are held provisionally for a maximum of 24 hours before being released to waitlisted players. Fees are generally non-refundable once the draw has been published, save for the withdrawal circumstances described in clause seven. Where an event is cancelled or postponed by Baseline Padel for reasons outside a player's control, fees will be refunded in full or credited to the player's account within a reasonable processing period, at the player's choice. Promotional discounts, membership-linked reductions, and multi-event bundle pricing cannot be combined unless explicitly stated in the event's own terms.

6. Partner and Team Formation Rules
For doubles and team events, both players in a pairing must independently meet the eligibility and category requirements for the division entered; a mismatch in standard between partners may result in the pairing being moved up to the higher-rated category. Partnerships must be confirmed at the point of registration, and changes to a confirmed partner after the draw has been published are treated as a substitution requiring committee approval rather than an automatic right. Players may not register for more than one team within the same category at the same event, though entry into differing categories at the same event, such as one doubles and one mixed division, is generally permitted where the schedule allows.

7. Withdrawal, Substitution and Refunds
Players who can no longer participate must notify the tournament office in writing as early as possible. Withdrawals made before the draw is published are typically eligible for a full refund or credit; withdrawals made after publication but before the event begins may be eligible for a partial credit at the discretion of the tournament committee, reflecting costs already committed on the player's behalf. Same-day withdrawals without prior notice, including no-shows, are not eligible for any refund and may affect the player's standing in future entry priority. Substitutions of one player for another within the same category are permitted up to a stated cut-off before the first match, subject to the replacement player independently meeting all eligibility criteria.

8. Age and Category Verification
Baseline Padel reserves the right to request identification or supporting documentation to verify a player's age, membership status, or external ranking at any point before, during, or after a tournament. Players entering junior or veteran age-banded categories must be able to satisfy the relevant age threshold as at the first day of the event; players who fall outside a band partway through a multi-day tournament remain eligible for the remainder of that event on the basis of their age at commencement. Any player unable or unwilling to provide reasonable verification when requested may be withdrawn from the draw without refund, and repeated attempts to misrepresent eligibility may result in a broader suspension from future tournament entry across all branches.

9. Conduct, Code of Play and Disqualification
All entrants agree to abide by the standard code of conduct governing on-court behaviour, including timely arrival, respectful engagement with opponents and officials, and adherence to standard scoring and let conventions. Serious breaches, including abusive conduct towards staff or other players, deliberate racket abuse, or manipulation of match outcomes, may result in immediate disqualification from the event without refund and referral to the club's broader disciplinary process. Lesser infractions, such as persistent lateness or disputes over scoring, will typically be handled by the on-site tournament official in the first instance, with any appeal directed through the escalation path described in clause eleven.

10. Weather, Court Availability and Rescheduling
At outdoor branches, matches are subject to suspension or rescheduling where weather conditions, particularly during the warmer months, are judged by on-site staff to pose a risk to player safety or court integrity. Where a match is interrupted, play will typically resume from the point of stoppage once conditions allow, though the tournament committee retains discretion to adjust formats, such as reducing match length, to keep the wider draw on schedule. Where an entire day's play must be moved indoors to an alternative branch to avoid cancellation, affected players will be notified as early as practicable, and reasonable efforts will be made to keep travel distances minimal.

11. Disputes and Escalation Path
Any dispute regarding a scoring decision, category placement, or on-court ruling should first be raised with the match official at the time it arises. If unresolved, the matter should be escalated to the tournament director present at the venue, whose decision on matters of play is final for the purposes of that match. Disputes concerning eligibility, disqualification, or refund entitlement that remain unresolved at branch level may be submitted in writing to the central tournaments team within 14 days of the event's conclusion, and a written response will typically be issued within 21 days of receipt. Decisions made at this central level represent the final stage of the internal review process.

12. Medical and Insurance Requirements
Entrants are responsible for ensuring they are medically fit to participate in competitive play and are strongly encouraged to hold personal accident or sports injury cover appropriate to tournament-level activity, as Baseline Padel's own facility insurance does not extend to personal medical costs arising from play. Players with a pre-existing condition that may reasonably affect their safety on court are asked to disclose this confidentially to the tournament office ahead of the event so that appropriate on-site precautions can be considered. Where a player is injured during a match, on-site staff will make a reasonable assessment of whether play can safely continue, and their decision to withdraw a player from that match on safety grounds is final and not subject to the standard dispute process.

13. Wildcard and Late Entry Provisions
A limited number of wildcard places may be reserved at the discretion of the tournament committee for players who do not meet the standard registration deadline but whose participation is considered to strengthen the draw, such as returning members or players with a strong recent record at another branch. Late entries submitted after the official closing point will only be considered where capacity allows and where the resulting draw can still be balanced fairly, and such entrants should expect to pay any applicable late entry premium. Wildcard and late entries remain fully subject to all other eligibility, conduct, and category rules set out in this policy.

14. Amendments to this Policy
Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend this policy from time to time to reflect operational needs, regulatory changes, or feedback from members and tournament participants. Where amendments affect an event for which entries have already been accepted, the version of the policy in force at the time of registration will ordinarily continue to apply to that event, unless the change is required for player safety or legal compliance, in which case the updated terms will take immediate effect across all branches. The current version of this policy is available on request from any branch and through the club's official communication channels.

title: Tournament Formats and Scoring
body:
1. Scope and Application
This policy governs all tournaments, leagues, box ladders, and organised social competitions run under the Baseline Padel name across all eight branches, whether hosted on indoor courts, outdoor courts, or a combination of both. It applies equally to member-only events, open invitationals, corporate bookings converted into competitive formats, and junior competitions unless a separate junior-specific ruleset has been published for that event. Where a discrepancy exists between this document and information printed on a specific event page, the event page prevails only if it has been reviewed and stamped by the Tournaments Department; otherwise this policy is authoritative. Branch managers do not have authority to alter scoring formats unilaterally without sign-off from the regional Tournaments Coordinator, and any such deviation must be documented and communicated to all registered players no later than 48 hours before the first scheduled match.

2. Standard Match Formats
The default format for Baseline Padel tournaments is the best of three sets, with a match tiebreak (first to ten points, win by two) played in lieu of a third set unless the event has been explicitly designated as a full three-set format on the registration page. Group-stage or round-robin phases within larger draws typically use a single set to six games, win by two, with a seven-point tiebreak at six games all, in order to keep court rotations moving to schedule. Knockout and semi-final rounds from the quarter-final stage onward generally revert to best of three full sets to reflect the increased stakes, though this is confirmed per event and never assumed by default. Players should check the specific bracket sheet posted at the host branch or on the digital scoreboard, as formats can differ between the group phase and the knockout phase of the same tournament.

3. Golden Point and No-Ad Scoring
Unless stated otherwise, all Baseline Padel tournament matches are played using golden point scoring at deuce, meaning that at forty-forty the following point is decisive and determines the game, with the receiving pair or player choosing which side to receive from. Traditional advantage scoring is reserved for finals and for any event specifically labelled as a "classic format" competition on its registration listing. Coaches, captains, and social organisers should note that golden point materially changes strategy and pacing, and players unfamiliar with it are encouraged to request a briefing from front-of-house staff before their first match, particularly at branches that run frequent turnover between recreational and competitive bookings on the same courts.

4. Match Tiebreak Procedures
Where a match tiebreak is used to decide a deciding set, it is played to ten points with a minimum two-point margin, and players change ends every six points as well as at the conclusion of the tiebreak itself. Serve rotates after the first point and then every two points thereafter, following standard padel convention, and the pair due to serve first in the tiebreak is the pair who received first in the immediately preceding game. Any dispute over serve order or end-change timing during a tiebreak should be raised immediately with the on-court supervisor or, where no supervisor is present, escalated to the branch duty manager before the next point is played; retroactive challenges once a match has concluded and been recorded will not be entertained.

5. Seeding and Draw Construction
Seeding for open and invitational tournaments is based primarily on prior Baseline Padel league standings, ranked ladder position, or verified external ranking data where supplied at registration, with the Tournaments Department retaining final discretion over seed placement in cases of incomplete or disputed information. Byes are allocated to the highest seeds first in draws that do not divide evenly by a power of two, and where a bye is contested as unfair by a non-seeded pair, the matter is reviewed by the Tournaments Coordinator rather than branch staff, since draw construction is centrally managed even when the event itself is hosted locally. Partial draws, meaning entries received after the published cutoff, are only accommodated where court and time availability allow, and late entrants accept placement into the draw as determined by staff, including potential placement in a preliminary qualifying round rather than the main draw.

6. Round-Robin Tiebreak Criteria
When round-robin groups conclude with two or more pairs level on match wins, placement is determined first by head-to-head result between the tied parties, second by set difference across all group matches, third by game difference across all group matches, and fourth, if still level, by a single deciding tiebreak played between the tied pairs at a time designated by the tournament desk. Retired or walkover matches are counted as a loss for tiebreak calculation purposes for the retiring or absent pair, but the completed score at the point of retirement, if any games were played, is not used in game difference calculations beyond that point. Any pair found to have manipulated a result or scoreline within a round-robin group to affect seeding outcomes for themselves or another pair may be disqualified from the tournament entirely, at the sole discretion of the Tournaments Department, with no refund of entry fees.

7. Weather Interruptions and Outdoor Branch Adjustments
At outdoor branches, matches interrupted by rain, excessive heat advisories, or dust conditions are paused at the discretion of the duty manager, and play resumes at the score standing at the point of interruption once conditions are deemed safe by branch staff. Where an interruption extends beyond a reasonable window, typically ninety minutes though this may be adjusted by the Tournaments Coordinator based on scheduling pressure, matches may be moved to an available indoor court at the same or a partner branch, provided all remaining players are notified in a timely manner. If conditions make same-day completion impossible, the Tournaments Department will reschedule remaining matches within the following seven days where feasible, and pairs unable to attend the rescheduled slot due to prior commitments should notify the tournament desk as early as possible so that a walkover or alternative accommodation can be arranged rather than a late withdrawal being recorded against them.

8. Walkovers, Retirements, and Late Arrivals
A pair arriving more than fifteen minutes after their scheduled match time without prior notice to the tournament desk forfeits the match as a walkover in favour of their opponents, and this walkover is recorded as a loss for all standings and tiebreak purposes. Retirements due to injury or illness mid-match are recorded as a loss to the retiring pair, with the completed score preserved for record purposes, and medical retirements do not entitle a pair to entry fee refunds except where the event's specific terms state otherwise. Repeated late arrivals or retirements by the same individual across multiple Baseline Padel events may be reviewed by the Tournaments Department as a pattern of conduct, and persistent cases may result in a requirement to provide advance notice or a temporary restriction from tournament registration.

9. Code of Conduct and Scoring Disputes
Players are expected to self-officiate scoring in the absence of an assigned referee, and disputes over a specific point should be resolved by replaying the point where genuine uncertainty exists, rather than by unilateral insistence from either side. Where a dispute cannot be resolved between the pairs, the on-duty supervisor is called to the court and their decision on that point is final and binding for that match, though the incident may still be noted in the tournament log for later review if conduct concerns are raised. Deliberate scoring manipulation, repeated disputing of clearly settled points, or abusive conduct toward opponents or staff during a scoring disagreement may result in a game or match penalty at the supervisor's discretion, escalating in serious cases to disqualification from the tournament by the branch manager in consultation with the Tournaments Department.

10. Court Allocation and Scheduling Conflicts
Court allocation for tournament matches takes priority over standard recreational bookings during published tournament windows at the host branch, and any recreational booking that overlaps with an extended tournament match will be relocated to an alternative court by staff wherever possible, with the affected member notified as early as practical. Where scheduling conflicts arise between two tournament matches requiring the same court, priority is given first to matches already in progress, second to knockout rounds over group-stage matches, and third to the match with the earlier original start time. Players competing in multiple events or divisions on the same day are responsible for managing their own schedule conflicts and should flag potential clashes to the tournament desk at registration so that staggered start times can be arranged where feasible.

11. Equipment, Ball Changes, and Court Standards
Official tournament balls are supplied by Baseline Padel and are changed according to the schedule published for that event, typically after the first seven games and every nine games thereafter for best of three formats, though pressure and heat conditions at outdoor branches may prompt earlier changes at the supervisor's discretion. Players may use their own rackets but not their own balls during official tournament matches unless a shortage requires temporary use of spare balls held at the front desk. Any dispute regarding court surface condition, net height, or lighting adequacy should be raised with the duty manager before the match begins; complaints raised after a match has concluded on the basis of court conditions will not be grounds for a replay or result reversal except in cases of clear and demonstrable equipment failure, such as a collapsed net or non-functioning court lighting mid-match.

12. Age Divisions and Mixed-Format Events
Junior divisions, where offered, follow modified scoring at the discretion of the Tournaments Department, which may include shortened sets or race-to formats to suit shorter attention spans and playing duration, and these modifications are always published separately from the standard adult ruleset. Mixed-gender and mixed-age social competitions may adopt handicap scoring, such as a starting game or point advantage for one pair, and any handicap applied is fixed at the draw stage and does not change based on how a match is progressing. Players entering an age-restricted division are responsible for accurate self-declaration of eligibility at registration, and any pair found to have misrepresented eligibility may be disqualified retroactively, with results adjusted accordingly for all other affected pairs in that division.

13. Prize Distribution and Result Certification
Official results are certified by the Tournaments Department once the final match of a division has concluded and the scoresheet has been countersigned by both competing pairs or, where a pair declines to sign, by the on-duty supervisor noting the reason. Prizes, where offered, are distributed following certification and are not released on the basis of a verbal result reported courtside. Any challenge to a final certified result must be raised in writing to the Tournaments Department within seven days of certification; challenges raised after this window will not be considered regardless of the nature of the claim, in order to preserve the integrity of published standings and any associated ranking points.

14. Escalation and Final Authority
Where a situation arises that is not explicitly addressed by this policy, branch duty managers are authorised to make a reasonable interim decision to allow play to continue, with the matter formally escalated to the Tournaments Department within 24 hours for a binding ruling. The Tournaments Department retains final authority over all matters of format, scoring interpretation, disqualification, and draw integrity across all eight branches, and its rulings supersede any informal agreement reached between players or branch staff on court. Members who remain dissatisfied following a Tournaments Department ruling may request a written review by submitting their concern through the membership office, which will be acknowledged within a reasonable period and addressed as promptly as circumstances allow.

title: Tournament Conduct and Disputes
body:
1. Scope and Application
This policy governs conduct, disputes, and disciplinary matters arising during any tournament, ladder event, box league, or organised competition held at Baseline Padel facilities, across all branches. It applies to registered competitors, invited guests, coaches, hitting partners, and spectators for the duration of the event, including warm-up periods, changeovers, and any prize presentation immediately following play. Participation in a Baseline Padel tournament constitutes acceptance of these terms in full, regardless of whether a player has read the published rules in advance.

2. Code of Conduct
All participants are expected to compete with honesty, respect opponents and officials, and refrain from language or gestures that could reasonably be considered abusive, threatening, or discriminatory. Deliberate racket abuse, striking balls out of the enclosure in anger, or damaging court surfaces and glass panels will be treated as a conduct violation regardless of intent. Coaches and supporters seated courtside are bound by the same standard and may be asked to leave the viewing area if their behaviour is judged to be distracting or intimidating to players on court.

3. Match Officiating and Line Calls
Most Baseline Padel tournament matches are self-officiated by the players themselves, with each side responsible for calling lines on their own side of the net in good faith. Where a dispute over a specific call cannot be resolved between the two pairs within a reasonable time, either side may request the nearest available staff member or duty supervisor to make a determination from outside the court. That determination is final for the point in question and may not be revisited later in the match, even if further evidence becomes available.

4. Scoring Disputes
If players lose track of the score or disagree on the current game or set tally, play should stop immediately and the point should revert to the last score both sides can mutually agree upon. Where no agreement can be reached, a duty supervisor will review any available scoreboard record, match sheet, or recollection from a neutral bystander before issuing a ruling. Persistent or repeated scoring disputes raised in what appears to be a tactical manner, particularly late in a set, may be treated as a form of gamesmanship and addressed under the conduct clauses of this policy.

5. Equipment, Attire, and Court Standards
Competitors must use rackets and balls that meet the specifications published for the relevant tournament tier, and organisers reserve the right to inspect equipment before or during a match if a query is raised by an opponent. Non-marking court shoes are mandatory on all indoor and outdoor courts; players arriving without appropriate footwear may be given a short grace period to change but risk forfeiture of the warm-up or an administrative delay penalty. Branded clothing carrying commercial logos beyond a modest size may be restricted during finals played under sponsorship arrangements, with specific guidance issued ahead of the relevant draw.

6. Coaching and On-Court Communication
Unless a specific event format explicitly permits mid-match coaching, players may not receive tactical instruction, hand signals, or shouted advice from anyone outside the court during a live point. Between points and at changeovers, brief encouragement is permitted, but detailed tactical direction from a coach or teammate is not, and repeated breaches may result in a warning followed by a point penalty against the receiving pair.
