Any doubt over whether communication crossed into coaching will be resolved by the duty supervisor, whose judgement on the matter is final.

7. Walkovers, Retirements, and No-Shows
Players are expected to be present and ready at the scheduled match time; a pair not present within fifteen minutes of the published call time, without prior notice to the tournament desk, will forfeit the match by walkover. A player who retires mid-match due to injury or illness should notify the duty supervisor directly so the result can be recorded accurately, and any subsequent medical documentation submitted within a reasonable window may be considered when reviewing eligibility for later stages or refund requests. Repeated late arrivals across a single tournament may result in exclusion from the remainder of the draw at the organiser's discretion.

8. Weather Delays and Outdoor Branch Adjustments
At outdoor branches, matches may be paused, shortened, or rescheduled at short notice due to heat, wind, or rain, and players will be notified through the tournament desk or on-site announcements rather than by fixed timetable alone. Where a match is interrupted mid-point, the point is replayed in full once conditions allow; where interrupted between games, the score simply resumes. Organisers reserve the right to convert a suspended match to a shortened tiebreak format if conditions do not improve within a reasonable period, and this decision cannot be appealed once announced, given the practical constraints of rescheduling a full draw.

9. Disciplinary Sanctions
Breaches of conduct are addressed on an escalating basis wherever practical: a verbal warning, followed by a point penalty, followed by a game penalty, and ultimately disqualification from the match and potentially the remainder of the tournament. Serious incidents, including physical altercations, threats, or deliberate damage to facility property, may bypass this escalation entirely and result in immediate disqualification along with referral to branch management for a longer-term membership review. Any sanction beyond a verbal warning will be recorded on the player's tournament history and may be taken into account in future entry decisions.

10. Fair Play, Eligibility, and Ranking Integrity
Players must compete under their own registered name and category, and misrepresenting age group, gender division, or club ranking to gain a competitive advantage is treated as a serious breach subject to disqualification and forfeiture of any prize secured. Suspected match manipulation, including deliberately losing a match or set for seeding purposes in a later round, will be investigated by tournament management, and any pair found to have acted in this manner will be removed from the event and may face suspension from future Baseline Padel competitions for a defined period.

11. Spectator and Guest Conduct
Guests and spectators attending tournament matches are expected to remain in designated viewing areas and refrain from coaching, heckling, or engaging directly with players or officials during live play. Staff and duty supervisors have the authority to ask any spectator to leave the venue if their conduct is disruptive, and a player is responsible for ensuring their own invited guests comply with this standard. Where spectator behaviour is judged to have materially influenced a match outcome, the affected pair may request a formal review under the appeals process described below.

12. Filing a Dispute or Appeal
Any formal dispute regarding a match result, sanction, or officiating decision must be raised with the duty supervisor before leaving the venue on the day of the match wherever possible, or submitted in writing to the tournament desk within 48 hours of the match concluding. Appeals submitted after this window will only be considered in exceptional circumstances, such as documented medical incapacity, and the decision on whether to accept a late appeal rests solely with tournament management. Verbal complaints raised informally, without a follow-up written submission, will not be treated as a formal appeal for record-keeping purposes.

13. Escalation and Final Authority
Disputes that cannot be resolved at branch level by the duty supervisor are escalated to the regional tournament director, who will review all available match records, witness statements, and any relevant video footage where it exists before issuing a written decision within a reasonable period. The regional tournament director's ruling is final and binding on all parties, and no further internal escalation route is available within Baseline Padel; any dispute unresolved at this stage falls outside the scope of this policy and would need to be pursued through independent means.

14. Amendments and Event-Specific Rules
This policy sets out the baseline standard applied across all tournament formats, but individual events, particularly sponsored finals or ranked series matches, may publish supplementary rules addressing format-specific matters such as substitute players, tiebreak variations, or extended coaching allowances. Where a conflict exists between this policy and event-specific rules published ahead of a draw, the event-specific rules take precedence for that competition only. Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend this policy between tournament cycles, with the current version always available from the tournament desk at every branch.

title: Internal League Rules
body:
1. Scope and Purpose
These Internal League Rules govern all recreational and competitive league play organised under the Baseline Padel banner across all branches, including both indoor and outdoor branches. They apply to seasonal ladder leagues, fixed-group round robins, and any mixed-format internal competitions run by branch coordinators. These rules do not extend to open tournaments, member-guest events, or externally sanctioned competitions, which are governed by separate published guidelines. Where a conflict arises between branch-level custom and these Rules, these Rules take precedence unless a written exception has been granted by the Regional Tournament Office.

2. Eligibility and Registration
Participation in any internal league requires an active Baseline Padel membership or a valid league-only pass purchased at the time of registration. Players must register through the official booking channel before the published closing window for that season; late registrations may be accepted at the discretion of the branch coordinator only where a division has not reached capacity. A player may register for only one division per league cycle unless expressly approved to play across age or skill categories due to bracket shortages. Any player found to have misrepresented their skill rating for the purpose of gaining a competitive advantage will be reassigned to an appropriate division retroactively and may forfeit points already earned in that cycle.

3. Divisions and Seeding
Divisions are structured by self-declared and coordinator-verified skill level, typically ranging from introductory to advanced categories, with seeding based on prior league performance, ranking history, or a supervised assessment for new entrants. Seeding disputes must be raised in writing to the branch coordinator within 72 hours of the draw being published. Where a division fails to reach the minimum of six registered pairs or individuals, the branch reserves the right to merge that division with an adjacent one, adjust the fixture format, or postpone the division to the following cycle, with affected players notified as early as practicable.

4. Match Scheduling
Fixtures are published on the internal league portal and, where applicable, on branch noticeboards, with each match window typically spanning a set number of days to accommodate player availability. Players are responsible for agreeing court times directly with opponents within the published window unless the branch operates a fixed-slot system, in which case attendance at the allocated time is mandatory. Indoor branches may offer greater scheduling flexibility owing to consistent court availability, whereas outdoor branches are subject to seasonal and weather-related constraints that may compress or extend match windows at the coordinator's discretion.

5. Rescheduling and Byes
A maximum of one reschedule request per fixture is permitted without penalty, provided both parties agree and the match is completed before the window closes. Requests made within 24 hours of a scheduled match are subject to coordinator approval and may require supporting justification such as illness or unavoidable work commitment. Where no agreement can be reached, the match will default to a bye scored in favour of the player or pair who demonstrably attempted to schedule in good faith, evidenced through portal messages or booking logs. Repeated failure to schedule matches across a cycle may result in removal from the league without refund of entry fees.

6. Walkovers, No-Shows and Withdrawals
A player or pair not present and ready to play within fifteen minutes of the agreed or allocated start time forfeits the match as a walkover, with the standard losing score recorded for league table purposes. Players wishing to withdraw from the league entirely must notify their branch coordinator in writing; withdrawals made before the midpoint of the cycle will result in remaining fixtures being recorded as walkovers against the withdrawing party, while withdrawals after the midpoint may affect the integrity of the table and will be reviewed case by case, potentially resulting in the removal of all that player's results from the standings. Persistent no-shows across multiple cycles may lead to a suspension from future league registration.

7. Scoring and Match Format
Unless otherwise stated for a specific league, matches are played as the best of three sets using standard padel scoring, with a match tie-break played in lieu of a third set where time constraints apply. League points are awarded on a structured basis reflecting wins, narrow losses, and walkovers, with the exact points table published at the start of each cycle and available on request from the branch coordinator. Any variation to scoring format for a particular division, such as timed matches during periods of high court demand, must be communicated to all affected players before the first fixture of that division is played.

8. Conduct and Fair Play
All players are expected to observe standard etiquette, including honest line-calling, respectful communication with opponents, and adherence to any coaching or supervision instructions given by branch staff during league play. Disputes over line calls or scoring during unsupervised matches should be resolved by mutual agreement between players in the first instance; where no resolution is possible, the match should be paused and a member of branch staff consulted if available. Any conduct deemed abusive, discriminatory, or unsafe will be escalated immediately under the club's separate Code of Conduct policy and may result in removal from the league independent of any league-specific penalty.

9. Disputed Results
Results must be submitted by the winning player or pair through the official portal within 48 hours of match completion, with the losing party given the opportunity to confirm or dispute the submitted score. Where a dispute arises and cannot be resolved between the parties, both players should submit their account of the match to the branch coordinator, who will review any available evidence such as booking records or witness statements from other members present. Unresolved disputes may be escalated to the Regional Tournament Office, whose determination on the recorded result is final and not subject to further appeal within the league structure.

10. Standings and Tiebreakers
League standings are updated on a rolling basis as results are confirmed, with the table typically visible to all registered participants via the internal portal. Where two or more players or pairs finish level on points at the end of a cycle, tiebreakers are applied in the following order: head-to-head result, set difference across all matches, game difference, and finally a coordinator-supervised tiebreak match if scheduling allows before the announcement deadline. Where a tiebreak match cannot be arranged due to travel, injury, or venue availability, the higher position will be awarded based on set difference alone, with this method disclosed to affected players in advance.

11. Promotion, Relegation and Re-Entry
At the conclusion of each cycle, a defined number of top finishers in each division are eligible for promotion to the next division, while an equivalent number from the bottom of standings may be moved down, subject to space and player consent. Players who decline promotion may remain in their current division for one further cycle before promotion becomes mandatory should they retain a qualifying position. Players returning after a period of absence from league play will re-enter at a division level determined by their most recent verified rating rather than automatically resuming their prior position.

12. Prizes, Recognition and Entitlements
Where a league cycle carries associated prizes, vouchers, or recognition such as trophies or seasonal rankings, these will be described in the specific league announcement issued at the start of that cycle. Entitlement to any prize is contingent on completion of a minimum proportion of scheduled fixtures, typically set to discourage players from withdrawing after securing an early lead. Any prize forfeited due to ineligibility will be reallocated to the next eligible finisher in the standings, and no cash-equivalent substitution will be offered for non-monetary prizes unless explicitly stated in the original league terms.

13. Fees, Refunds and Cancellations
League entry fees are payable at the time of registration and are generally non-refundable once the draw has been published, reflecting the administrative and court allocation commitments already made. Where Baseline Padel cancels a division or an entire league cycle due to insufficient numbers, venue unavailability, or circumstances beyond reasonable control, registered players will be offered a full refund or credit toward a future cycle at their choosing. Partial refunds are not available for players who withdraw voluntarily after the league has commenced, except where supported by documented medical grounds reviewed by the branch coordinator.

14. Appeals and Final Authority
Any player wishing to formally appeal a decision made under these Rules, including but not limited to seeding, scoring disputes, or disciplinary outcomes, must submit a written appeal to their branch coordinator within seven days of the decision being communicated. The coordinator will forward unresolved or complex appeals to the Regional Tournament Office within a further seven days, together with all relevant match records and correspondence. The Regional Tournament Office holds final authority over all internal league matters, and its written decision concludes the internal appeals process, with no further review available through individual branch management.

title: Ranking Points and Seeding
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs how ranking points are earned, calculated, and applied across all Baseline Padel branches, and how those points translate into seeding positions for club, regional, and invitational tournaments organised under the Baseline Padel banner. It applies to all registered competitive players holding an active membership or tournament pass at any branch, including outdoor branches where seasonal scheduling may affect the calendar of qualifying events. The policy does not extend to purely social or corporate league play unless such play has been explicitly designated as a points-bearing event by the tournaments department in advance and communicated through the official booking platform.

2. Qualifying Events
Only tournaments formally listed on the Baseline Padel tournaments calendar as points-bearing will contribute to a player's ranking total. This includes branch-level opens, inter-branch cups, category championships, and any invitational event flagged as ranked at the time of listing. Friendly round-robins, coaching-led ladders, and casual box leagues do not carry ranking value regardless of the level of competition involved, and players should not assume points will be awarded retroactively to an event that was not designated as ranked before entries opened.

3. Points Allocation by Tier
Events are classified into three tiers reflecting their scale and entry requirements: Tier One covers flagship opens and finals-of-finals events drawing entrants from across all branches; Tier Two covers standard branch-level opens and category championships; Tier Three covers smaller invitational or short-notice events. Tier One results carry the highest point value, followed by Tier Two, then Tier Three, with the exact scale published alongside each event listing. Players are awarded points based on the round reached rather than match count alone, meaning a run to the semi-final of a Tier One event will typically outweigh a title won at Tier Three, reflecting the intent that ranking position should reward sustained performance against stronger fields.

4. Rolling Twelve-Month Window
A player's ranking total reflects points accumulated across a rolling window measured from the date of calculation backwards, rather than points earned within a fixed season. As older results fall outside this window they are automatically removed from the running total, and players will see their ranking adjust accordingly even without new tournament activity. This rolling approach is designed to keep rankings a current reflection of form rather than a permanent record, and members are encouraged to check their standing periodically rather than assume a single strong result will hold indefinitely.

5. Best Results Counted
Where a player has competed in more events than the maximum number counted toward ranking, only the highest-scoring results within the rolling window are retained in the calculation, with lower-value results discarded automatically by the system. This means players are not penalised for entering additional events purely for match practice, and are encouraged to compete regularly without fear that a single weak result will drag down an otherwise strong ranking position.

6. New and Returning Players
Players without sufficient ranked results to generate a calculated position are assigned a provisional seeding based on self-declared playing history, coaching assessment where available, and any results achieved at other recognised padel organisations, subject to verification by the tournaments desk. Provisional seedings are reviewed after a player's first two ranked events at Baseline Padel and adjusted to reflect actual performance, which may result in a player moving up or down the draw for subsequent entries. Returning players who have been inactive long enough for their previous points to fall outside the rolling window will similarly be treated as provisional entrants until sufficient recent results are recorded.

7. Doubles Partnerships and Shared Points
Because padel is played in pairs, ranking points earned in a given event are credited individually to each player rather than to the partnership as a unit, meaning a player's overall ranking reflects a composite of results achieved alongside different partners over time. When seeding a doubles draw, the pairing's combined seeding value is calculated from both players' individual rankings, generally by averaging or otherwise weighting them according to the method published for that specific event, since methods may vary slightly between flagship and standard tournaments. Players forming a new partnership shortly before an event should expect the pairing's seed to reflect this combined calculation rather than either player's individual ranking alone.

8. Walkovers, Byes, and Retirements
A walkover awarded due to an opponent's late withdrawal generally carries reduced point value compared with a completed match at the same round, reflecting that no match was actually contested. Byes issued for draw-balancing purposes carry no points at all, as no opponent was faced. Where a player retires mid-match due to injury or other cause, points are awarded to the surviving player based on the round in progress at the time of retirement, while the retiring player receives points corresponding to the round they had already completed prior to the retirement, not the round in which the retirement occurred.

9. Withdrawal and Forfeit Consequences
A player who withdraws from a tournament after the draw has been published but before their first match forfeits any points that would have been earned from that event and may, at the discretion of the tournaments committee, have a portion of previously earned points suspended if the withdrawal is deemed to have disadvantaged other entrants without reasonable cause, such as documented illness or a genuine scheduling conflict raised in good time. Repeated late withdrawals across multiple events within the rolling window may result in a player being moved to provisional seeding status regardless of their calculated total, as consistent unreliability undermines the integrity of the draw for other competitors.

10. Cross-Branch Recognition
Ranking points are recognised uniformly across all branches, meaning a result achieved at one location carries identical weight to the same result achieved at any other branch, including between indoor and outdoor branches despite differences in court surface or seasonal conditions. This uniform treatment ensures that a player's ranking reflects overall standing within Baseline Padel as a whole rather than performance at a single site, and supports fair seeding when players travel between branches to enter events not offered locally.

11. Category and Age-Group Adjustments
Points earned in age-restricted or category-specific draws, such as veterans or junior categories, are tracked separately from open-category points and do not automatically transfer between categories. A junior player who ages out of their category, or a veteran player who chooses to enter an open draw, will carry only the points relevant to the category being entered, with a provisional seeding applied where insufficient category-specific history exists. Mixed-category events, where offered, use a blended calculation published in advance for that specific tournament rather than a fixed club-wide formula, given the variation in format between such events.

12. Disputes Over Seeding
A player who believes their seeding has been calculated incorrectly should raise the matter with the tournaments desk at the hosting branch in writing before the draw is finalised, providing specific details of the results in question. Seeding disputes raised after a draw has been published and matches have commenced will not result in a redrawn bracket, as this would be disruptive and unfair to other entrants who have already prepared for their scheduled opponents; instead, any correction identified will be applied to the player's ranking total going forward and reflected in seeding for their next event.

13. Escalation Path
Where a dispute cannot be resolved at branch level, the matter should be escalated in writing to the central tournaments committee, which will review the calculation against the published points schedule and respond within a reasonable working period. Decisions of the tournaments committee on points calculation and seeding methodology are considered final, though the committee retains discretion to make a goodwill adjustment in exceptional circumstances, such as a documented system error affecting multiple players, in which case affected members will be notified directly and any correction applied retroactively within the current rolling window.

14. Policy Review
This policy is reviewed periodically by the tournaments committee to ensure the points structure remains fair as the competitive calendar grows and as new event formats are introduced. Any material change to tier values, the rolling window duration, or the seeding calculation method will be published on the tournaments calendar in advance of the events it affects, and will not be applied retroactively to results already recorded, ensuring players can rely on the rules in force at the time they competed.

title: Payment Methods and Billing
body:
1. Accepted Payment Methods
Baseline Padel accepts a range of payment methods across all branches, including major debit and credit cards, direct bank transfers, and approved digital wallets linked to a member's mobile device. Cash is accepted at reception desks for casual court bookings and pro-shop purchases only, and is not accepted for membership fees or academy programme payments due to reconciliation requirements. Outdoor branches with satellite reception points during peak season may temporarily restrict payment options to card and digital wallet only, and any such restriction will be clearly signposted at the point of booking. Members are encouraged to register a primary card on file to streamline recurring transactions and reduce delays at check-in.

2. Membership Billing Cycles
Membership fees are billed on a recurring cycle determined by the plan selected at sign-up, typically monthly, quarterly, or annually, with the billing date fixed to the anniversary of the original enrolment rather than a calendar date. Members switching between branches or plan tiers will have their billing cycle recalculated proportionally, with any adjustment reflected as a credit or charge on the following invoice. Where a member joins partway through a promotional period, the first invoice may reflect a prorated amount rather than the full standard rate, and this will be itemised clearly on the statement issued through the member portal.

3. Court Booking Payments
Court bookings made through the app, website, or reception must be paid for in full at the time of reservation unless the member holds a membership tier that includes complimentary or discounted court credits. Bookings left unpaid beyond the confirmation window, typically fifteen minutes from the time slot selected, will be automatically released back into general availability. Group bookings organised by a single lead player may be split among participants using the in-app payment-splitting function, though the lead player remains ultimately responsible for the full amount should other participants fail to settle their share within the stated window.

4. Card Authorisation and Holds
When a card is registered for recurring billing or used to secure a court booking, a small temporary authorisation hold may be placed on the account to confirm validity. This hold is not a charge and will be released automatically by the issuing bank within a standard clearing period, generally within a few business days, though the exact timing depends on the member's bank rather than on Baseline Padel. Members who notice a hold that has not cleared after ten business days should contact their branch reception or the central billing team, who can provide a reference number to assist the bank in releasing the funds.

5. Failed Payments and Retry Policy
Where a recurring membership payment fails due to insufficient funds, an expired card, or a bank-side decline, the system will automatically retry the charge up to three times over the following seven days. Members will receive a notification by email and through the app after each failed attempt, along with a direct link to update payment details. If all retry attempts are unsuccessful, the membership will be flagged as overdue and access privileges may be temporarily suspended until the balance is settled, though bookings already confirmed and paid for prior to the suspension remain valid.

6. Currency and Pricing
All prices across Baseline Padel branches are displayed and billed in UAE dirhams. Members paying with foreign-issued cards may see a currency conversion applied by their own bank, and any conversion fee or exchange rate margin is determined solely by the card issuer and not by Baseline Padel. Pricing for memberships, court hire, coaching packages, and retail items is reviewed periodically and any adjustment will be communicated to existing members with reasonable advance notice before it takes effect on their next billing cycle, rather than applied retroactively to prior invoices.

7. Corporate and Group Accounts
Companies and organised groups booking on behalf of employees or members may set up a consolidated corporate account, allowing multiple individual bookings to be billed centrally through a single monthly invoice rather than per-transaction card payments. Corporate accounts require a signed agreement with the central accounts team and are typically subject to a minimum monthly usage commitment across participating branches. Invoices for corporate accounts are issued on a fixed cycle and payment is expected within the terms agreed at setup, usually within a short window from the invoice date; late settlement may result in suspension of booking privileges for all linked individual users until the account is brought current.

8. Refunds and Credits
Refunds for cancelled bookings, coaching sessions, or membership downgrades are processed back to the original payment method wherever technically possible. Where the original method is no longer valid, such as an expired card, the refund will instead be issued as an account credit usable against future bookings or membership fees at any branch. Processing times for refunds to cards vary by issuing bank and are generally outside Baseline Padel's direct control, though the initiation of the refund on Baseline Padel's side is typically completed within a few business days of approval. Requests for refunds outside the standard cancellation window are considered on a discretionary basis and should be submitted in writing to branch management.

9. Promotional Codes and Vouchers
Promotional codes, gift vouchers, and referral credits may be applied at checkout for eligible bookings and membership sign-ups, subject to the specific terms printed on or issued alongside the code. Codes cannot generally be combined with other active promotions unless explicitly stated, and any unused balance on a partially redeemed voucher remains available for future use until the voucher's stated expiry, expressed always as a validity period from the date of issue rather than a fixed date. Vouchers purchased as gifts are non-refundable for cash once issued but may be transferred to another member's account upon written request to reception.

10. Automatic Renewal and Cancellation
Memberships are set to renew automatically at the end of each billing cycle unless the member submits a cancellation request through the app or in writing before the renewal date. Cancellation requests received after the billing date has passed will not be refunded for that cycle but will prevent any further charges from the following cycle onward. Members on fixed-term contracts, such as those tied to a promotional rate, may be subject to an early termination consideration if cancelling before the minimum term has elapsed, details of which are disclosed clearly at the point of sign-up.

11. Disputed Charges and Chargebacks
Members who believe a charge has been made in error should raise the matter directly with the branch billing desk or the central support line before initiating a chargeback with their card issuer, as this allows for a faster and more accurate resolution. Baseline Padel will investigate disputed charges within a reasonable period, typically resolving straightforward cases within ten business days, and will provide supporting transaction records where relevant. Where a chargeback is filed without prior contact and is later found to be unsubstantiated, the member's account may be placed under review and future bookings may require pre-payment by an alternative verified method while the matter is resolved.

12. Outstanding Balances and Suspension
Any outstanding balance on a member's account, whether from a failed membership payment, an unpaid corporate invoice portion, or a chargeback reversal, must be settled before further bookings can be made at any branch. Accounts with balances outstanding beyond thirty days from the original due date may be referred to the central accounts team for formal follow-up, and continued non-payment may result in permanent suspension of membership and forfeiture of any accrued credits or loyalty points. Members experiencing genuine financial difficulty are encouraged to contact branch management proactively to discuss a reasonable settlement arrangement before the account reaches this stage.

13. Data Security and Payment Information
All payment information collected across branches, whether entered online, through the app, or at a reception terminal, is processed through secure, encrypted channels in line with recognised industry standards. Card numbers are not stored in full on Baseline Padel's internal systems; instead, a tokenised reference is retained to enable recurring billing without exposing sensitive details. Staff are trained never to request full card numbers or security codes verbally, and members should treat any such request, whether by phone or email, as suspicious and report it immediately to branch management or the central support line.

14. Escalation and Customer Support
Members with unresolved billing concerns after engaging their home branch's reception team may escalate the matter to the central billing department, whose contact details are available through the app and on request at any branch. Escalated cases are typically assigned a reference number and reviewed within a stated turnaround period, with updates provided by email as the investigation progresses. Where a resolution cannot be reached at this level, members may request a final review by senior management, whose decision represents the conclusion of Baseline Padel's internal escalation process for payment and billing matters.

title: Refunds, Credits and Wallet Balance
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel manages refunds, account credits and wallet balances across all eight branches, including both indoor and outdoor facilities. It applies to court bookings, membership fees, coaching packages, tournament entries, retail purchases made through our pro shops, and any other chargeable service offered under the Baseline Padel brand. Where a specific product or promotional offer carries its own terms that conflict with this policy, those specific terms will take precedence, but in all other respects this document governs how monetary disputes, cancellations and account balances are handled. Staff at all branches are trained to apply this policy consistently, and members should expect the same treatment regardless of which location they attend.

2. The Baseline Wallet
Every member and registered guest has access to a Baseline Wallet, a digital balance tied to their account that can be used to pay for bookings, coaching, events and retail purchases at any branch. Funds may enter the wallet through direct top-ups, refunds issued as credit, promotional bonuses, or compensation for service disruptions. Wallet balances are not a form of stored currency in the legal sense and cannot be withdrawn as cash or transferred to a bank account under normal circumstances. They exist solely to be spent on Baseline Padel products and services. Members can check their balance at any time through the reception desk at any branch or via their online account, and a full transaction history is available on request.

3. Standard Booking Cancellations
Court bookings cancelled more than 24 hours before the scheduled start time are eligible for a full refund, issued by default as wallet credit unless the member specifically requests a refund to the original payment method. Cancellations made between 24 hours and 6 hours before the booking will receive a 50 percent wallet credit, reflecting the reduced likelihood that the slot can be resold. Cancellations inside the 6 hour window, or unexplained no-shows, are not eligible for any refund or credit, as the court is held exclusively for that member during peak scheduling periods and cannot typically be reallocated on short notice. Members who repeatedly cancel within the non-refundable window may be asked to prepay for future bookings.

4. Weather and Facility Disruptions at Outdoor Branches
Outdoor branches are naturally more exposed to conditions that can render a court unplayable, including excessive heat advisories during certain periods, sandstorms, or unexpected maintenance issues such as lighting or surface faults. Where Baseline Padel cancels or interrupts a booking due to conditions outside the member's control, the affected session will be refunded in full as wallet credit automatically, with no action required from the member. Where a member chooses not to play due to conditions that the club has not formally deemed unsafe or unplayable, standard cancellation timeframes in Clause 3 will still apply. Indoor branches are not subject to weather-related disruption but may occasionally experience air conditioning or facility issues that are handled under the same automatic credit principle.

5. Membership Refunds and Pro-Rata Adjustments
Membership fees are generally non-refundable once the membership period has commenced, reflecting the discounted rate members receive compared with pay-as-you-go pricing. Exceptions are made in cases of relocation outside the UAE, medical circumstances supported by appropriate documentation, or extended service unavailability caused by the club itself, such as a prolonged closure of a member's home branch. In approved cases, a pro-rata refund will be calculated based on the unused portion of the membership term, minus any discount differential already enjoyed relative to standard pricing, and will normally be issued as wallet credit. Cash or card refunds for memberships are considered only in exceptional circumstances and require sign-off from branch management.

6. Coaching Packages and Multi-Session Bundles
Coaching packages purchased as a bundle of sessions are refundable on a pro-rata basis only where the remaining sessions have not been scheduled or where a member is unable to continue due to injury, relocation, or a coach becoming permanently unavailable without a suitable replacement being offered. Partial refunds are calculated based on the per-session rate at the time of purchase rather than any bundled discount rate, and any already-used sessions are deducted at full price before the remaining balance is refunded. Requests to refund a coaching package simply because a member has changed their mind after several sessions have already taken place will not normally be accepted, though wallet credit may be offered at the discretion of the coaching manager.

7. Tournament and Event Entry Fees
Entry fees for tournaments, ladders and social events are refundable in full up to a defined withdrawal deadline communicated at the time of registration, typically set several days before the event to allow organisers to rebalance draws and order catering or merchandise. Withdrawals after this deadline are not eligible for a refund, as costs will already have been committed on the member's behalf, though the club may at its discretion allow the entry to be transferred to another member or to a future event of equivalent value. Events cancelled by Baseline Padel due to insufficient participation or unforeseen circumstances will be refunded in full to the original payment method, or as wallet credit with a small bonus if the member elects to keep the funds within their account.

8. Non-Refundable Items
Certain purchases are treated as final sale and are not eligible for refund except where faulty. This includes retail items such as racquets, footwear, apparel and consumables once used, opened, or worn, as well as gift vouchers once issued, and any promotional or discounted booking explicitly marked as non-refundable at the point of sale. Members are encouraged to review product descriptions and booking terms carefully before completing payment, as pro shop staff are able to advise on sizing and suitability prior to purchase but cannot reverse a sale once goods have left the branch in used condition.

9. Refund Method and Processing Times
Where a refund to the original payment method is approved, members should allow up to 10 business days for the funds to appear, as processing depends on the member's own bank or card issuer in addition to internal processing at Baseline Padel. Wallet credits, by contrast, are typically applied within 48 hours of approval and can usually be used immediately for any future booking or purchase. Refunds are always issued in the currency and to the payment method originally used wherever technically possible; where the original method is no longer valid, such as an expired card, the refund will default to wallet credit until alternative arrangements can be confirmed with the member.

10. Wallet Credit Expiry and Forfeiture
Wallet credit issued as a goodwill gesture or as compensation for a service disruption will typically carry an expiry period, most often 90 days from the date it is issued, after which any unused portion may be forfeited. Credit arising from a member's own cancelled booking or an approved refund does not expire under normal circumstances, provided the underlying membership account remains active. Where an account is closed, suspended for a breach of club conduct rules, or remains dormant for an extended period, any remaining wallet balance may be forfeited in accordance with the club's terms of membership, though members are always notified in advance and given a reasonable opportunity to use or query the balance before forfeiture takes effect.

11. Disputed Transactions and Chargebacks
Members who believe they have been charged in error should raise the matter directly with their home branch or the central member services team in the first instance, rather than initiating a chargeback with their card issuer, as this allows Baseline Padel to investigate and resolve the issue more quickly and without additional fees being applied to the member's account. Where a chargeback is filed before internal resolution has been attempted, the club reserves the right to suspend wallet and booking privileges on the account pending investigation. Legitimate disputes are typically resolved within 5 to 10 business days and, where the member's claim is upheld, any associated bank fees incurred by the club as a result of a premature chargeback may be deducted from the resolved refund amount.

12. Promotional and Goodwill Credit
From time to time Baseline Padel may issue promotional credit tied to seasonal campaigns, referral schemes, or as a goodwill gesture following a service complaint. Such credit is issued at the sole discretion of the club, is generally non-transferable between accounts, and cannot be exchanged for cash under any circumstances. Promotional credit will always state its expiry period and any restrictions on which services it can be applied to, such as exclusions on already-discounted bookings, at the time it is issued. Members are responsible for reading these terms, as unused promotional credit that lapses due to an unstated expiry will not typically be reinstated after the fact.

13. Escalation Path
Members who are unsatisfied with a refund or credit decision made at branch level may request escalation to the regional member services team, who will review the case within 5 business days and issue a written response. If the matter remains unresolved, a final review can be requested from the head office finance team, whose decision represents the final stage of the internal escalation process. Throughout this process members are encouraged to keep records of booking confirmations, payment receipts and any correspondence with staff, as these will assist in a faster and more accurate review of the case.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is reviewed periodically to reflect changes in payment processing, facility operations across all branches, and general club practice, and Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend any clause with reasonable notice provided to members through the usual communication channels, including in-branch notices and account messaging. Changes will not be applied retroactively to disputes already under active review at the time of amendment. Members are encouraged to check the current version of this policy periodically, particularly before relying on specific timeframes for cancellations, refunds or wallet credit expiry.

title: Pricing Structure, Peak and Off-Peak
body:
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out how Baseline Padel structures court pricing across peak and off-peak periods at all eight branches, including both indoor and outdoor facilities. It applies to all bookings made through the mobile application, the website portal, reception desks, and any bookings arranged verbally with staff that are subsequently confirmed in the system. The intention is to ensure transparency for members and guests alike, to manage demand fairly across busy and quiet periods, and to give staff a consistent framework for handling queries, exceptions, and disputes relating to court fees. This document should be read alongside the General Membership Terms and the Court Booking and Cancellation Policy, as pricing interacts closely with both.

2. Definition of Peak Hours
Peak hours are defined as the periods of highest anticipated demand at each branch, typically covering early morning slots before the working day begins, and the evening block from late afternoon through to closing time on weekdays, along with the majority of daytime hours across the weekend. Because demand patterns differ between branches depending on their surrounding population and typical member demographics, each branch publishes its own peak schedule on the in-app booking calendar, and this schedule takes precedence over any general description found in promotional materials. Members should always check the live calendar before assuming a slot is peak or off-peak, as the classification can shift with seasonal demand even where the clock time remains the same.

3. Definition of Off-Peak Hours
Off-peak hours cover the remaining slots not designated as peak, generally falling in the mid-morning and early afternoon window on weekdays, and limited slots later in the evening at weekends once the busiest windows have passed. Off-peak pricing is set at a reduced rate compared to peak pricing, reflecting lower expected occupancy, and is intended to encourage utilisation of courts during quieter parts of the day. Bookings that begin in an off-peak slot but extend into a peak slot due to an extended or back-to-back reservation will be charged at a blended rate, with the portion of time falling into each category billed according to the respective rate card, calculated automatically by the booking system at the point of confirmation.

4. Seasonal Adjustment for Outdoor Branches
Outdoor branches are subject to seasonal pricing adjustments that indoor branches do not experience, owing to the impact of temperature and daylight on playability. During the cooler months, outdoor courts typically see extended peak windows as more members choose to play at times that would otherwise be off-peak indoors. During the warmer months, daytime slots at outdoor branches may be discounted further, or in some cases suspended from active booking altogether, where court surface temperatures are deemed unsuitable for safe play by branch management. Any such suspension will be communicated through the app and posted at the relevant branch reception with as much notice as is practically possible.

5. Rate Card Publication and Review
Each branch maintains a published rate card covering standard peak and off-peak pricing for members and non-members, which is reviewed on a periodic basis by the central pricing team in consultation with branch managers. Rate cards may vary modestly between branches to reflect differences in local operating costs, court type, and typical demand, meaning a peak slot at one branch is not guaranteed to cost the same as a peak slot at another. Members are encouraged to check the current rate card within the app before confirming a booking rather than relying on previous bookings as a guide to current pricing, since rates are subject to change without individual notification, though material changes will be flagged through the general communications policy.

6. Membership Tier Pricing Differentials
Baseline Padel operates several membership tiers, and each tier carries a distinct discount applied against the standard peak and off-peak rate cards. Entry-level membership typically receives a modest discount on off-peak bookings only, while higher tiers receive discounts across both peak and off-peak slots, along with priority access to a limited allocation of peak slots reserved specifically for their tier during the daily release window. Guests accompanying members are charged according to the guest rate applicable at the time of booking, which is calculated separately from the member's own discount and cannot be combined with promotional codes unless explicitly stated in the promotion's terms.

7. Public Holiday and Special Event Pricing
On officially observed public holidays, and during club-hosted tournaments, exhibition matches, or other special events, standard peak and off-peak classifications may be suspended in favour of an event-specific rate published in advance through the app and branch noticeboards. Where a special event occupies a significant proportion of available courts at a branch, remaining courts not allocated to the event will typically be priced at standard peak rates regardless of the time of day, in recognition of the reduced overall availability. Members holding recurring bookings that fall on a date affected by a special event will be contacted directly regarding any changes to their usual slot and associated pricing, and will be offered a comparable alternative slot where their original booking cannot proceed.

8. Dynamic Pricing During Periods of Elevated Demand
During periods of unusually high demand, such as extended favourable weather at outdoor branches or a surge in interest following a promotional campaign, branches reserve the right to apply a temporary demand surcharge to a limited number of peak slots, capped at a percentage set centrally and never applied retroactively to bookings already confirmed. Any slot subject to a demand surcharge will display this clearly before payment is completed, and members will not be charged a surcharge they did not explicitly accept at the point of booking. Surcharges are reviewed on a rolling basis and removed once demand normalises, with no fixed minimum or maximum duration attached to their application.

9. Cancellation, Rescheduling, and Rate Reversion
Where a booking made at peak rates is cancelled within the permitted cancellation window and rebooked into an off-peak slot, the applicable off-peak rate will apply to the new booking, and any difference owed will be reflected in the member's account balance or refunded according to the standard refund method. Conversely, a member moving from an off-peak booking into a peak slot will be required to pay the difference before the new booking is confirmed. Cancellations made outside the permitted window remain subject to the standard cancellation fee as set out in the Court Booking and Cancellation Policy, and rate reversion does not apply retroactively to bookings that have already commenced.

10. Corporate, Group, and Academy Bookings
Corporate bookings, large group reservations, and structured academy sessions are priced separately from the standard individual rate card, reflecting the block nature of the booking and any coaching or facilitation costs involved. Corporate and group rates are negotiated directly with branch management or the central events team and are typically confirmed in writing ahead of the session, superseding any figure a member might calculate independently using the standard peak or off-peak rate card. Academy sessions for junior or adult development programmes carry their own fixed pricing structure that does not fluctuate with time of day, since these sessions are scheduled by the coaching team rather than selected freely by the participant.

11. Currency, Taxation, and Payment Processing
All prices displayed within the app and at branch reception are shown inclusive of any applicable taxation and in the standard local currency, with no separate service charge added at the point of court booking unless explicitly stated for a specific event or package. Payment is processed at the time of booking confirmation for most slot types, though certain membership tiers permit deferred settlement through a monthly account statement, subject to a satisfactory payment history. Any failed payment will result in the booking being held provisionally for a short period before automatic release back into general availability, allowing the member an opportunity to resolve the payment issue without immediately losing the slot.

12. Price Change Notification
Where the central pricing team implements a structural change to peak or off-peak definitions, or a material adjustment to the underlying rate card, affected members will be notified through the app's messaging centre and, where the change materially affects an existing recurring booking, by direct message ahead of the change taking effect. Members are not entitled to retain a previous rate indefinitely once a change has been properly notified, save for any transitional grace period explicitly stated in the notification itself. Promotional or introductory rates are time-limited by nature and revert to the standard applicable rate automatically once their stated validity period lapses.

13. Disputes and Escalation Path
Any member who believes they have been charged incorrectly under this policy should first raise the matter with branch reception, who are equipped to review the booking record and rate card applied at the time of the transaction. Where the matter cannot be resolved at branch level, or where the member disputes the classification of a slot as peak rather than off-peak, the query should be escalated to the central member services team, who will review the booking against the published schedule in effect at the time and respond within a reasonable working period. Any resulting adjustment, whether a refund, credit, or correction to future pricing, will be processed through the standard account adjustment procedure rather than as a cash refund, except where cash or card refund is the only practicable remedy.

14. Policy Review and Final Provisions
This pricing structure is reviewed periodically by the central operations team to ensure it remains reflective of genuine demand patterns, operating costs, and member expectations across all branches. Nothing in this policy overrides the specific terms of an individual membership contract or a written corporate agreement, and where a conflict arises between this general policy and a specific written agreement, the specific agreement will prevail. Baseline Padel reserves the right to introduce new pricing tiers, slot classifications, or branch-specific variations as the business evolves, with any such changes communicated in line with the notification provisions set out above.

title: Corporate Accounts and Invoicing
body:
1. Eligibility and Account Setup
Corporate accounts are available to registered businesses, government entities, and organised sports bodies that wish to book court time, coaching packages, or membership allocations on behalf of employees, clients, or members. To open a corporate account, an authorised representative must submit a completed application through the club administration office at any branch, along with a valid trade licence or equivalent registration document. Applications are reviewed within five working days, and Baseline Padel reserves the right to decline any application without providing a detailed reason, though in most cases this relates to incomplete documentation or an inability to verify the requesting entity. Once approved, the corporate account holder will be assigned a dedicated account number that applies across all branches, allowing consolidated tracking of bookings and spend regardless of which location is used.

2. Credit Terms and Invoicing Cycles
Approved corporate accounts are typically issued invoices on a monthly cycle, covering all court hire, coaching fees, equipment rental, and food and beverage charges accrued under the account number during that period. Standard payment terms are thirty days from the invoice date unless an alternative arrangement has been agreed in writing at account opening. Invoices are dispatched electronically to the nominated finance contact and, where requested, a secondary contact within the organisation. It remains the responsibility of the corporate account holder to ensure that contact details are kept current; Baseline Padel will not waive late charges on the basis that an invoice was sent to an outdated email address that the account holder failed to update.

3. Credit Limits and Review
Every corporate account is assigned a credit limit at the point of approval, based on anticipated usage and the supporting documentation provided. Should projected activity exceed this limit, the account holder must request a review before further bookings are accepted on credit terms; bookings that would breach the limit without prior approval may be held pending settlement of outstanding balances. Credit limits are reviewed periodically, generally every six months, and may be increased or decreased depending on payment history, usage patterns, and the standing of the account. A consistent pattern of late payment may result in a reduced limit or a shift to pro forma invoicing, where payment is required in advance of any booking being confirmed.

4. Authorised Users and Booking Access
Corporate accounts must nominate a primary administrator who holds authority to add or remove authorised users permitted to make bookings against the account. Authorised users may book courts, reserve coaching sessions, and order refreshments at any branch by quoting the account number and their individual authorisation code. Baseline Padel does not verify the internal approval processes of the corporate entity and will honour any booking made using a valid authorisation code; disputes arising from bookings made by employees or members who were not properly authorised internally are a matter for the corporate account holder to resolve, not the club. Where a corporate account holder wishes to restrict spending by department, team, or individual, this can be arranged through the account administration team, though such restrictions must be configured at least three working days before they are intended to take effect.

5. Late Payment and Overdue Balances
Invoices not settled within the agreed payment term are considered overdue and may attract a late payment charge calculated as a percentage of the outstanding balance, applied at intervals for as long as the amount remains unpaid. Accounts with overdue balances exceeding sixty days from the original invoice date will typically have booking privileges suspended across all branches until payment is received or a revised payment plan is agreed with the finance office. Suspension does not cancel any pre-existing bookings already confirmed, though the club reserves the right to cancel these as well in cases of significant or repeated non-payment. Corporate account holders experiencing genuine cash flow difficulty are encouraged to contact the finance office proactively, as payment plans are considerably easier to arrange before an account falls into arrears than after.

6. Disputed Charges
Any charge that a corporate account holder believes to be incorrect must be disputed in writing within fourteen days of the invoice date, referencing the specific booking, date, and branch in question. Disputes raised after this window may still be reviewed at the discretion of the finance office, but there is no guarantee of adjustment once an invoice has been fully processed and, in some cases, already reconciled against tax filings. While a dispute is under review, the account holder is expected to settle the undisputed portion of the invoice in full and on time; only the specific line items in question may be withheld pending resolution. Repeated disputes over similar charges may prompt a review of the account's booking permissions to identify whether the underlying issue is a misunderstanding of pricing tiers rather than a genuine billing error.

7. Cancellations and No-Show Charges on Corporate Bookings
Court and coaching bookings made under a corporate account are subject to the same cancellation windows that apply to individual bookings, generally requiring cancellation at least twelve hours in advance to avoid a charge, though outdoor branches may apply slightly longer notice periods during the cooler months when demand for evening slots is highest. No-show charges and late cancellation fees are billed to the corporate account in the same invoicing cycle as the original booking and are not separately negotiable after the fact, since these charges reflect court time that could otherwise have been allocated to another user. Corporate account holders running large events or block bookings involving multiple courts should note that cancellation of part of a block, rather than the whole, may still incur charges on the unused portion depending on how much notice is given relative to the original reservation.

8. Multi-Branch Usage and Consolidated Reporting
One of the principal advantages of a corporate account is the ability to use any of the eight branches interchangeably while all activity is consolidated onto a single monthly invoice. Corporate account holders may request a branch-by-branch breakdown alongside the consolidated invoice at no additional cost, which is particularly useful for organisations wishing to allocate costs internally by office location or department. Indoor and outdoor branches are billed at their respective rate cards, so a consolidated invoice may show variation in per-hour pricing across line items; this reflects differing facility types rather than any inconsistency in billing and should not be treated as an error unless the rate applied does not match the published rate card for that specific branch and time slot.

9. Currency, Taxation, and Statutory Charges
All corporate invoices are issued in the local currency and include any applicable statutory taxes at the rate in force at the time of the transaction. Should tax rates change during a billing cycle, invoices will reflect the rate applicable on the date each individual charge was incurred rather than a blanket rate for the whole invoice, which may result in a single invoice showing two different tax calculations across its line items. Corporate account holders requiring a formal tax invoice for their own compliance purposes should indicate this at account opening, as certain formatting and detail requirements can be built into the standard invoice template from the outset rather than requested retrospectively.

10. Amendments to Corporate Account Details
Changes to company name, billing address, nominated contacts, or banking details used for payment must be submitted in writing and supported by appropriate documentation, such as an updated trade licence in the case of a company name change. Baseline Padel will not action verbal requests to alter payment or contact details, regardless of how the request is communicated, as a safeguard against unauthorised account changes. Processing of amendments typically takes up to five working days, during which time the account will continue to operate under its existing details to avoid disruption to ongoing bookings.

11. Termination of Corporate Accounts
Either party may terminate a corporate account agreement by providing thirty days' written notice to the other. Upon termination, any outstanding balance becomes immediately due in full, and a final invoice covering activity up to the closure date will be issued within the standard monthly cycle rather than immediately upon notice being given. Corporate account holders wishing to reopen an account previously closed due to non-payment will be required to settle any historical balance in full and may be asked to provide a deposit or accept pro forma invoicing for an initial period before standard credit terms are reinstated.

12. Escalation Path for Unresolved Issues
Where a corporate account holder is unable to resolve a billing or service issue through the branch administration office, the matter should be escalated in writing to the central finance office, which oversees corporate accounts across all branches. Escalations should include the account number, a summary of the issue, and any relevant invoice or booking references to avoid delays caused by incomplete information. Matters not resolved at this level within a reasonable period may be raised with the club's commercial operations team, who hold final authority over corporate account decisions including credit terms, fee waivers, and account reinstatement following suspension.

13. Force Majeure and Facility Closures
In circumstances where a branch is closed temporarily due to weather, maintenance, or other events beyond the club's reasonable control, any corporate bookings affected will be rescheduled where possible or credited against the next invoice rather than refunded directly, unless the account holder specifically requests a refund in writing. Outdoor branches are inherently more susceptible to weather-related closures, and corporate account holders operating primarily through outdoor branches should factor this into their planning, particularly for time-sensitive events such as tournaments or client entertainment bookings where rescheduling options may be limited.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
This policy is subject to periodic review and may be amended at the discretion of Baseline Padel to reflect operational or regulatory changes. Material changes affecting existing corporate account holders will be communicated in writing with reasonable notice before taking effect, and continued use of a corporate account following such notice constitutes acceptance of the revised terms. Corporate account holders are encouraged to request the current version of this policy periodically, as historical printed or emailed copies may not reflect subsequent amendments.

title: Promotions, Vouchers and Discount Codes
body:
1. Scope and Application
This policy governs all promotional offers, vouchers, gift cards and discount codes issued or accepted by Baseline Padel across all eight branches, whether those branches operate indoor courts, outdoor courts, or a mixture of both. It applies equally to offers redeemed in person at reception, through the Baseline Padel booking app, or via any third-party platform with which Baseline Padel has a current commercial arrangement. Where a specific promotion carries its own bespoke terms distributed at the time of launch, those bespoke terms take precedence over this general policy only where they are more restrictive; in all other respects this document remains the governing framework. Members and guests are deemed to have accepted this policy the moment a discount code or voucher is applied to a booking, regardless of whether they have read it in full.

2. Eligibility for Promotional Offers
Promotional pricing is generally reserved for new bookings made after the offer's publication and cannot ordinarily be applied retroactively to a reservation already confirmed and paid for. Unless a promotion explicitly states otherwise, offers are limited to one redemption per person per promotional period, and Baseline Padel reserves the right to verify eligibility using the name, mobile number and membership identifier associated with an account. Corporate, academy and junior programme members may be excluded from consumer-facing promotions where those members already benefit from a separate discounted rate structure, and staff members and their immediate household are not eligible for public promotional codes under any circumstances. Any attempt to circumvent eligibility rules, including the creation of duplicate accounts, will result in the offer being void and may trigger the sanctions described in clause 11.

3. Voucher Issuance and Format
Vouchers issued by Baseline Padel may take the form of a printed certificate, a digital code delivered by email or SMS, or a credit balance visible within a member's app wallet. Every voucher carries a unique reference number, and this reference number must be quoted or scanned at the time of redemption; Baseline Padel cannot honour a voucher for which the customer is unable to produce this reference, even where proof of purchase exists in another form. Vouchers purchased as gifts are transferable to any third party unless the voucher was itself issued as part of a non-transferable promotional campaign, in which case this restriction will be stated clearly on the voucher itself. Lost or deleted digital vouchers can usually be reissued by reception staff after identity verification, though a short administrative delay of up to two business days should be expected while the original code is traced and cancelled.

4. Validity Periods and Expiry
All vouchers and discount codes carry a defined validity window, typically expressed as a number of days from the date of issue rather than a fixed calendar date, and this window is printed on the voucher or stated in the confirmation message accompanying a digital code. Once a voucher has expired it cannot be redeemed, extended or converted to account credit except at the discretion of branch management, which may consider extension requests where the delay in use was caused by a documented service disruption on Baseline Padel's part, such as prolonged court closure at the customer's home branch. Seasonal promotions tied to particular weather-dependent periods, such as offers aimed at encouraging use of outdoor branches during the cooler months, will typically carry shorter validity windows than standard gift vouchers, and customers should check the specific expiry terms before purchase rather than assuming a standard twelve-month window applies.

5. Redemption Process at Booking
Discount codes must be entered at the checkout stage of the booking process, either within the app or by the reception team if the booking is made over the counter or by phone. Codes cannot be applied after a booking has been confirmed and paid for in full, since the underlying payment processing does not support retroactive discounting once a transaction has settled. Where a customer forgets to apply an eligible code, Baseline Padel may, purely as a gesture of goodwill and not as an obligation, offer an equivalent credit toward a future booking, but this is assessed case by case and is not guaranteed. Only one discount code may be applied per booking unless a promotion is explicitly marked as stackable, and Baseline Padel's booking system is configured to reject a second code automatically in most cases, so customers should not assume that a system error allowing two codes to be applied simultaneously reflects an intentional policy.

6. Minimum Spend and Exclusions
Many promotional codes carry a minimum spend threshold or are restricted to particular products, such as court hire only, coaching packages only, or retail purchases only, and these restrictions will be stated within the offer's specific terms at the time of publication. Court hire discounts do not generally extend to ancillary charges such as equipment hire, coaching add-ons booked separately, or food and beverage purchases at branches with on-site cafés, unless the promotion specifically states that it covers the full transaction. Peak-hour bookings, tournament entry fees and private event hire are typically excluded from general promotional codes given the different pricing structure applied to these categories, and any code that appears to apply successfully to an excluded category in error will be corrected by Baseline Padel prior to the booking being finalised, with the customer notified of the adjusted price before payment is taken.

7. Combining Offers with Membership Discounts
Customers holding an active Baseline Padel membership already benefit from preferential court rates, and in most cases promotional discount codes cannot be combined with a membership rate, since doing so would apply two discounts to a single transaction. Where a promotional campaign is designed specifically for members, this will be stated clearly, and the system will apply whichever discount delivers the greater saving to the customer rather than stacking both. Guests booked under a member's account are subject to the same combination restrictions as the member themselves, and any attempt to apply a public promotional code to a guest booking that has already received a member referral discount will result in the system prompting the customer to choose one benefit only.

8. Refunds and Cancellations Involving Promotional Bookings
Where a booking made using a voucher or discount code is subsequently cancelled in line with the standard cancellation policy, any refund due will reflect the amount actually paid by the customer rather than the full undiscounted price of the session. If the voucher itself was a single-use code, it will typically be treated as consumed and will not be automatically reinstated, although customers experiencing a service failure on Baseline Padel's part, such as a court being unplayable due to unresolved maintenance, may request reinstatement of the voucher through reception. Gift vouchers redeemed partially against a booking that is later cancelled will usually have the relevant value returned to the voucher balance rather than issued as a cash refund, since gift vouchers are not refundable to a payment card except where required by law.

9. Fraudulent or Invalid Codes
Baseline Padel monitors discount code usage across all branches for unusual patterns, including codes shared publicly beyond their intended audience, codes generated through unauthorised means, or repeated redemption attempts from a single account using multiple similar codes. Any booking found to have used a fraudulent, expired, or unauthorised code will be flagged, and Baseline Padel reserves the right to cancel the booking, charge the customer the full undiscounted rate, or suspend the account pending investigation. Customers who receive a code through informal channels, such as social media reposts or messaging groups, are responsible for confirming its legitimacy before use, and Baseline Padel accepts no liability for a booking disrupted as a result of a customer relying on a code that later proves invalid.

10. Partner and Third-Party Promotions
From time to time Baseline Padel participates in joint promotions with external partners, including corporate wellness schemes, hospitality partners, or payment providers offering cashback or bonus codes. Redemption of these third-party codes is subject both to this policy and to any additional terms set by the partner organisation, and Baseline Padel is not responsible for resolving disputes that arise from the partner's own systems, such as delayed cashback processing. Where a partner promotion is withdrawn or amended by the partner with limited notice, Baseline Padel will honour codes already issued up to their stated expiry wherever technically possible, but cannot guarantee continuity of an offer that depends on a third party's ongoing participation.

11. Misuse and Sanctions
Deliberate misuse of promotional offers, including but not limited to the creation of duplicate accounts to claim a new-customer discount multiple times, the resale of non-transferable vouchers, or the manipulation of referral schemes through fabricated bookings, is treated as a breach of the customer agreement. Baseline Padel may respond to confirmed misuse by voiding the discount applied, requiring payment of the outstanding balance, suspending access to online booking privileges, or, in serious or repeated cases, terminating the customer's membership entirely. Any such decision will be communicated in writing, and the customer will be given an opportunity to explain the circumstances before a final sanction is applied, except in cases of clear and repeated fraud where immediate suspension is necessary to protect the wider membership base.

12. Technical Errors and System Glitches
On rare occasions a technical fault within the booking platform may allow a discount code to be applied incorrectly, whether by granting an unintended discount percentage, permitting use beyond the stated expiry, or allowing a code to be combined with another offer against the system's normal rules. Where such an error is identified, Baseline Padel reserves the right to correct the price charged, cancel the affected booking with a full refund of the amount actually paid, or contact the customer directly to arrange an alternative resolution. Customers are asked to report any pricing discrepancy they notice at the time of booking rather than proceeding on the assumption that an unusually favourable price is intentional, as this allows the matter to be resolved swiftly and avoids any later inconvenience of a booking being adjusted or cancelled.

13. Escalation and Complaints
Customers who believe a voucher or discount code has been wrongly declined, incorrectly applied, or unfairly withdrawn should first raise the matter with reception staff at their home branch, who are authorised to resolve straightforward cases on the spot. Where a resolution cannot be reached locally, the matter should be escalated in writing to the central customer service team, who will typically respond within a reasonable number of business days and may request supporting documentation such as booking confirmations or screenshots of the original offer. Baseline Padel aims to resolve all promotional disputes fairly and consistently across all branches, and decisions made at one branch will generally be treated as precedent for materially identical cases raised elsewhere within the group.

14. Policy Review and Amendments
Baseline Padel reserves the right to amend this policy at any time to reflect changes in commercial strategy, payment processing capability, or regulatory requirement, and the most current version will always be made available through the app and at reception across all branches. Amendments will not affect the terms of a voucher or discount code already issued and validly held by a customer at the time of the change, save where the amendment is required to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation. Customers are encouraged to review the current version of this policy periodically, particularly before making a significant purchase such as a bulk gift voucher order, to ensure they are relying on the most up-to-date terms.
